💡 Key Takeaways
  • It took Battlefield Studios over four months to tell Battlefield 6 players what they can actually expect from the game over the course of this year, in terms of content - but we’re glad to see a initiative laid out nonetheless.
  • The developer unveiled a grand 2026 roadmap, covering three more seasons presently in the works, and a wealth of newly introduced additions across the entire game, including new maps and the introduction of a new theatre of combat.
  • In a wide-ranging latest video dubbed The Year Ahead, members of the Battlefield 6 development team have revealed a lot of new information about the future of the multiplayer shooter, going over plenty of the features and new content coming over the course of this year.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It took Battlefield Studios over four months to tell Battlefield 6 players what they can actually expect from the game over the course of this year, in terms of content - but we’re glad to see a initiative laid out nonetheless.

The developer unveiled a grand 2026 roadmap, covering three more seasons presently in the works, and a wealth of newly introduced additions across the entire game, including new maps and the introduction of a new theatre of combat.

In a wide-ranging latest video dubbed The Year Ahead, members of the Battlefield 6 development team have revealed a lot of new information about the future of the multiplayer shooter, going over plenty of the features and new content coming over the course of this year.

Recent findings suggest that the video confirmed that BF6 has at least three other seasons in the works. Season 3, which begins in May, will be followed by Season 4, and Season 5 later in the year. Season 5 is the most mysterious, which is understandable.

In a recent development, we’ve known about some of what’s coming in Season 3, such as the remake of Golmud Railway (now called Railway to Golmud), but the video also revealed that a remake of Battlefield 3’s Grand Bazaar - now Cairo Bazaar - will also arrive later in the same season. Other exciting additions, such as battle royale solos and ranked play for Redsec are also on the agenda for Season 3.

Recent findings suggest that season 4, set for July, looks to be the biggest so far, with the introduction of naval combat, which will be available across two maps. Tsuru Reef, which is stated to be even larger than Golmud, the largest map in BF6. The Pacific-set map won’t be the only one, as later in the season, another remake will arrive, this time of the iconic Wake Island.

Industry observers note that the introduction of naval combat will bring with it a fresh dynamic wave system, aircraft carriers with operational flight decks, and new naval vehicles. Custom lobbies and Spectator Mode are also planned for Season 4.

Season 5 will bring three maps to BF6, rather than two, but all of its content remains under wraps.

According to recent reports, perhaps a sour note is that almost all of the maps referenced and shown in the video are remakes of maps from other Battlefield games, or reimagined at the very least. The Battlefield series is no stranger to remaking its own maps, but Battlefield 6 appears to be leaning on it much more than past entries.

If it’s any consolation, however, the map remakes we’ve played so far in Battlefield 6 have gone through major changes that have contributed to giving them a different flow and feel from their classic versions, or even remakes in other BF games.

Over the course of 2026, you can also expect the return of persistent servers, as well as a server browser to find them all - just like the good ol’ days. This includes the ability to host your own, though it’s unclear quite how this is going to work.

Season 3 is set to revealed in the coming days, so you’ll be hearing back from BF Studios in the near future.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that diablo 4 is gearing up for its biggest post-launch event yet: the upcoming release of the Lord of Hatred expansion. As was the case with Vessel of Hatred before it, expansion releases alter the seasonal flow in a few ways, and Blizzard has now explained how.

The game’s next season - its 13th - has been officially revealed as Season of Reckoning. The new season will kick off alongside the expansion’s release next week, and will be available to all players, just like all previous seasons.

Although Season of Reckoning will roll out as normal, the season itself won’t be as meaty, at least when it comes to the sort of gameplay mechanics and themes players have come to expect from each new season.

You’ll still find the normal Season Rank chase, Smoldering Ashes, and various rewards at each chapter. Season Blessings will also return, but that’s about it for progression outside of the game itself. If it’s any consolation, there are more goals and objectives to tackle this season.

Sources indicate that the even better news is that, according to Blizzard, future seasons will follow the classic format, which makes sense. The new season will come with a battle pass, of course, featuring four Reliquaries, as usual. The first Reliquary is free, while the others are paid.

In a recent development, blizzard has also confirmed the the pre-load for Lord of Hatred is available now on all platforms. Even if you’re not getting the expansion, patch 3.0.0's pre-load includes all expansion content regardless, so you may as well pre-download it to be ready for April 27/28. On launch day, you’ll also need to download a smaller patch, version 3.0.1.

It has been revealed that in case you missed it, we published our Lord of Hatred review earlier in the week. Give it a read if you’re curious about the expansion’s impact on the narrative, and how it changes core Diablo 4 gameplay.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Declaring a Best Way of Doing Things is a fool’s game, though in recent years my favourite entries in the Tricky Hitting genre – inclusive of soulslikes and their hybridised disciples – have been the substantial, bulging ones.
  • Recent findings suggest that even in the latter stages, with a full kit of precisely four ranged spells, Death’s Door is a simple proposition.
  • According to recent reports, still, it’s clever with its limitations.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Declaring a Best Way of Doing Things is a fool’s game, though in recent years my favourite entries in the Tricky Hitting genre – inclusive of soulslikes and their hybridised disciples – have been the substantial, bulging ones. Elden Rings and Silksongs, with vast kingdoms and deep, rattling toolkits for surviving them. The reason it’s a fool’s game is because you can also have something like Death’s Door, a taut, compact, lighthearted little actioner that fills eight hours instead of 80 and yet never feels underwhelming or compromised for it.

Recent findings suggest that even in the latter stages, with a full kit of precisely four ranged spells, Death’s Door is a simple proposition. You are a crow. You hit things. Occasionally you shoot things. You collect the souls of a frog, a yeti, and a grandmother. Everything in-between directly relates to finding the errant monster/pensioner, or at a stretch, upgrading one of those four abilities.

According to recent reports, still, it’s clever with its limitations. Environments are small in number but vary wildly in tone and texture, and they tightly weave their paths into criss-crossing bundles that maximise travel – evoking the sense of a great, ranging adventure within relatively tiny spaces. The lack of a wiki’s worth of combat options also never becomes a problem, partly because it spreads out its spell unlocks, and partly because the smooth, flowing back-and-forths of its central swordplay are pleasurable enough to carry it anyway. Good bosses, too! They’re all characterful, memorable weirdoes who fight unlike anyone in their minion armies, and usually come with a hidden weakness to deduce and exploit.

Which is welcome, as these big lads and lasses do tend to launch difficulty spikes right up your feathered backside, and do so in a game that isn’t otherwise as fussed about trial-and-error pain endurance as some of its inspirations. They don’t, however, bring the mood down. At times, this tale of a pitch-black soul reaper working as an agent of Death (complete with an office of Death and embittered co-workers of Death) can get downright cosy, leading through you through warmly-lit jungles and breezy waterside ruins.

In a recent development, recently replaying, I’d also forgotten how witty it can be. Little gaglets are sprinkled throughout, both visual and verbal, but the best jokes are saved for – funnily enough – the bosses, who’ll raise your pre-fight spirit with some amusingly terrible trash talk before becoming the punchline themselves. I audibly wheezed the first time a death animation immediately cut to the foe’s impromptu funeral, their beaked killer among the precious few guests. And even when the joke is recycled later, I couldn’t help tittering at the sight of my enemy – who seconds earlier, had been attempting to fatally sit on me – lying nobly in state.

Sources indicate that I previously considered ending my Valor Mortis review by calling it a gateway into the more demanding side of action-RPGs; a shorter, simpler alternative to FromSoft’s overwhelming titans that might nonetheless serve to introduce curious newcomers to their shared quirks and qualities. The game equivalent of splashing your chest with water before jumping into a pool. In hindsight, Death’s Door was always a better fit for that description, though there’s enough else here you don’t need to be prepping for something tougher to appreciate its lean, keen adventuring.

Tech Report: Paradox boss Frederik Wester stepping down after several tumultuous years for the Cities Skylines and Stellaris publisher

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that paradox Interactive's Frederik Wester has declared he's stepping down from the role of CEO after a combined decade and a half leading the company.
  • In a statement announcing the change in leadership, Paradox remarked Wester had "decided to step down as CEO to continue focusing on the firm's long-term development as a member of the Board." Paradox's current deputy CEO, Mattias Lilja, will take over Wester's role from 4th January 2027.
  • "I'm truly grateful to all our engaged players and talented colleagues who contribute to outstanding gaming experiences every day," Wester said of his decision.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that paradox Interactive's Frederik Wester has declared he's stepping down from the role of CEO after a combined decade and a half leading the company. The news follows several tumultuous years for the publisher best known for grand strategy games including Stellaris, Europa Universalis, and Crusader Kings 3.

In a statement announcing the change in leadership, Paradox remarked Wester had "decided to step down as CEO to continue focusing on the firm's long-term development as a member of the Board." Paradox's current deputy CEO, Mattias Lilja, will take over Wester's role from 4th January 2027. Wester is to remain in the position until then in order "to ensure an orderly transition".

"I'm truly grateful to all our engaged players and talented colleagues who contribute to outstanding gaming experiences every day," Wester said of his decision. "They are the ones who made these years amazing. My blueprint was never to be CEO for life. The goal was to build the foundation before passing the baton on for the next chapter in the organization's journey. Since I returned as CEO, we've streamlined our strategy, rebuilt our pipeline and developed our commercial offering. Mattias has had a central role in laying this foundation, and now is the right time to hand over. Given his experience and vision, he is exceptionally well positioned to take the company to its next level.".

Wester has twice served as Paradox CEO since joining the company in 2003. His first stint ran from 2009 to 2018, after which he became Paradox's executive chairman of the board. He returned to the CEO role in 2021, and has overseen a troubled period for the company. This has included the embattled development of Vampire: The Masquerade Bloodlines 2 - which finally debuted last October after multiple delays, near cancellation, and a switch in developer. Unfortunately the game failed to resonate with critics and audiences, and Paradox announced a 162 percent decline in operating profit earlier this year as a result of its commercial failure.

Wester's most recent watch - which began with an admittance of "inappropriate behaviour" amid a damning report into Paradox's workplace culture - has also seen the high-profile cancellation of Sims competitor Life By You, an indefinite delay for Prison Architect 2 after Paradox parted ways with original developer Double Eleven, and a split with BattleTech studio Harebrained Schemes following the commercial failure of The Lamplighters League. Paradox's Cities Skylines 2 has also been blighted with controversy: after a disastrous launch in 2023, its console release is still yet to emerge, and development is now being handled by a upcoming studio after Paradox split with former developer Colossal Order last year. In 2004, Wester admitted the publisher had "made the wrong calls in several projects".

Despite all this, incoming CEO Mattias Lilja remains buoyant. "Paradox has a unique DNA that has made us one of the greats in deep and engaging strategy and management games," he wrote in a statement announcing his promotion. "Now we’re stepping up the pace: we will make further investments in our core business, push the boundaries of our game design, work even more closely with our loyal players, develop more and better tools and services that benefit both modders and players, and continue to sharpen our ways of working and our organisation, with player value in focus.".

In a recent development, paradox, does of course, have some promising games on its upcoming slate. Alongside continued work on grand strategy stalwarts like Crusader Kings 3, Europa Universalis 5, and Stellaris, next year sees the release of Lego Skylines, and post-apocalyptic grand strategy game Afterworld is also on the way.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

HoYoverse just wrapped up a pretty exciting Zenless Zone Zero Special Program that not only delivered all the details on the next significant upgrade, it also came with the unexpected announcement that the action RPG is on its way to Steam.

Previously, all HoYoverse games with PC versions have always been directly available from the developer’s website, or through the Epic Games Store. In other words, Zenless Zone Zero will soon mark the massive firm’s debut on Valve’s platform.

Sources indicate that the main focus of the livestream, of course, has been Version 2.8, otherwise known as New Eridan Sunset. This upcoming release is scheduled for May 6, though the Steam version does not yet have a date.The new release sees the release of two new Agents, as well as the brand-new Wind attribute enemy.

The release also acts as the last chapter of Season 2, and it sees Ramiel becoming the main target of different factions in the Outer Ring. The two new arrivals, together with Proxies and Cissia will embark on a quest to learn the new identity of Ramiel.

The first new Agent is Promeia, the executioner of Krampus. She’s an S-Rank Ice Anomaly Agent who can consume Trial by Cold to trigger Abloom on enemies. This is done by converting Corrosive Chill.

By using her EX Special Attack, she can enter the Bound Absolution state, which allows her to automatically Perfect Dodge any attack that targets her. If you have another Anomaly or Support Agent on the team, Promeia can further boost the entire squad’s Abloom damage.

Industry observers note that the second addition in 2.8 is Starlight - Billy, also an S-Rank Agent, though wielding Physical Rupture instead. This is the upgraded form of Billy, and he arrives on a combat motorcycle to bring his signature Starlight Knight to the fight. Through it, he can deliver big Physical burst damage.

Recent findings suggest that the higher Billy’s health, the more Sheer damage he deals. In fact, all Physical damage he deals lands as Sheer damage. Further building on his tank-like role, his skills can also restore his own health.

Re-runs in Version 2.8 will be Lucia in the first half, and Orphie & Magus in the second. The other exciting addition coming with this revision is the new Wind attribute enemy, and the accompanying Vortex mechanic.

According to recent reports, when an enemy is inflicted with the Wind Attribute Anomaly, any other Anomaly attack type that gets applied will trigger Vortex, rather than Disorder. This deals AoE Anomaly damage of the type that matches the corresponding element.

It has been revealed that throughout the version’s runtime, you’ll be able to take part in the Marcel Bootopia-themed event, which gives you control of Eous and lets you explore a Bangboo resort island. The island has been closed due to an outbreak of Hollows, and you must rescue Bangboos and find treasures.

If you do, you’ll earn Booltergeist and its Bangboo core for your troubles. This is an A-Rank Bangboo that can float around and fire lasers in combat. Its damage is further boosted whenever certain teammates are present.

The Ultimate Verdict Trial is another event you can check out that lets you fight alongside newcomer Promeia, or take part in other mini-activities that all reward Polychrome. Finally, you can look forward to a newly introduced Hoshimi Miyabi outfit: Dignified Blossom, which will be available in the store.

Before you jump back in next month, it always helps to catch up on the latest Zenless Zone Zero codes to make sure you’re not missing out on any freebies.

We got confirmation a couple of months ago that the US Army's 3rd Infantry Division was offering a four-day pass to play Grand Theft Auto 6 for soldiers who re-enlist for at least two years. And now the time has come to collect.

In a recent development, talking to Task & Purpose one soldier who took advantage of the program, Sgt. Jamire Smith, described how he's planning to spend the long weekend: "I'm all campaign. I’m all about the heist. I think I have a good 24 hours to waste on it.

"I was actually in the process of getting out, I was towards my final stages of getting out … but my manufacturer and the battalion helped me navigate through that and they revealed me that there’s still a need for me, and that I am still a clear and value asset to the team, and so that’s really what drove me to say 'let’s keep going, let’s keep driving'. Maybe be a lifer in this, since I already made it my career.".

Industry observers note that in total 43 soldiers re-enlisted through the GTA 6 incentive, an idea that was born from Staff Sgt. Brittany Wolfer.

"It's not supposed to be the deciding factor," Wolfer says. "There is always going to be a disconnect between your senior command and your lowest soldier. So how do you bridge that gap to where that lower soldier still knows that their battalion commander or their senior leadership cares about them and sees what they're interested in. And that’s kind of what this was for.".

Recent findings suggest that wolfer first brought the idea to her battalion commander who actually played GTA 2 back in the day and so was up for trying the incentive out. "I came into [the unit], there hadn’t been a counsellor for about eight months, so there was a lot of gaps and things that were falling through because the soldiers didn’t have that presence within the formation," Wolfer adds. "This kind of was just a way to grab people's attention and kind of be like, 'Hey, here I am. I’m the person you’re gonna come talk to,' and [it] kind of snowballed from there.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that faster-moving, sometimes maddening, and obsession-forming. Football Manager finds a way to make spreadsheets fun again.

According to recent reports, PC Gamer's got your back Our experienced team dedicates many hours to every review, to really get to the heart of what matters most to you. Find out more about how we evaluate games and hardware.

What is it? The latest in a long line of life-absorbing sports management sims.Release date November 10, 2026Expect to pay $60/£50Developer Sports InteractivePublisher SegaReviewed on Ryzen 7 9800X3D, Radeon RX 9070XT, 16GB RAMSteam Deck TBALink Official site.

It's difficult to convey to non-players how deeply Football Manager gets under your skin. It's the kind of game that becomes your mental screensaver, the fallback topic whenever your brain isn't explicitly required to think about something else. A Slack DM came in this morning and for a second I interpreted 'DM – [Name]' as Slack assigning my colleague the defensive midfielder position. When did they add that feature? I caught myself thinking for a second.

In a recent development, that in itself doesn't mean Football Manager 27 is a great game. This series is capable of fostering fixation even on its off games, like last year's tile-ridden UI tangle FM26. But this new release makes meaningful progress by untangling that UI, improving the flow of the game between matches, and—the holy grail—giving you some clue as to why you're losing, and what you can do about it.

The latter point comes thanks to the introduction of the 'tactical effectiveness' system. This is a visual rating of all the factors that affect your team's performance, and it lives in your tactics screen as a colour-coded scale. The better all those underlying factors are working, the higher your tactical effectiveness scale goes. Click on it and you see under the hood of FM's simulation, at all the elements which determine your squad's performance, from individual player ability and training effectiveness to each player's degree of buy-in to your tactical vision.

That screen gives a degree of transparency to what's deciding whether you win or lose, and having played these games since Championship Manager 2, I've been wishing for that transparency for a long time.

But it's not without its problems. This being the introduction of this fresh system, its effects feel overly exaggerated. If your team has a low tactical effectiveness they'll lollop about on the pitch like it's their first day on Earth, even in the most basic formations that my school's under 11s side could execute. It's extremely frustrating to watch the sport's absolute elite wandering about in the final third like they've forgotten where the goal is, or witness Champions League-calibre centre backs totally baffled by their markers running in a straight line towards goal. This is probably how it feels to be a Man United manager in real life, but it still feels like a failing of the match engine to visualise poor tactical effectiveness in a true-to-life way.

The flipside of that coin is that there's a lot of gratification to be had in increasing that TE scale, and FM 27 does a good job of surfacing the ways to do it. It means setting more tactical familiarity sessions in the training screen, a doorway I haven't personally darkened for years as a manager since it allowed me to delegate that task to my assistant. It also finds its way into recruitment, showing you a rough prediction of how well a player will contribute to that all-key rating even before you sign them. I really enjoy this new way of thinking about signings, and relish the chance to be proactive about improving performances instead of changing things at random and crossing my fingers.

Industry observers note that on the pitch, there's some modest progress since last year. Fresh animations, specifically flair passes and players recovering from a stumble after being shoulder-barged, tell you something useful about that player's attributes and how they can be used. Meanwhile on the presentation front, there are a few new angles during pre-match sequences and trophy ceremonies.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

Industry observers note that there's also a lot of the usual release-era nonsense. In my save I seem to have a goal waved off for offside every twenty minutes, and keepers seem to have started coating their boots and gloves in teflon when receiving the most straightforward backpasses or clearing up routine balls. These odd glitches happen every year before the first few patches roll out, and revision 27.1.0 does seem to address most of the odd match engine behaviour I've noticed.

But I'm disappointed that progress is that gradual. Particularly as FM's move to the Unity engine was so disruptive, prompting the series to skip a year. I expected that engine switch might mean the match engine evolves more swiftly, but that doesn't seem to be the case based on this release.

In a recent development, instead, the really significant additions and improvements can be found in the nooks and crannies, the boring bits you wouldn't write about in the Steam description. How do you make navigable menus, more game setup customization options and quicker progress between matches sound sexy? Nevertheless, these are the changes that add up and make FM 27 feel much more enjoyable than last year's game.

The prime example of these small but mighty changes is the 'continue flow'. When you start a fresh game, you can now control how often the game stops the passage of time to return you to your inbox after you hit 'continue'. Hardly the most exciting feature on paper, but it addresses a crucial and longstanding problem: progress had become punitively slow. More than any loss at home to a relegation side or any unreasonable telling-off from the board, it was this feeling of wading nose-deep through molasses that sapped my desire to keep playing recent FM games, and it turns out that fixing the problem is as simple as selecting the 'streamlined' continue flow so that the game stops progressing time less often and moves you from match to match at a faster rate.

This is a game about setting long-term intends and watching them come to fruition. Winning one match isn't where the payoff comes, it's three seasons in when you see how much your youth academy graduate's stats have developed. So it really does matter that FM 27 hastens the pace and you can see those long term plans resolve.

There's been something of a deft Cruyff turn from Sports Interactive on the direction of its UI this year, after the overhaul in FM 26 was received as positively as a taxation on laughter. The menu tiles have been pared right back, menus themselves are much faster to load and in general it's more intuitive to get to the screens you're looking for.

Recent findings suggest that that doesn't mean Football Manager 27 has a good UI. I still too often find myself hunting for basic actions now buried several menus deep, like having to click Portal - Career - My Profile - Actions - Go On Holiday to start simming through fixtures. For reference, here's how it worked in Championship Manager 01/02: [Manager Name] - Go On Holiday.

It has been revealed that I still find myself struggling to process the morass of information being thrown at me by certain menus too, particularly the matchday screens. More detail does not equal more fun, and most of these info panels are useless to me, serving only to obscure the bits I do want to check. There's more customisation this year to allow what these menus show you, but you can't remove info panels entirely or simplify screens.

In a recent development, just like the obsession that a Football Manager game inspires, it also has a way of making minor annoyances feel big over time. When that happens, you have to zoom out and remind yourself it got you to care this much in the first place because the experience is fundamentally great. It's like a Paradox strategy game where all the nobles are 20-year-old inside forwards. It's a labyrinth of menus that makes you want to give up and do something else, but you don't. Because there's so much sandbox potential, such a vast and detailed world being simulated in minute detail, and such a feeling of payoff when those long-term looks come good.

In a recent development, and that's why it's so significant that Football Manager's biggest changes are about giving you transparency about what's going wrong, what you need to do to fix it, and then letting you progress at the speed you want to. That makes it feel less like a complicated German board game you lost the instructions for, and more like managing a football team.

In a recent development, faster-moving, sometimes maddening, and obsession-forming. Football Manager finds a way to make spreadsheets fun again.

Mucky and disreputable kiosk game Probably Stolen – Cyberpunk Shopkeeper Sim is getting three big updates over the next few months that add extra starting scenarios, building on the existing wealth of goods, materials, vocations and techs. Those starting scenarios range from peddling human meat to running the finest cyber-frappucino stall this side of Tannhäuser Gate. There are no hard release dates, and the contents of each enhancement may alter, but developers Questing Goose Studio have shared some rough timeframes.

Industry observers note that coming up in mid-December, there's the Junker starting scenario, which I assume is all about trading scrap, rather than being a Prussian nobleman. You'll get a bespoke perk, fresh items, and the ability to hire, equip and send scavs on expeditions. This update will also include some minor expansions for the Fence and Gunsmith vocations – the latter will be able to flog or otherwise make use of shotgun shells, 25mm grenade rounds and a tier 3 handmade SMG, alongside new armour.

It has been revealed that late January is when you'll "very likely" get the chance to be an Organ Dealer, care of the second major update. "Players will start by buying different organs and fulfilling specific requests, and will later be able to grow or print organs," a Steam blog explains. You'll also be able to filter blood and remove diseases, with different blood types having different value modifiers. How will you get your hands on organs? By sending horrible black market thugs on foraging "expeditions".

Last but not least, the planned April revision will add the Street Food Vendor starting scenario. This lets you weave a livelihood around choice beverages and edibles from a range of cultures, supported by updates to the game's Aquaculture and Hydroponics tech. Sounds a lot cheerier than the organ trading racket, but then again, Probably Stolen will doubtless find a way to make it utterly grim. Guests at Sweeney's Cantina know better than to ask what our frappucinos are made of.

Industry observers note that are you playing Probably Stolen? It's been doing better than expected. I was keen on the demo, but my attention was lured away by a truly upsetting game about dogpeople in caves.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Developer FromSoftware has unveiled that online multiplayer servers for Dark Souls 2 and 3 are back online following a nearly two-week outage.

According to recent reports, fromSoftware temporarily disabled multiplayer on 30th October, citing what it called "a server matter". Some speculated this could be related to the recently discovered PHP security bug, which impacted a number of other games.

Recent findings suggest that fromSoftware never specified the exact issue impacting its servers, and today's statement is equally vague. "Regarding the temporary suspension of the game server for Dark Souls 2, and Dark Souls 3, the investigation has been completed and the fix has been applied. The game server and online features are now restored," a notice on Dark Souls' official site reads.

"We sincerely apologise for the inconvenience caused, and thank you for your patience and understanding.".

Online servers do more in FromSoftware games than simply facilitating co-op and PvP; they're also responsible for handling messages players leave for each other in-game, as well as the ghostly representations of players who just went through the same area, helping the Dark Souls series' forlorn worlds feel a little less solitary.

According to recent reports, this isn't the first time Dark Souls servers have gone offline, either. In 2022, servers for all three games went offline due to a vulnerability that allowed malicious code to run on them. In that instance, it took FromSoftware three months to bring servers back online for some games, and as many as nine months for others.

In other FromSoftware news, the studio recently confirmed - following months of speculation - it's officially delaying the Switch 2-exclusive The Duskbloods to sometime in 2027.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The initial reviews have arrived for GTA 6, and it's safe to say the game has been an absolute smash hit with critics.

The metascore has settled on a 99, making it one point off a "perfect" score of 100. In a year stuffed with fantastic games substantial and small, it's become the highest rated title of 2026.

More than that, though, it's the highest rated game of all time.

Reaching 99 is almost unheard of; only one other game has achieved the same level of acclaim — The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (1998).

However, GTA 6 has held onto its 99 score after more than 160 reviews; Ocarina of Time's metascore counts just 22 — though that's of course indicative of the era in which it released. There are simply more gaming outlets now, but that just means it's tougher to get consistent scores.

Rockstar's crime caper has received insanely consistent acclaim, and that might just give it an edge over the Nintendo classic. It's incredibly rare to see near-total agreement on a subjective work like this.

Critics are unanimous in their praise of GTA 6's open world, the relationship between protagonists Jason and Lucia, and the complex systems behind its myriad characters, activities, and missions.

Here are some snippets from just a few of the reviews — including our own, of course.

In a recent development, "GTA 6 is the deepest, densest, most accomplished open world since Red Dead Redemption 2. Rockstar has set a new sandbox standard here, with a world that feels alive and populated with real people; Leonida is a place where it appears almost anything can happen at any time.".

Sources indicate that "Somehow, GTA 6 lives up to the hype. Rockstar Games has crafted the most incredible open world I've ever experienced in a video game, packed with so much detail that I'll want to continue exploring it for months and likely years to come. It's coupled with a campaign that's full of extremely entertaining missions, led by two main characters who I've become much more invested in than I'd anticipated.".

"Like all videogame protagonists, Jason and Lucia are ciphers through which the player exerts their will on the digital world. And yet, through the co-authored interplay of the characters Rockstar has written, and the people you personally tune them into becoming, they form one of the great partnerships in entertainment: beautiful and deadly, open to the possibilities of their world and, despite the violence they inflict on those beyond their circle, driven forward not by fear, but by love.".

Sources indicate that "A game of opposites and awe, minute detail and impossible scale, Rockstar pushes back the horizon of video games once again with GTA 6. An irreducible mix of silliness, intimacy, grand ideas and rock 'n' roll action - and a load more after that.".

"Rockstar Games' latest release is a monumental achievement in storytelling, immersion, gameplay, and breadth of content.".

Industry observers note that "GTA 6 is the highest-fidelity sandbox of its generation. Rockstar has built an open world of truly astonishing scale, scope, and quality. There's a degree of sophistication to everything GTA 6 does, and there's no aspect of the series' gameplay that hasn't been improved over past instalments.".

"Only Rockstar commands the time and money necessary to make a game as dedicated to small details. And only Rockstar can execute on the realising such a granular vision unimpeachably. The obsession with the minutia both explains and justifies the 13-year wait. This game is the culmination of everything the developer has previously achieved in the open-world space that pushes the genre to heights that, in all likelihood, no other developer will be able to reach. GTA 6 is an astonishing open-world action game that I’d wager won’t be outdone until Grand Theft Auto 7.".

"Exquisitely detailed, endlessly ripe for experimentation, and uncompromisingly engineered, Grand Theft Auto 6 is the single most impressive video game I have ever played.".

"Grand Theft Auto 6 is a modern masterpiece. Rockstar's developers have created a remarkable open world that excels in storytelling, gameplay, visuals, music and technology to achieve something truly unmatched. Minor performance issues don’t dull the sparkle of an absolute must-play experience. GTA 6 was more than worth the wait.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, hoYoverse just wrapped up a fresh Genshin Impact Special Program, where the developer revealed everything there is to know about the game’s next major enhancement. Truth Amongst the Pages of Purana, or as its friends call it, Luna 7, was unveiled as part of the showcase.

This next patch has a lot going for it, and it will be in players’ hands everywhere on May 20.

Recent findings suggest that luna 7 will take us back to Sumeru for its new Archon Quest, where a new crisis that threatens to plunge the nation into chaos is brewing. Nahida is out of the picture, and someone who looks suspiciously like Il Dottore has emerged.

If you complete this chapter at launch, you’ll earn up to 560 Primogems, as well as Nicole's Ascension Materials. Nicole is the first of three playable characters arriving with this patch. Something else you’ll unlock if you finish the chapter rapidly is a newly introduced Weekly Boss that HoYo says has “unpredictable abilities.”.

And if you haven’t played in a while, don’t worry, you can refer to the Guiding Notes feature to catch you up on what’s been going on in the world. This is part of a larger effort from the team to make story progression more seamless, and also includes improved quest autosave prompts.

Nicole Reeyn is highest-profile and most interesting, being the first playable member of the Hexenzirkel. The mage is a 5-Star Pyro Catalyst wielder intended as a support member of the team. She can boost the ATK of all party members, even those not at the moment on the field. She also generates a shield while doing so.

Industry observers note that her Elemental Burst allows her to summon an Arcane Projection that follows the active character, sending out Coordinated Attacks that match their Elemental Type. Outside of combat, Nicole can help you find treasures by calling upon a Seelie to guide you to them. Quite fitting, as you’ll be exploring in the inside of the Witch's Lodge in Nicole’s Meeting Point in Luna 7, so bring her along.

Industry observers note that lohen, the Vice Captain of the Knights of Favonius' Fifth Manufacturer, is the second upcoming character. Also a 5-Star addition, he is instead a Cryo Polearm wielder designed for aggressive combat. His main use is dealing massive Cryo DMG, and he can do that by managing two resources unique to him: Joy, and Will to Win.

Recent findings suggest that through his Elemental Skill, he can enter the Masterstroke state, allowing him to build up (and consume) Joy to unleash enhanced skills. The more his teammates fight, the more Will to Win he biulds, which can later be used to boost his effectiveness further. For an even more powerful display of force, bring along a Hexerei character when he’s on your team.

Recent findings suggest that prune is the third and final addition. Prune is a 4-Star Anemo Catalyst wielder, and her kit is inspired by her Witch Hunter aspirations. Using a bell and a hammer, she can deal DMG of several elements at once, and trigger Swirl reactions.

It has been revealed that nicole, and Lohen will debut in Luna 7’s first half, while Prune will follow in the second. The first half will also see a Durin rerun, with Mavuika returning in the second half. You can look forward to a latest limited-time event as part of Luna 7, with a focus on Klee's Little Hexenzirkel.

You’ll find a series of mini-games you can play alongside Prune, as well as Qiqi, Yaoyao, and Sayu. If you play, you could earn the Super Awesome Magic Key, an exclusive weapon skin. Miliastra Wonderland is doing its thing, too, with a new sports festival for you to take part in.

One fresh gameplay addition worth calling attention to is that Manekins can now perform actions in Teyvat. The Kamera, which you can use to capture moments with Manekins, is getting upgraded, too, with new editing tools and assets.

Before you pick the game back up, be sure to check out our recently-updated Genshin Impact codes page for some free stuff you may be missing.

Review: GTA 6 (Xbox) - The Most Breathtaking Open-World Game Of All Time

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1574 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Purexbox

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, where do you even start with a game like GTA 6?
  • We've all spent the last 13 years trying to figure out what GTA 6 might look like by the time it arrives, and the answer is perhaps more simplistic than some had theorised - it's basically GTA 5 mixed with Red Dead Redemption 2, but with a ton of added detail and ambition on top.
  • Industry observers note that before we get to the open world, which is surely the most incredible aspect of the entire game, we should first touch on the story of Lucia and Jason.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, where do you even start with a game like GTA 6? Not only is it the most highly-anticipated video game we've ever seen, but it's also attempting to live up to ridiculous expectations set by its predecessors over the years. GTA 3 revolutionised how we thought about 3D open-world epics, Vice City and San Andreas pushed things to the next level, GTA 4 took yet another massive step into the HD era, and GTA 5 propelled the series into another stratosphere.

We've all spent the last 13 years trying to figure out what GTA 6 might look like by the time it arrives, and the answer is perhaps more simplistic than some had theorised - it's basically GTA 5 mixed with Red Dead Redemption 2, but with a ton of added detail and ambition on top. That's all it needed to be, and I reckon people are going to absolutely love it.

Industry observers note that before we get to the open world, which is surely the most incredible aspect of the entire game, we should first touch on the story of Lucia and Jason. These two amateur criminals accidentally run into each other and establish a relationship (which can alter between platonic and romantic depending on how you interact throughout the campaign), and after a simple score goes wrong, they find themselves being dragged into more and more dangerous scenarios. That's the basic premise, and the rest is up for you to discover yourself.

The GTA 6 Extended Preview from a few months ago left me very concerned about whether there was enough intrigue to the two main characters (along with the NPCs for that matter), but I needn't have worried. Lucia is a fiesty, hot-headed personality - the type of person who thinks less about the consequences and more about the high life she's determined to acquire - while Jason is extremely laid back to a hilarious extent at times, although also highly capable in pretty much any situation he finds himself in. The two bounce off each other really nicely, and their dynamic definitely remains engaging throughout the campaign's duration.

Industry observers note that while I really don't want to spoil anything story-related, the mission structure is very much what you'd expect from GTA 5 and RDR2. In other words, there's a well-balanced mix of laid-back and humorous missions along with more intense shootouts and getaways that significantly ramp up in intensity. They've managed to get really inventive and ambitious with some of the later missions in particular, and I think there's no doubt they're the best of any GTA game.

I also want to point out the use of music in GTA 6's missions, which caught me off-guard and became one of my low-key favourite features. In a nutshell, if you find yourself in the likes of a shootout or a getaway, you'll often notice that curated tunes play in the background to amplify the situation. The developers sometimes even go a step further by making the lighting around you pulsate to the beat, or by introducing lyricists to create a menacing vibe, and it can turn an otherwise generic mission into an amazing one. Seriously, I can't overstate how much I love this feature.

Sources indicate that the story itself takes 40ish hours if you completely rush it (which admittedly I've been doing for the most part to hit this embargo), but if you take your time and do at least a decent amount of the optional stuff, it's likely more around 60-100+ hours. As I say, I've enjoyed all of those hours, and I think the campaign seriously hits its stride in the final third - the vast majority of memorable moments are saved for the latter stages.

I don't want you to fixate on the 40-100+ hour figure though, and that's because GTA 6's open world is so incredible and so vast that you could be playing it for months, and likely years, and not see everything it has to offer. We've never seen a GTA world like this - traffic levels are extremely high, the number of NPCs on the streets is ridiculous, it always feels like something's happening around every corner (there are so many random encounters!), you'll find loads of buildings you can go into, there's so much detail on everything... it's just an absolute dream for anyone who loves the idea of immersing themselves in this game.

It has been revealed that GTA 5 had an amazing open world too, but after going back and playing it for the purpose of this review, there are two major differences that stand out - there's far less actually happening in the world at any one time (and therefore much less to interact with), and the map just feels tiny in comparison. GTA 6's state of Leonida incorporates so much more than just Vice City itself, including many other highly-populated areas such as Key Lento and Ambrosia. The first time you actually see Vice City in a mission (assuming you haven't gone and explored it previously) is a highlight of the entire game - it immediately appears so vast and so incredibly detailed that it feels like a next-gen experience.

In a recent development, the way in which you interact with that world as a player has evolved as well. Cops are smarter than ever, and not only prove a tough challenge when attempting a getaway at three stars or more, but they also remember what you look like - and therefore you sometimes have to disguise yourself by changing into different outfits. Stealing a car now requires you to think about what kind of lock system it has on it, and whether there's a tracker fitted that will alert the police to your location. Cars can even run out of fuel now! Every element feels more in-depth than we've seen in GTA in the past, but Rockstar has crucially balanced the impact just right, so it's never to the detriment of your ability to just have fun.

I do think you'll get the most out of the game if you pace yourself though. It feels intentionally designed to encourage a slow playstyle where you explore, hang out, browse the fully-featured social media and news feeds on your phone (complete with video clips and comment sections), take part in games like pool and minigolf, engage in countless side-missions and random encounters, watch and play a ridiculous amount of purpose-built content on your in-game TV, and ultimately just see what you can discover without rapidly jumping from mission-to-mission. The amount of content here is overwhelming, but in a really satisfying way.

Of course, it's almost a given at this point that GTA 6 looks visually incredible, and I can confirm that it's definitely a stunner on Xbox Series X. There's some occasional pop-in, but it's minimal, and I only ran into a few tiny bugs during the review period (which may have been ironed out for release anyway). The performance is mostly very smooth considering the circumstances as well - yes, it's a bit jarring at first to go back to 30FPS if you've been playing 60FPS games for the most part in recent years, but give it an hour-or-two, and you probably won't care anymore. Seriously, it's a total non-concern for me at this point, and I'm more than happy playing at 30FPS.

It should be noted that I played around 30 hours on a VRR-enabled display during the review period, and around 10 hours without one. I was perfectly happy with the performance in both cases, with the only noticeably significant frame rate drops occurring during very rare and visually intensive gameplay sequences.

Industry observers note that so, is there anything I don't like about GTA 6? The only thing I'd say is that it doesn't top my tier list in terms of greatest GTA stories ever, although it's probably still in the top three. It's a narrative that'll fully invest most players from start to finish, and there are shocking moments and twists that are bound to last long in the memory, but I also reckon it gets a bit too convoluted and farcical at times. That said, the final third of the campaign is jam-packed with intense story elements and incredibly action-packed missions, guaranteeing some truly jaw-dropping moments.

Its tone can also feel overly harsh and uncomfortably serious in specific circumstances, but hey... this is Grand Theft Auto after all. Every GTA has its moments like that, but the impact feels more striking this time due to the enhanced sense of realism. Fortunately, there's plenty of lighthearted humour to be found along the way as well.

Recent findings suggest that somehow, GTA 6 lives up to the hype. Rockstar Games has crafted the most incredible open world I've ever experienced in a video game, packed with so much detail that I'll want to continue exploring it for months and likely years to come. It's coupled with a campaign that's full of extremely entertaining missions, led by two main characters who I've become much more invested in than I'd anticipated.

I'd have been fuming if you'd told me in 2013 that I'd have to wait 13 more years for the next GTA game, but now that it's finally here, I'm just relieved they've somehow managed to pull off another Game of the Decade contender once again.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, we're less than a month out from Avengers: Doomsday, and we still don't know for sure if Deadpool and Wolverine will appear in the worlds-colliding Marvel movie.
  • When you break it down, Deadpool 3 and Doomsday share a lot of similarities.
  • But it cannot be denied that Doomsday looks a whole lot darker than the third Deadpool entry.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, we're less than a month out from Avengers: Doomsday, and we still don't know for sure if Deadpool and Wolverine will appear in the worlds-colliding Marvel movie. But even if the chalk-and-cheese duo doesn't show up in the new movie, the comedy outing reveals us how even in the face of universes colliding, you can still have a bit of fun.

When you break it down, Deadpool 3 and Doomsday share a lot of similarities. Both movies feature Marvel heroes at risk of their respective universes being destroyed by a new threat, and the only way to combat the substantial bad is to join forces with other comic book figures. Heck, a sprinkle of the original Fox-era X-Men show up in both features.

But it cannot be denied that Doomsday looks a whole lot darker than the third Deadpool entry. So, with so much impending Doom (quite literally), I just hope Doomsday has taken note from Deadpool 3, and adds some humor along the way.

In a recent development, even before it has hit screens, it is clear that the upcoming Marvel Phase 6 movie will go to some dark places. The official synopsis hints that Doomsday will close the chapter on the MCU as we know it, saying goodbye to certain heroes to make way for latest ones, reading: "Courageous teams from three universes must come together to prevent a catastrophic event… Their choices and actions in this crucial moment will lay the foundation for the future of the Multiverse." In many ways, it feels like the beginning of the end.

It has been revealed that welcome to Road to Doomsday, GamesRadar+'s weekly MCU rewatch series. Over 15 weeks, we'll be revisiting each Marvel movie and TV show on Disney's list of essential movies to watch ahead of Avengers: Doomsday, sharing our thoughts upon rewatching and deciphering what we can learn about the next Marvel mega-event from each entry. Why not relive some MCU highlights and watch along with us?

The Doomsday cast list is so unbelievably stacked that some heroes are sure to perish earlier on, and I am fearing the worst for the original Fox-era X-Men. This would make sense, as the original X-Men, including Patrick Stewart's Charles Xavier, Ian McKellen's Magneto, and James Marsden, have never been part of the MCU. So, it seems odd to bring them back now, just as a latest X-Men movie is in the works, set to introduce a younger group of the same mutants. Yeah, it's not looking good.

But Doomsday doesn't have to be all doom and gloom. Deadpool has had his fair share of setbacks, from losing his wife to literally being tortured into the scarred-faced mutant we know today. The anti-hero's traumatic background is often forgotten due to his sense of humor. He has even more hurdles thrown his way in Deadpool & Wolverine, when the TVA threatens to destroy his own universe. But, amongst the carnage, one of the most successful R-rated movies of all time still dished out the gags, from Chris Evans' cameo as Johnny Storm to Deadpool poking fun at Kevin Feige's "no-cocaine rule.".

With that in mind, there's obviously something missing from Doomsday's recipe. That is, of course, self-proclaimed 'Marvel Jesus' himself and his clawed buddy. Even though Reynolds and Jackman's Doomsday casting has not been unveiled, I have a strong feeling that a cameo is on the way. Why would Marvel Studios have included Deadpool & Wolverine in its list of essential MCU movies to watch ahead of Doomsday if not? The clues are everywhere. Whenever there is a big Doomsday announcement, Reynolds is not far behind.

Avengers: Doomsday has a chance to right the wrongs of Captain America: Brave New World and do Sam Wilson's Cap justice.

During Marvel's panel at San Diego Comic-Con 2026, Reynolds crashed the event dressed in a dark denim Deadpool suit (riffing off 'Jean Grey'). But we wonder why he was there at all when he doesn't have an upcoming Marvel movie to promote. The star has been leaving breadcrumbs all year, teasing his involvement by posting the Avengers logo with an anarchy sticker over the top, and saying that Deadpool "works best on scarcity and surprise." The plot thickens as Reynolds and Jackman have screenwriting credits on Avengers: Doomsday, per the Writers Guild of America’s directory, to which Reynolds responded, "Not to brag, but I do not read.".

Could Deadpool and Wolverine's unlikely duo be just what Avengers: Doomsday needs? I think so. If anything, the 2024 movie proves that when the world is at risk of complete destruction, audiences need a goofy moment or two to keep them hanging on. Of course, Robert Downey Jr.'s Doctor Doom will be a lot harder to defeat than Cassandra Nova, but with such a huge team (plus the Merc with a Mouth and Logan possibly on standby), I'm still holding out hope for the Avengers.

Deadpool & Wolverine is available to stream now on Disney Plus, ahead of the release of Avengers: Doomsday on December 18 in the US and 16 in the UK.

Look ahead with our list of upcoming Marvel movies and check out how to watch the Marvel movies in order ahead of your next rewatch. See you next week as we revisit Captain America: Brave Latest World.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Mystic Messenger, arguably one of the best dating sims around, has been dormant for about seven years.
  • The free-to-play mobile dating sim has started banning players with seemingly too many Hourglasses - the game’s virtual currency - saved up in their accounts.
  • The news exploded on the Mystic Messenger subreddit overnight, with over a dozen reports from players logging in to play normally, only to receive an in-game notice that their accounts had been banned.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mystic Messenger, arguably one of the best dating sims around, has been dormant for about seven years. Despite not receiving new content or any meaningful updates in all that time, the game remains popular with its core fans, many of whom just woke up to some shocking news about their accounts.

The free-to-play mobile dating sim has started banning players with seemingly too many Hourglasses - the game’s virtual currency - saved up in their accounts. So far, it looks like players with 1,000 or more have been targeted, but others with far fewer hoards have reported getting the axe, too.

The news exploded on the Mystic Messenger subreddit overnight, with over a dozen reports from players logging in to play normally, only to receive an in-game notice that their accounts had been banned.

Recent findings suggest that the message players received is identical, and doesn’t mention the specific reason for the ban. “Your account has been banned because abusive behavior has been detected from your account,” it reads, ending with a support email address the affected user can contact if they believe they’d banned in error.

Sources indicate that it didn’t take a while for players to realise that most, if not all of the bans are for players with thousands of Hourglasses in their accounts. The virtual currency can both be acquired in-game just by playing, as well as through direct real-money purchases.

For a nearly ten-year-old game that stopped receiving content three years into its life, it’s easy to see how a dedicated group of players would be able to acquire so many Hourglasses by simply playing regularly for so long.

When contacted by the affected players, Cheritz, the developer and publisher of the game, has instructed them to send receipts of how they acquired Hourglasses (assuming they were purchased) to verify whether or not they’d been fraudulently obtained.

Considering that Mystic Messenger has practically been abandoned by its developer, certain exploits have emerged over the years that allowed players to farm Hourglasses faster than intended, but those instances have always been dealt with then and there.

The blanket and sudden nature of this ban is what’s spooked players, especially those who’ve been logging in for years and never thought accruing in-game currency from playing the game too much would make them the target of a ban.

The running theory is that most of the bans are unintentional, and may be the result of a latest automated security system that’s been implemented. It’s entirely possible, especially if its’s AI-based, that the new system simply couldn’t distinguish between those who have earned (or bought) their Hourglasses fairly, and those who used exploits.

The timing of the ban wave is also suspect. With the game’s 10th anniversary coming up in July, it could be that Cheriz is preparing to release a large revision for Mystic Messenger, which may include newly introduced content. If most of the playerbase is already sitting on massive amounts of in-game currency, they may simply use that to fast-track their way to unlocking the new content, which would greatly affect the developer’s bottom line.

Industry observers note that this is a problem that other live service games have run into in the past. Just recently, extraction shooter Arc Raiders added a cap to the amount of Cred players can hold in their accounts very quickly after its launch. That currency is used to buy cosmetic sets in the store, so the logic is easy to follow.

All of that has certainly put a damper on the enthusiasm of the game’s most active players, many of whom were excited to get together in person for the coming 10th anniversary, participate in community nights and so on to celebrate.

It’s also disheartening to see a fanbase so loyal; playing a game as regularly for so long without new content, to be treated so poorly. Even without knowing what the game is, it’s impressive that so many people have kept the flag of their favourite game flying for so long.

To find out how this dating system works, here’s a Mystic Messenger primer that explains it all. Once you’ve wrapped your head around it, you’ll no doubt want to pick the correct answers for every guest, and this guide will help you nail every one.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • CD Projekt Red has revealed that it used - and is using - generative AI technology to treat and alter the voice of the Polish actor who portrayed Geralt of Rivia in upcoming Witcher 3 expansion Songs of the Past.
  • Sources indicate that the actor, Jacek Rozenek, has portrayed Geralt of Rivia in all the major Witcher games, meaning his voice has become as synonymous with the role in Poland as Doug Cockle's has for people playing in English.
  • In a recent development, it's for these reasons that CD Projekt Red - with Rozenek's consent - employed the help of a manufacturer called Respeecher to alter the lines he recorded for The Witcher 3's Songs of the Past expansion using generative-AI technology.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

CD Projekt Red has revealed that it used - and is using - generative AI technology to treat and alter the voice of the Polish actor who portrayed Geralt of Rivia in upcoming Witcher 3 expansion Songs of the Past.

Sources indicate that the actor, Jacek Rozenek, has portrayed Geralt of Rivia in all the major Witcher games, meaning his voice has become as synonymous with the role in Poland as Doug Cockle's has for people playing in English. But Rozenek suffered a severe stroke in 2019 that left him temporarily unable to speak, and when he was able to talk and perform again, the tonality and quality of his voice had changed.

In a recent development, it's for these reasons that CD Projekt Red - with Rozenek's consent - employed the help of a manufacturer called Respeecher to alter the lines he recorded for The Witcher 3's Songs of the Past expansion using generative-AI technology. As confirmed to Game File, an AI trained on Rozenek's previous Witcher work is retreating his recordings to make them sound more like the Geralt you hear elsewhere in The Witcher 3.

It has been revealed that "The point is that this voice should be as close as possible to my voice from 12 years ago," Jacek Rozenek explained. "I have great trust ... for the creators of this game.".

Game File heard both treated and untreated recordings of Rozenek's Songs of the Past work, and reported a "significant" difference between them. Rozenek's untreated voice was apparently "deep and gravelly" and "noticeably rougher than his recordings for the original game". But treated, the voice was "far smoother and sounds younger", and closer to the original Witcher 3 Geralt recordings.

According to recent reports, this isn't the first time CD Projekt Red has used generative AI for voice recordings in one of its games. The studio worked with Respeecher in 2023 to produce new voiceover lines for Cyberpunk 2077 expansion Phantom Liberty. Viktor Vektor actor Miłogost "Miłek" Reczek passed away in 2021, after the original game was released, and CD Projekt Red didn't want to recast the role. Reczek's sons apparently gave their blessing for their father's voice to be artificially generated.

"I do think this is one of those ways where you can use AI ethically with consent and also to do something good," CD Projekt Red localisation producer Mikołaj Szwed told Game File, referring to the Rozenek recordings.

"For future projects, when we consider Geralt is becoming older and has a deeper voice, this is not a problem for us at all. It's more about this specific situation here, where we have both the voice from 12 years ago and from now next to each other, which could kind of take people out of the experience and feel that there is this difference.".

Sources indicate that the third Witcher 3 expansion, Songs of the Past, releases at some point next year, an unprecedented 12 years after the original game rolled out. It adds an entirely newly introduced region, Letten, and centres its main story around Geralt's missing bardic bestie Dandelion, whose family lives there.

In preparation for the expansion, a remastered version of The Witcher 3 was released a couple of months ago, overhauling the old role-playing adventure and bringing its baseline presentation more in line with what we'd expect from a modern game; it also overhauled some animations and enemy behaviours and reworked skill trees. For that reason, old-gen consoles PS4 and Xbox One won't receive the Songs of the Past expansion, despite The Witcher 3 being available on them.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • I am nothing if not entirely predictable.
  • It has been revealed that GTA 5, once it made its way to PC, was always a game I played both with a keyboard and mouse and with a controller plugged in.
  • It has been revealed that it was the same with Red Dead Redemption 2, a game I completely avoided until it finally came to the PC.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I am nothing if not entirely predictable. I've waited 13 years to play a upcoming Grand Theft Auto game and the first thing I do when I finally get around to booting GTA 6—and definitely not spoofing my home address to access it early—is jam a mouse and keyboard into my Xbox Series X just to see.

It has been revealed that GTA 5, once it made its way to PC, was always a game I played both with a keyboard and mouse and with a controller plugged in. Keeb and rodent for shooting, especially in the first-person mode, and the controller for just getting about in the game world. It was a real best of both worlds kinda thing that the PC does so well.

It has been revealed that it was the same with Red Dead Redemption 2, a game I completely avoided until it finally came to the PC. Keyboard and mouse for runnin' and gunnin' and a controller for horsin' around. Yeehaw.

So, I was hoping—hoping against hope, really—that I could just do the same with GTA 6. I was hoping that I could just plug in my little Mountain keyboard and my DeathAdder mouse, and it would just work.

Recent findings suggest that sadly no, there is no mouse and keyboard support for GTA 6. There is for Xbox, and my keyboard works fine just in the home screens, but as soon as you hit the game itself… nada. Keyboard and mouse support is still very much an occasional thing for Microsoft's console. It is supported, but it's on a per-game basis where devs have to actively code support into their Xbox versions of a title in order for a keyboard and mouse to work.

According to recent reports, it's not actually that rare—some 450 games, and substantial games such as Cyberpunk 2077 and Alan Wake 2, have some level of support for one or both peripherals. But it is certainly not something Rockstar has spent any time putting in place when it was spending an extra year optimising the game after the delayed release. Which is a shame, given that the organization has gone to great lengths to add a huge level of detail to its world to the point it almost feels like it's thought of everything.

More frustrating given that right now I bet there are Rockstar developers playing the game on keyboard and mouse in internal PC-only builds of the game. Would I have sacrificed sitting on my comfy sofa playing it writ large on my living room wall through my 4K projector just to sit at my desk with a keyboard and mouse? Maybe. It would have certainly felt like I was playing it on PC.

The PC Gamer Circuit Breaker newsletter breaks down the latest PC gaming tech, and finds you the best deals on the best products.

Something else Rockstar hasn't put into the game is any steering wheel control. Jacob, as a racing fan, tried to get his PlayStation wheelbase running on his PS5 copy of the game… but alas that is unsupported, too. Which was a source of frustration for him as he co-opted his partner in carrying his sim rig into his living room to try it out and now she is refusing to help put it back after his failure.

But this is a situation that might have to change moving forward. The next-gen Xbox machine, codenamed Helix has already been confirmed as being able to play PC games. In a recent interview with Jason Ronald, Xbox VP of Next Gen, this was again reiterated.

It has been revealed that "We're very clear on the design goal: Helix is designed to be a console that is also capable of playing games from your PC," says Ronald. "It is not a PC that can also play console games.".

Recent findings suggest that this means it's going to have to support PC games, and that potentially means baked in support for keyboard and mouse in the hardware itself, rather than enabled on a per-title basis. After all, PC games kinda take those inputs for granted, no? So, maybe Red Dead Redemption 3 on Project Helix might come with keyboard and mouse support from the get-go, even if it's not necessarily released on PC straight away.

Still, for GTA 6 right now, basically it's controller or nothing, so make sure to get yourself a good pad—that's one of the biggest upgrades I've made to my setup for GTA 6.

Steam is abuzz this week with a couple of long-anticipated rolls out, but in Forza Horizon 6’s case, at least, the game isn’t even out for what will be most of its players. The anticipated sequel in the open-world driving game series doesn’t officially launch until May 19, but owners of its most expensive version - the Premium Edition - can play it right now.

Recent findings suggest that that version of the game includes more than just a few days of early access, of course, but you’d think the $120 price tag would’ve only been palatable to a small group of players. Not the case with this game.

Industry observers note that forza Horizon 6, which has spent 16 weeks in Steam’s global top sellers list, right now occupies the number two spot, having jumped up three spots this week in anticipation of the launch. The game has also naturally been popular with players, so popular in fact that it has already overtaken the player counts of all other Horizon games on the platform.

It has been revealed that at the time of writing, the game has peaked at 128,157 concurrent players on Steam alone (via SteamDB). The figure has already climbed several times during the writing of this story, so you can only imagine how much higher it’s going to get deeper into the weekend.

All of that, of course, days before the official launch on Tuesday, when, theoretically, the majority of the game’s audience will be able to start playing. In just a few short hours, Horizon 6 has already gone well above Forza Horizon 5’s peak concurrent of 81,096, as well as Forza Horizon 4’s peak 75,689 players.

It has been revealed that steam is the only platform that publishes player numbers, of course, but it’s easy to see how similar the enthusiasm is going to be on Xbox. Though the game is not yet part of the Game Pass line-up, those who don’t want to wait could buy the Premium Edition Upgrade to get the included content, and play it right now.

It has been revealed that game Pass, and Xbox / Windows Store numbers don’t factor into Steam’s, which is another thing to consider when viewing the numbers holistically. Indeed, given how successful Forza Horizon 5 has been on PlayStation 5, Horizon 6’s upcoming release on Sony's console is bound to be even bigger.

Industry observers note that forza Horizon 5 has been off to a similarly flying start in the first few days of its own advanced access launch, so it’s obviously not surprising to see Horizon 6 do better there. In case you missed it, check out our review of Forza Horizon 6. In short, we really liked it, even if we expected more.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, valve has issued an revision on its Steam Machine stock levels, waiting lists, and purchasing process, saying that the 512GB model has now achieved "add to cart status". After months of joining a lottery-based waiting list to secure the brand's alternative to a gaming PC, you can now grab the entry-level model and its bundled controller with no waiting or reservation constraints.

In a recent development, unfortunately, the same can't be mentioned of the 2TB model, which could even see further price hikes, let alone wait lists. Valve posted an revision to its hardware blog yesterday evening, confirming that despite the doom and gloom of the 2TB model, "We've finished getting purchase invites out to all reservation holders.".

The blog post states, "We've been able to fulfill all current reservations for the 512GB model with no waitlist remaining, and have wrapped up sending purchase invites out to all remaining 2TB reservation holders.

"However, we are continuing to encounter supply constraints for hardware components, which impacts our ability to source parts.".

The Steam Machine, along with the Steam Controller and Steam Frame, were all meant to launch in "early 2026", but the very same supply constraints Valve is mentioning this week caused massive delays and (presumably) big price hikes on the organization's new generation of hardware.

On the 2TB model's future availability, Valve says: "We expect to have more details to share in January about additional supply.".

But given the RAM shortages that are ongoing, and that SSD prices just keep increasing, it's highly likely that Valve will need to jump the 2TB model's price to even higher ranges in the new year, because the current RAM and SSD situation reveals no sign of stopping.

"We are continuing to build more Steam Machine units, but memory and storage costs continue to increase at unprecedented levels; as a result we don't yet know the number we are able to make, and at what price we'll be able to offer them," says Valve.

With more updates in January, it seems as though Valve is issuing a fairly general and open-ended statement here in order to leave a lot of wiggle room. But the above quote in particular leaves the possibility open for a temporary discontinuation of the 2TB model, or a price hike on fresh stock.

Thankfully, if people are still on the waiting list for a 2TB model, Valve is allowing them to choose a 512GB model instead while supplies last, while opting out of the queue for the 2TB version.

That may be the best alternative when stock levels are this uncertain, as Valve claims, "the number of customers on the waitlist exceeds our current production; even when we are able to build more it will be at smaller quantities than we planned.".

The upcoming update adds a newly introduced chapter to the Planarcadia arc, and introduce a new playable character.

The newly introduced narrative chapter will also unveil more about Mortenax Blade, the Trailblazer themselves, and the husk of the Aeon.

Mortenax Blade is the hero of this chapter, and he’s going to step into the World in Canvas. The goal is to - by borrowing the power of Voracity - excise Shuhu from his body and end the curse.

The Trailblazer goes on a trip of their own in Version 4.3, this time to Inkford Hermitage, right on the edge between the World in Canvas and the real world. They’re going to undertake this journey to warn Graphia of the Asat Pramad threat.

In a recent development, in case you hadn’t already guessed, Mortenax Blade is this version’s new playable character. The 5-Star Fire-Type swordsman is on the Path of Nihility. Blade’s Ultimate allows him to enter an enhanced state by deploying a special Bounded Field.

In a recent development, while the field is active, all enemies receive more DMG. Entering this state is also how Blade unlocks his skill, which uses a Sword Formation to deal more damage. This is then used to essentially unlock a second, more powerful Ultimate for him.

Industry observers note that the benefits of Mortenax Blade’s kit extend to his teammates, too. Any ally who attacks an enemy with him on the team, they inflict a debuff on them. This also builds up a special Charge that Blade can later use with his Skill.

Version 4.3’s launch arrives alongside the Gift of Tempered Blade event. Through it, you can claim a new Trailblazer Outfit piece for free, but only after getting Mortenax Blade from Warping. The first phase’s rerun will be Yao Guang, and the second phase will bring back both Cyrene and Phainon.

You can also expect the Wispae Amusement Park to arrive within the World in Canvas, which you’ll get to design. You can blueprint where the rides will go, pick the different themes, set visitor routes and more.

Starward Mode is another fresh addition, which can be found in Memory of Chaos, Pure Fiction, and Apocalyptic Shadow. Starward will see you take on three different stages, which you’ll need three teams for. Clearing each challenge with full stars will reward you 100 Stellar Jades extra per chase.

Sources indicate that there’s more coming down the line, too. A fresh Fate/Stay Night [Unlimited Blade Works] collaboration will arrive in a content up this summer. The event will give players a chance to earn Gilgamesh or Archer for free by logging in.
