💡 Key Takeaways
  • Nvidia's founder and CEO Jensen Huang has resigned from his position as leader of one of the most valuable companies in the world.
  • After days mired in controversy, which began amid reports of Huang's alleged affair with a Chinese spy, Nvidia has announced Huang's resignation as organization president, chief executive officer, and board member, effective immediately.
  • Industry observers note that "Colette has helped lead Nvidia through a period of extraordinary growth and has a deep understanding of our business, customers, operations and financial position," Harvey Jones, chair of Nvidia's board of directors wrote in a statement accompanying the news.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nvidia's founder and CEO Jensen Huang has resigned from his position as leader of one of the most valuable companies in the world.

After days mired in controversy, which began amid reports of Huang's alleged affair with a Chinese spy, Nvidia has announced Huang's resignation as organization president, chief executive officer, and board member, effective immediately. Finance chief Colette Kress will take over as interim CEO and will remain in the position until a permanent CEO is chosen.

Industry observers note that "Colette has helped lead Nvidia through a period of extraordinary growth and has a deep understanding of our business, customers, operations and financial position," Harvey Jones, chair of Nvidia's board of directors wrote in a statement accompanying the news. "She is supported by an experienced leadership team that has been instrumental in executing Nvidia's strategy and advancing its technology roadmap. The Board has full confidence in Colette and the leadership team, and we expect the company's operations, customer commitments and product roadmap to continue without interruption.".

Kress, in the same announcement, says she intends to build on the foundation laid by Huang over the past 33 years, and "continue advancing the work that has made Nvidia a leader in accelerated computing and AI, and execute on the opportunities ahead." Perhaps unsurprisingly, there's no mention of gaming graphics cards in there.

Nvidia's announcement ends by thanking Huang for his time at the organization: "Jensen’s contributions to Nvidia are profound. Nvidia is one of the most consequential technology companies in the world. The Board and the company thank Jensen for his immeasurable contributions to the company and the industry.".

Nvidia's board met on Wednesday to decide whether to remove Huang amid allegations he had participated in a second affair, this time with a subordinate, following reports of his alleged affair with a Chinese spy. That initial incident prompted a organization-wide apology from Huang and an independent investigation exploring whether he'd been the target of a "foreign intelligence effort".

Nvidia will likely remain under increased scrutiny moving forward. There are particular concerns around the company's chips being imported to China despite trade bans.

You'd better get used to seeing GTA 6 break records, because the game's not even out yet in most countries and it's already crushing long-standing numbers.

Indeed, the hype is so colossal that Rockstar's open worlder broke the all-time record for livestream viewers just minutes after its release in regions where it's already the 19th November.

According to Streams Charts' data, GTA 6 has peaked a frankly absurd 7.2 million viewers across streaming platforms Twitch (3.1 million), YouTube (2.7 million), and Kick (1.4 million), and others.

The crazy part is that this figure could well be eclipsed as GTA 6 becomes available in more regions, and more streamers start to broadcast their gameplay.

Team-based shooter Valorant previously held the all-time record, which was set back in 2020, when watching livestreams could net you access to the game's PC beta.

It peaked at 1.7 million viewers, meaning that GTA 6 has absolutely demolished the record — and honestly, it's hard to imagine anything topping it for years and years to come.

According to recent reports, A significant part of the point of The Blood of Dawnwalker is that you're on a fixed time limit. You've got 30 in-game days and nights to try and save your family, and if you don't manage to see everything the game has to offer, well, the game's director is fine with that. But that doesn't matter as much now, as The Blood of Dawnwalker is getting its 1.2 patch next week that adds in a newly introduced game plus mode.

"If you completed the Epilogue, you can dive right back into Vale Sangora with Newly introduced Game+!" a post from the devs explains. "Your level, skills, and inventory will carry over; the level cap will be raised to 100; enemies will be balanced and scale uniformly across all regions; and items will have NG+ versions with updated stats." Sounds like your usual new game plus affair! I suppose it is a good opportunity to try out different things compared to your first playthrough, but I'm not exactly aligned with the idea that the timer restriction is too restricting (as some mods have made clear how others feel that way).

In any case, the update goes a tad further than that. If you got the Eclipse Edition of the game, the in-game soundtrack that came with it "will be extended with additional songs from the game." You can expect the soundtrack on streaming services soon, too. While details are slimmer here, there are also some planned balance changes, like updated enemy health pools and how often they use their abilities during combat, and terrain geometry has seen some improvements to allow for "smoother movement during combat and exploration.".

Overall, a bit of a smaller upgrade compared to the last one, but one I'm sure will be welcome to some all the same. If you've not had a chance to check the game out yet and still feel on the fence about it, here's some lovely words from Mark's review: "There’s always that sense that something vital or unexpected could be lurking around the next corner, to pull you into a quest dripping with depth and intrigue. It works to ensure the more busywork-esque tasks attached to angering Brencis and his Boyars never make Vale Sangora feel home to a string of boring boxes to tick. It’s a vibrant, constantly changing place with a thousand different threads metaphorically criss-crossing just beneath its surface, just as ancient ruins literally criss-cross beneath its swamps, crags, and forests.".

PC Gamer's got your back Our experienced team dedicates many hours to every review, to really get to the heart of what matters most to you. Find out more about how we evaluate games and hardware.

Corsair is continuing the 2026 trend of brands pushing out upcoming and innovative mouse technologies. In this case, it's all in the 'PureVector' part of the name. In partnership with AimLabs, Corsair has made a mouse that can adjust sensitivity in different directions to tailor it to your movements and help you aim better.

That's the claim, anyway. In practice, I've found that PureVector hasn't improved my aim, both subjectively while gaming and objectively based on multiple AimLabs tests. Some pro players that Corsair highlights claim it's helped them, so your mileage may vary.

Apart from PureVector, though, the mouse itself deserves some attention, as it's still a very performant, lightweight mouse for competitive gaming. It has some upgrades compared to its predecessor, the Sabre V2 Pro, too.

✅ You want to try the latest tech: You might get better results than I did with PureVector. It tailors sensor sensitivity in different directions based on how you aim.

❌ You want good value for the basics: If you just want a comfy mouse with solid build quality that performs well, you can find something of better value elsewhere.

Sources indicate that the aim-assisting PureVector technology in this mouse promises a lot, but in my case it fails to deliver, as my aim doesn't improve from turning it on. It's a solid, lightweight, competitive mouse regardless, but it's too expensive for what it is without delivering on the PureVector promise.

Replacement skates, USB-A to USB-C cable, wireless dongle, AimLabs PureVector software integration.

Industry observers note that in most ways, the Sabre V3 Pro PureVector Ergo is your standard competitive gaming mouse: lightweight, few frills, simple design, good sensor. It is lighter than most competitive mice with a solid shell, though a little heavier than its predecessor, the Sabre V2 Pro.

It has been revealed that setting aside the PureVector aiming shenanigans for a moment, probably the biggest improvement compared to the Sabre V2 Pro is its battery life, which has been doubled. Apart from that, you're getting a 42,000 DPI sensor, optical clicks, and some bigger replacement skates included in the box.

In a recent development, now we come to the main attraction: PureVector. Corsair has designed the mouse's internals and firmware to permit different sensitivities in different directions. So, for instance, it can move slightly slower horizontally than vertically.

Sources indicate that corsair has worked with AimLabs to let you test your aiming in the latter software and then have the mouse adjust your directional sensitivity for you. The PureVector software within AimLabs has been made with the help of a bunch of aiming data (over 4 billion data points, apparently) and machine learning. The end result is, in theory, a mouse that can tailor its sensitivity in different directions to stop you over-shooting or under-shooting your target.

The PC Gamer Circuit Breaker newsletter breaks down the latest PC gaming tech, and finds you the best deals on the best products.

Again, in theory, this should also save you time when you aim, and Corsair claims it can save more time than reducing the latency of clicks—the latter is, for example, what we see the Logitech G Pro X2 Superstrike and X3 Superstrike focusing on.

Sources indicate that it's worth noting that Corsair highlights a number of pro players who say they've benefitted from this new tech. However, for my part, I haven't noticed a difference.

Industry observers note that for reference, I play Counter-Strike 2 at about FaceIt Level 7 or Premier 18–20,000 rating (approx. top 15%). I'm far from a pro, but I'm far from the worst. In-game, I didn't notice any difference between my aim with PureVector set up and with it disabled.

I also repeatedly tested my aim in the AimLabs SpiderShot Precision test, and I actually had slightly better results using another mouse without PureVector (the SteelSeries Sensei Pro), and the latter mouse my hand was less familiar with.

Recent findings suggest that more than this, though, I can't help but feel that it's a bit of a band-aid solution to poor aim. If you're overshooting your shots when you aim left, for instance, you could get PureVector to lower your sensitivity in that direction. But why not instead work on training your hand not to overshoot? That way, having good aim won't be dependent on using this one mouse, and you can get used to aiming consistently in different directions.

According to recent reports, pureVector aside, the Sabre V3 Pro performs well. The sensor is great and feels very responsive. Ditto the latest optical mouse clicks. I have no complaints about its performance as a general mouse, I just don't see the use in PureVector myself. Of course, your mileage may vary, as it seems to have for some pro players.

One area where the Sabre V3 Pro does particularly shine, just like the Sabre V2 Pro, is in its light weight. This latest iteration feels even sturdier than the previous one and still manages to be lighter than most competitive gaming mice.

Battery life is a definite selling point of the Sabre V3 Pro PureVector. It's a lot better than I was expecting. The Sabre V2 Pro can only manage about 70 hours at 1 kHz, and this new one doubles that to 140 hours.

Sources indicate that I think Corsair has struck a great balance here, because it's not as light as the V2—which was 36 g—but 41 g is still incredibly light, and I'd much rather have the bigger battery than shave off those few extra grams. You're not getting any fancy wireless charging or hot-swappable batteries here, but 140 hours of battery life is great.

Sources indicate that the Corsair Sabre V3 Pro PureVector Ergo is, as its excruciatingly long name suggests, pretty ergonomic. It's not the biggest ergo mouse I've used—the Zowie EC2-DW and SteelSeries Rival Pro both feel a bit bigger in-hand—but it still feels comfy under my medium-sized palm.

There's also a non-ergo, symmetrical version for the same price, and you can get carbon fiber or magnesium versions for each, if you're willing to spend even more ($200 and $230, respectively).

It has been revealed that I like the lightweight ergonomic version, though. Its slightly smaller size, combined with its light weight, also means holding it in a fingertip or claw grip doesn't feel too bad, which isn't something you can say about many ergonomic mice. Palm grip is still the main intention here, though. Playing Counter-Strike on low sensitivity feels great.

In a recent development, build quality is decent, too, which is a bit of a relief because the previous version, the Sabre V2 Pro, sacrificed some on this front to achieve its 'ultralight' status. There's no creak or flex along the sides, and only a slight bit of flex on the underside. The side buttons feel great, with no pre-travel, and the scroll wheel has well-defined steps.

There is some pre-travel to the left- and right-mouse buttons, however, and they don't feel as satisfying to press as some other mice like the Razer Viper V4 Pro or SteelSeries Rival Pro. They're far from bad, just not quite up to the standard of some other expensive gaming mice I've tried.

The version I've got here, the 'Ergo' one, is pretty plain and looks quite similar to its predecessor, the Sabre V2 Pro. It's plain white, with only some very subtle grey accents. I'm fine with that, as the focus is on performance and comfort.

Any extra aesthetic fancies are likely to add to the weight, which isn't worth the sacrifice for this kind of mouse. As with most ultralight mice, you know what you're getting aesthetically, and it's minimal.

This mouse uses the same software as the previous V2 Pro. What's noteworthy is the software is browser-based—there's no locally-installable app to use. That's mainly because you're expected to just set it and go, without returning to adjust things.

You can set up profiles to toggle between DPI using a mouse button combination, however. And the web software can be used offline if you install it as an app in your browser, so internet outages shouldn't cause any problems.

The web hub is basic but gets the job done. The battery indicator isn't very precise, only showing a tiny icon and no percentage numbers, but that's my only complaint.

According to recent reports, the AimLabs integration is perfectly fine, too. Assuming you've got it installed on Steam, you can allow the web hub to boot it up for you from there, or boot it up yourself. Once in, you can navigate to PureVector and let it run you through the aim training to adjust your sensitivity in different sweep directions. It's intuitive, and the directional charts it shows are clear enough.

At $180/£160, the Sabre V3 Pro PureVector Ergo is an expensive mouse. It joins the likes of the G Pro X2/X3 Superstrike, Viper V4 Pro, DeathAdder V4 Pro, SteelSeries Rival Pro, and other high-end, competitive gaming mice.

It has been revealed that can it compete with these? In my opinion, not quite. These other gaming mice each have extra features and upcoming technologies that go some way towards justifying the very high price tags. The Superstrikes have analogue clicks, the Viper V4 Pro has FrameSync, the Rival Pro has hot-swappable batteries and UWB connectivity.

In a recent development, the DeathAdder V4 Pro doesn't have anything too fancy like that, but is a very solid gaming mouse. I'd class the Sabre V3 Pro PureVector in this category, alongside the DeathAdder. That's because while the PureVector technology is indeed very fresh, I haven't found it to have much of an impact, and so I'm left considering its merits as a general competitive gaming mouse, setting aside this new aim assist tech.

Recent findings suggest that there are merits to it that justify a price tag above $100: light weight, comfy ergonomic shape, optical clicks, responsive scroll wheel, great battery life. But not enough to justify $180—not without something extra, which PureVector promises but, in my case, fails to deliver. Unless, that is, you're set on getting a mouse as light as this one is that still has a sturdy shell.

Industry observers note that you could instead, for instance, go for something like the Mchose K7 V2 Ultra+ for about $90. Or a Pulsar mouse like the Pulsar X2 CrazyLight for $130, which sometimes drops to about $100 on sale.

In a recent development, if you fancy spending the extra to try it out for yourself and see if you can get the kinds of benefits the pros that Corsair highlights espouse, go for it. But for my money, I'd be opting for a cheaper lightweight mouse, or one with better build quality like the Viper V4 Pro.

1. Best wireless: Razer Viper V4 Pro.

Industry observers note that 2. Best wired: Glorious Model O Eternal.

3. Best budget wireless: Mchose G3 V2 Pro.

4. Best competitive:Logitech G Pro X3 Superstrike.

According to recent reports, 5. Best lightweight: Corsair Sabre V2 Pro.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Available June 3 through July 29, the new event allows Monopoly Go players to jump in the world of The Simpsons.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Monopoly Go players have been looking forward to a major crossover event for what felt like months, and though most of the details ended up leaking, nothing actually beats official information.

The world of The Simpsons has officially arrived in Monopoly Go, and there's a whole lot for players to dive into. The show's creative team even produced a latest animated short, featuring Mr. Monopoly, and Mr. Burns.

Available June 3 through July 29, the new event allows Monopoly Go players to jump in the world of The Simpsons. You'll be able to build, and explore all around multiple iconic locations from the show.

Along the way, you'll run into Simpsons characters like Homer, Marge, Bart, Lisa, and of course, Mr. Burns. Developer Scopely teamed up with the show's creative team to create many references, and Easter Eggs for you to discover. You'll find some of those on chance cards, but most of the world has been changed to be part of The Simpsons, including getting to bribe Chief Wiggum to escape jail.

Industry observers note that the developer promises a deeply connected world with Simpsons narratives and characters that alter seasonal maps, and offer unique sticker sets and animated sequences to dive in. Incidentally, this is The Simpsons' first appearance in a mobile-exclusive game in 13 years.

Here's a breakdown of everything you can expect, straight from Scopely:.

Episodes: Narrative-driven encounters that create stories inspired by The Simpsons. Episodes play out across seasonal boards, sticker sets, and minigames, all capped off with an animated short.

Sticker sets: Every Episode comes with its own limited-time sticker set, taking cues from the latest Simpsons story. Collectible artwork, character journeys and other rewards are yours to claim for the duration of each Episode.

The Simpsons Run: Every two weeks, a latest Springfield character will take over the Free Parking tile, kicking off character-driven runs.

Simpsons-themed Shutdowns and Heists: Monopoly Go's shutdowns and heists get a Simpsons makeover, with Springfield-inspired chaos and disasters.

Bribe Wiggum: This changes Go to Jail to allow players to bribe Chief Wiggum, giving you a chance to earn a bigger reward, but not without introducing an element of unpredictability.

Simpsons chance cards: The chance card collection grows with over 50 Simpsons-themed cards full of memes, references and one-liners from the show.

If you're excited to jump in tomorrow, be sure to check out these Free Monopoly Go Dice Links before you dive into the new content.

"This game is the culmination of everything the developer has previously achieved in the open-world space that pushes the genre to heights that, in all likelihood, no other developer will be able to reach. "A game of opposites and awe, minute detail and impossible scale, Rockstar pushes back the horizon of video games once again with GTA 6. An irreducible mix of silliness, intimacy, grand ideas and rock 'n' roll action - and a load more after that.".

"Grand Theft Auto VI delivers a remarkably immersive and ambitious open-world experience, blending thrilling gameplay, diverse activities, and a compelling relationship between Jason and Lucia. 💡 Key Takeaways

  • Earlier this month, developers began complaining about delays to Valve's approval process, which was extending the time it took to get their games published on Steam.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

More indie developers say they've been forced to delay the impending release of their games as a result of Steam's growing approvals backlog - a relatively recent problem that's believed to stem from an influx of AI slop on the platform.

Earlier this month, developers began complaining about delays to Valve's approval process, which was extending the time it took to get their games published on Steam. Valve responded, explaining approval times could now take up to 12 days, due to the number of submissions it was having to re-review. One week on, the situation doesn't seem to have improved.

New turn-based tower defence game Australia Did It: End-of-the-World Railway Defense Business, co-developed by acclaimed indie designer Rami Ismail and Aesthetician Labs, was previously set for release on 10th November. Unfortunately, the game has now been delayed while the wait continues for Valve to review the latest build.

In a recent development, "We're still waiting for Steam to give us the final greenlight and finish their build review process," publisher Mystic Forge wrote on the Steam forums. "We have been stuck waiting for it for a few weeks now and unfortunately we just don't know when they will get around to reviewing it at this point.".

Speaking to Eurogamer, Ismail added that Australia Did It has been in Steam's approval queue for much longer than he's used to: "We've been in the queue since 20th October, failed over a minor controller input issue on 5th November (which we resolved the same day), and we've been waiting again since with no meaningful response from Valve despite follow-ups.".

"I'm used to hold-and-wait patterns on console," Ismail continued, "but Steam has historically been much more snappy - 10-14 days pre-launch was usually enough to fail twice and still ship on time," he added.

It has been revealed that amazing Slot Survivor (A.S.S.), the debut title from TwoMenGames, is facing similar issues, and has had to retract its release date announcement after being stuck in Steam's approval queue. Amazing Slot Survivor, which adds a slot machine spin to the bullet heaven auto-shooting genre, was initially set for release on 13th November.

"Steam's review process for the release is taking longer than we expected," TwoMenGames wrote in a message on Steam. "We know many of you have been counting on the schedule we confirmed earlier, and we are very sorry to bring you this [postponement] news instead of the good news you were hoping for." Amazing Slot Survivor's demo, which was previously set to disappear with the game's full release, has returned to Steam until the developer introduces a latest launch date.

These are far from the only examples, and a cursory look on social media reveals many more indie games are affected by the problem, including the likes of Bottled by Bears, and Food Devils.

Sources indicate that valve recently attempted to address the delays its facing by introducing stricter submission guidelines designed to stop the lowest-effort games, such as those vibe-coded entirely with gen-AI, from joining its approval queue. However, Ismail doesn't think that's good enough.

Industry observers note that "I am concerned that Valve trying to avoid taking a political position on AI is forcing them into choices that will inevitably be worse for developers," he told Eurogamer. "If sloppers can submit several game clones a day through automated systems, the only way for Valve to stem the tide of games damaging genuine developers' work is to put constraints on game distribution, increase fees, or make the process more complicated.

"In the 'open market' Valve seems to so adore, they're going to be the ones carrying the costs for moderation, so I don't think they'll like the open market on this - but there's no outcome of this that allows Valve neutrality on AI and not do things that will ultimately make life worse for genuine developers," he added.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Years after we said goodbye to Katniss Everdeen and Peeta Mellark, they return for another surprise appearance in The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping.

Once again, Jennifer Lawrence and Josh Hutcherson return as the District 12 victors – and they're not alone, either, with Woody Harrelson also returning as Haymitch Abernathy.

"The energy was great. It was great to have the three of them back," Francis Lawrence, who has directed five out of six Hunger Games movies, tells us when we meet with him in London to discuss the film. "I've done four movies with Jen, and so we remain in touch as with Josh and Woody, and they stay in touch, and so it's not like we haven't seen each other in years and years and years or anything.

"But I think to reunite as a whole for the purpose of making something that's Hunger Games related was really special," he continues. "We're a bit of a family, everybody that makes these movies, and that's crew included. And so, when Jen and Josh and Woody all came in, they landed in Germany, and I remember getting a text from Jen that she and Josh were in the bar having a beer, and I was wrapping. And so, I came in, and Nina [Jacobson, producer] came in, and the DP came in, and this camera operator came in, and our sound guy, and our stills guy, and suddenly there's 40 people who have been making these movies together for years, and that reunion I think was really the special part. A shoot day is a shoot day, and it was nice to do, but I think just having everybody in that whole family that's been there – at least with me since 2012 – together, having a drink before the shoot was really fun.".

Sunrise on the Reaping also introduces some newcomers to the franchise, including McKenna Grace as District 12 tribute Maysilee Donner, Joseph Zada as a younger version of Haymitch, and Whitney Peak as Haymitch's Covey girlfriend Lenore Dove Baird.

According to recent reports, "I was so giddy. I was really giddy," Peak indicates of her reaction to the return of Lawrence, Hutcherson, and Harrelson.

In a recent development, though the return was confirmed by Lawrence before the film was released, there was an attempt at keeping the trio's presence secret on set. Industry observers note that earlier this year in a bit of a shakeup for the fleshiest kid in town, Super Meat Boy entered into a fresh dimension in the aptly named Super Meat Boy 3D. I've not played it but it seems like a good take on the format. Clearly, though, sometimes you just need to play the hits, as a new release of the original game is on the way in the form of Super Meat Boy Again+, a remaster with updated graphics, levels and plenty more.

What is there is very clearly Super Meat Boy, uh, again, just with a massive new lick of paint. There is probably some kind of joke to be made about it being DLSS yassified, but I'm too tired to think of one, so, you get the point. But it does look pretty good! I do kind of miss the Flash game aesthetic, I think there's a real charm to the sort of visual design sensibilities you'd find from that era, but this remaster certainly ain't ugly at least. Apparently it's not just the art that's new, as there's also new music, cutscenes, secrets and "stuff.".

In a recent development, if the animated sequences featured in the trailer, which you can have a gander at above, are included in the final game that'll be a treat to watch too, as I think they better capture the Newgrounds pseudo sub-genre of animation than the graphical overhaul. It sounds like they will be looking at the Steam page, so, a treat to look forward to while committing an act of masochism by playing it!

There's no release date attached to this remaster, so we'll all just have to sit tight for an update there. The original is still listed on Steam, but if you fancy as major a dose of nostalgia as the trailer is trying to present to you, you could always go play the original, plain old regular Meat Boy. It's playable right on Newgrounds thanks to the Flash emulator Ruffle and works like a dream! Or if you're happy to wait, you could always wishlist the new one on Steam.

Guide: GTA 6: Tips & Tricks You Need to Know

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that GTA 6's vast open world is begging to be explored, but before you sink your teeth into Leonida, there are a handful of tips and tricks you should know.
  • Below are 12 spoiler-free GTA 6 tips and tricks that will improve your life in Leonida:.
  • GTA 6 doesn't have traditional difficulty options like other games, but there are a couple of ways you can make Leonida more manageable.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that GTA 6's vast open world is begging to be explored, but before you sink your teeth into Leonida, there are a handful of tips and tricks you should know. This spoiler-free GTA 6 guide includes info on a dozen key features and mechanics that will help you make the best start to your life in Vice City.

Below are 12 spoiler-free GTA 6 tips and tricks that will improve your life in Leonida:.

GTA 6 doesn't have traditional difficulty options like other games, but there are a couple of ways you can make Leonida more manageable.

Press Options and select Settings > Gameplay. Scroll to the bottom (options 24 and 25) and you can choose to enable Accessible Combat and Reduced Vehicle Damage, as shown:.

Accessible Combat will both reduce the damage you take in gunfights, while increasing the damage enemies receive, making firefights much more manageable.

It has been revealed that reduced Vehicle Damage, meanwhile, will reduce the damage your car takes when in crashes or combat. This means there's less chance of your car becoming difficult to control or exploding.

According to recent reports, the game will warn you that enabling these "changes the balance and experience of gameplay", meaning your experience will be a lot easier. Using them does not alter the story or disable Trophies, however.

GTA 6 has a new control scheme which modernises its gameplay by mapping run to L3 and jump to Cross/X.

For those of you who've spent over a decade playing GTA 5 and GTA Online, however, you may prefer to use Rockstar's more traditional control scheme.

Fortunately, this is relatively easy to enable.

Press Options and select Settings > Control Scheme, as pictured:.

The control scheme will automatically be set to the new Default layout, but you can toggle to Classic if you prefer the GTA 5 approach.

As its name implies, GTA 6 is all about grand theft auto — or, in other words, stealing cars.

Most vehicles you find parked around Vice City will be locked, but it is possible to steal them quicker with a very simple tip.

When the minigame for any criminal activities appear — like using your Slim Jim, Clone Key, or even hotwiring a car — there's a pink "sweet spot" you can find to speed up the action:.

This makes it quicker to break in and make a quick getaway.

Just move the sticks around to find the right spot, and use those extra seconds wisely to escape swiftly:.

According to recent reports, GTA 6 has a living, breathing open world that encourages exploration. If you take the time to look around, you'll almost certainly discover something to do.

However, if you want to continue with the story and you're not sure what to do next, there's a way to easily see your next objective or story mission.

Press the Touch Pad to open your map and then using the index on the left of the screen, press Right to see a list of available story missions, with mandatory objectives at the top and optional ones listed below:.

You can immediately set a waypoint to any mission with Cross/X.

There is no traditional fast travel in GTA 6, but there is a way you can get around the map rapidly for a nominal fee.

Bring up your smartphone by pressing Up and select RydeMe:.

You'll need to have an active waypoint, which you can choose from within the app or by picking one in advance via your map with Touch Pad.

You'll be notified a driver is on the way and you'll be able to see them from your minimap:.

Once you get in your Ryde, hold L2 to focus on your driver. You can then hold Triangle to skip your journey for $100 and immediately arrive at your destination:.

Longer journeys will cost more than shorter ones, but fast travelling this way is relatively inexpensive overall.

According to recent reports, there are two types of money in GTA 6: cash stored in your wallet and money protected in your BuckMe bank. The latter will unlock as part of Chapter 1.

You can see both types of money at any time by pushing Down:.

Money stored in your wallet will be lost if you're Busted or Wasted during gameplay, so it's really important you put this in your BuckMe bank.

The easiest way to do this is press Up to access your smartphone and select BuckMe > ATM Finder:.

In a recent development, this will automatically select a waypoint to the nearest ATM machine. Follow it and deposit any funds in your wallet into your BuckMe bank, where it'll be safe even if you get arrested or die:.

Throughout GTA 6, Jason and Lucia will build a criminal profile which can affect how NPCs and the wider world of Leonida responds to you.

Recent findings suggest that murdering enemies will contribute towards a more aggressive criminal profile. As such, you may want to consider a non-lethal approach.

One way to do this is by favouring stealth and grabbing enemies with R2, so you can cleanly knock them out without killing them:.

Another option, if you get caught up in a gunfight, is to target non-vitals like kneecaps and arms.

You can easily see non-vitals by pressing L3 and R3 and aiming at yellow parts of the body:.

You'll know an enemy has been debilitated without killing them if a yellow X appears in your weapon's reticule. A red X will appear if your target has been murdered.

If you need to set a quick waypoint to an crucial location in GTA 6, you don't necessarily need to press Touch Pad to bring up your map.

Instead, hold Down and you'll get an alternative in-game view of any nearby shops, waypoints, or story missions:.

You can highlight any of these and press R3 to automatically set a GPS route to where you want to go.

There'll be times in GTA 6 when you're separated from your car and you want to spawn it nearby.

You can do this by opening your smartphone with Up and selecting the Scooter Bros app:.

Select which car you want to use from the app and you'll be charged a fee depending on the delivery distance and your car's current condition:.

Your car will then automatically spawn in a nearby location, marked on your minimap:.

Stealing or entering a car in GTA 6 does not mean you'll have access to it forever.

You'll need to park it in a Parking Space or Garage to temporarily store it, and register it at a Pay 'N' Spray to keep it forever.

Find a car you want to keep and set a waypoint for a Pay 'N' Spray, like with this Emperor Sultan I just stole:.

It has been revealed that drive into the Pay 'N' Spray and select Register to swap the plates. The fee commanded will depend on the value of the car:.

Note that you will need free Stored Vehicle slots to register your car. You can sell previous cars directly at the Pay 'N' Spray:.

Alternatively, you can press Up to open your smartphone and select Vice City Real Estate. This will let you buy more garages for additional Parking Spots:.

This feature becomes available during a story mission, so you may not immediately have access to it if you're still early in the campaign.

Generic upgrades are available for all vehicles at any Mod Shop, but if you want specialist tunings you need to go to the right shop.

These are marked with a blue Wrench icon.

Press Up to open your map and then Right to open the map index.

Select Vehicles > Mod Shops and look for a Mod Shop with a blue Wrench icon, as shown:.

Set a waypoint for the appropriate Mod Shop and you'll find all of the customisations and specialised upgrades available for your current vehicle.

Just like in real-life, staying on top of your smartphone notifications in GTA 6 can be time consuming.

Fortunately, the game will mark important messages for you in the Reminders tab:.

Press Up to bring up your smartphone and then press Square to access your Reminders.

Here you'll find a curated list of key messages, including in-game news articles and NPCs who are waiting for your replies:.

Hopefully you've learned a thing or two with this spoiler-free GTA 6 walkthrough and collectibles guide. Are there any other tips and tricks you think the world should know? Share them in the comments section below.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that world of Warcraft: Forever players are having a blast in the new MMO, but not everyone is basking in the rays of its successful launch.
  • But it's not that too much time behind the computer is keeping WoW players on the other side of the globe away from their precious Vitamin D.
  • World of Warcraft: Forever, if you didn't already known, has a lovely in-game day/night cycle that aligns with your server clock rather than your local time.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that world of Warcraft: Forever players are having a blast in the new MMO, but not everyone is basking in the rays of its successful launch. Players located in Australia, New Zealand, and other Oceania countries are having a bit of a sunlight problem.

But it's not that too much time behind the computer is keeping WoW players on the other side of the globe away from their precious Vitamin D. Rather, it's in-game sunlight that's scarce for our Oceania friends.

World of Warcraft: Forever, if you didn't already known, has a lovely in-game day/night cycle that aligns with your server clock rather than your local time. So, for a British player, the server time is one hour ahead of GMT. That means if I play during the day I see the sun hanging over Azeroth, and if I do a late night MMO session it's replaced by the moon.

However, while Oceania players can access a data centre in Australia that allows for a solid connection to WoW, they still share the same mega-servers with North Americans. That mega-server is aligned with North American time, differing drastically from Oceania time zones. In other words, for World of Warcraft: Forever players in Oceania, day is night and night is day. And they've had enough!

Reddit user Playful_Artichoke981 has been at the forefront of requests asking Blizzard to address the problem , though they're far from alone. At the moment, Oceania players see full daylight in-game from around midnight to 6am in the morning, which obviously is far from normal gaming hours for the majority of players in the region.

Recent findings suggest that "We don't hate the nighttime. We just want variety," writes Playful_Artichoke981. "We don't want to have to compromise our sleep schedules to experience this game in all its glory." Another user, cuddlegoop, echoes the sentiment: "I am totally fine with my day/night changing when I join an NA party. Just let me see the sun! I was up late last night and the view over the bay at Shadowfan Keep in the dawn was so beautiful I want to see stuff like that more often.".

Eurogamer has contacted Blizzard to ask if it has plans to address the matter, but we've not received a response at the time of writing.

World of Warcraft: Forever is proving exceptionally popular, breaking records as the biggest launch in the series' history. And based on what I've played this week, it's looking to be a brilliant MMO that's well worth jumping into, if you have the time.

I just found a curious artifact of the Old West in GTA 6, and the best part is I stumbled across it completely by accident.

That's right, partner: Arthur Morgan's cowboy hat is in Grand Theft Auto 6, and you won't find it in some trendy Western fashion shop or in a McMansion as part of a wealthy crypto bro's collection.

If you want to wear it yourself, I'll tell you below where you can find it.

I was out in Port Gellhorn looking for a particular kind of car for reasons completely unrelated to clothing accessories. While I was driving, I spotted a sign on the side of the road with a balloon tied to it, reading "Yard Sale" with an arrow pointing down the road.

I followed the sign which led to more yard sale signs and, yup, sure enough, the signs pointed me to an actual yard sale. And among the items for sale was a very familiar-looking hat.

It's called a "Genuine Cowboy Hat" and, this being a yard sale, it only cost $5. But I knew the second I saw it that this was no ordinary cowboy hat. Here, have a look at it from the back.

It has been revealed that yep. No mistaking that. I even got a little pang of sadness thinking about good ol' Arthur Morgan. I miss him. Maybe when I'm done with GTA 6, I'll strap on my spurs and take another ride through Red Dead Redemption 2.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

Directions: Head to Port Gellhorn. It's in Kelly County on the western side of the state along the coast. In the southern tip of Port Gellhorn, there's a small neighborhood of about five houses just northwest of the Dirt Merchants mod shop.

Look for the driveway filled with yard sale clutter: furniture and electronics and such. There's a bunch of balloons, a cut-out of a nearly naked cowboy, and a significant American flag flying. You'll find the hat toward the back sitting on top of a guitar case on a couch. There's also a shirt, a cap, and some shoes for sale that definitely didn't belong to Arthur.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Xbox leader Asha Sharma has alluded to harnessing the power of generative AI when making games, in a memo published this afternoon.
  • Recent findings suggest that the memo, titled 25 years of Xbox, charts the growth of Microsoft from small beginnings through to the thousands-strong company it is today.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Xbox leader Asha Sharma has alluded to harnessing the power of generative AI when making games, in a memo published this afternoon.

Recent findings suggest that the memo, titled 25 years of Xbox, charts the growth of Microsoft from small beginnings through to the thousands-strong company it is today. But it's Sharma's comments at the end of the memo that are of particular interest.

According to recent reports, while talking about what the next 25 years could bring, Sharma lamented that "too many ideas never become games" and that "too many games fall short of what their creators imagined". "For decades, this has been the unavoidable tradeoff of ambition," she wrote. "We must change this.".

In a recent development, sharma continued: "Throughout human history, the scale of what we could create was determined by the people, capital, and resources we could command. That relationship is beginning to break. A single person will soon be able to wield capabilities that once required entire nations. A small team will be able to build worlds that today demand hundreds of developers and hundreds of millions of dollars. And our largest studios will be able to pursue ambitions as far beyond today's games as Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 is from its first entry in 1982.".

Sources indicate that there is no explicit mention of generative AI here, but the language is suggestive - "a single person will soon be able to wield capabilities that once required entire nations". Furthermore, Asha's memo follows last month's announcement of an Xbox Labs initiative that also sounded like it was based around generative AI, despite avoiding the phrase specifically.

This isn't a surprise, of course. Microsoft as a wider manufacturer is all-in on generative AI, with Copilot, and Sharma's background at Microsoft is in AI. But it's an area she's avoided speaking too enthusiastically about since her hiring as Xbox boss earlier this year. At the time, Sharma remarked she has "no tolerance for bad AI", and there's been such a lot else going on in the months since - including wide-ranging restructuring resulting in the loss of thousands of Xbox jobs - that the topic of generative AI has fallen into the background. Perhaps now we're seeing the sprouting seeds of it.

We've asked Microsoft for clarification.

When you think about GTA as a series, the first thing that probably comes to mind is driving through crowds of people, gunning down whoever you like, just generally doing crime without any care in the world. I wouldn't exactly call it an empathy game, not to say that other games are any better at such a thing anyway. But with GTA 6 out, crikey, next bloody week, a new interview has gone up with co-studio head Rob Nelson where he shared that you have a bit more space to be empathetic compared to previous entries.

"Crime is a fundamental part of GTA - at least up until now, it has been," Nelson told The Guardian (via @GameRoll_, ta IGN) in a fresh interview. "We're trying to make sure we're not punishing people for playing the game they are used to … [but] your actions will have some effect on how the game plays out." When asked about whether this will be the first GTA game to encourage people to be empathetic, Nelson responded, "I would say so. I would say that it's a product of the story we're trying to tell. We've tried for the first time in a GTA to provide mechanisms that encourage it, for those who want to.".

I am deeply curious as to what those mechanics may be, given that most of what we've seen so far is pretty relegated to shootin', lootin' and a bit of smoochin'. If you steal a car, is there an NPC that loses their job because of it? Can you repair the harm you caused through that action? I'm sure hardly anyone else that's vibrating through their skin in excitement for almost having the game in their fingertips will be asking such questions, I'm just often wary of empathy mechanics in games.

It has been revealed that in any case, doesn't matter all that much for us PC lot just yet, especially because Rockstar are preparing themselves both legally and technically to tackle pirated copies of the game. Rockstar will obviously be quite busy at the moment too, not just because of that whole launching a game thing, but because UK-based workers will be voting to unionise as we speak. If formed, it could be 1600 members strong, which would make it the biggest games union in the UK. Solidarity with all the workers as the voting process continues. I hope you get the result you deserve.

Feature: 10 Features That Surprised Me While Playing GTA 6 On Xbox Series X

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1199 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Purexbox

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By now, you've hopefully had a chance to check out our review of GTA 6 for Xbox Series X elsewhere on Pure Xbox, and it exists because Rockstar gave us multiple weeks' worth of early access to the game ahead of release.
  • I was the lucky person to take on the review responsibility for the latest Grand Theft Auto, and I've put basically all of my free time into it since late October.
  • It has been revealed that some of these were already known prior to today, whereas others might be brand-new information.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By now, you've hopefully had a chance to check out our review of GTA 6 for Xbox Series X elsewhere on Pure Xbox, and it exists because Rockstar gave us multiple weeks' worth of early access to the game ahead of release.

I was the lucky person to take on the review responsibility for the latest Grand Theft Auto, and I've put basically all of my free time into it since late October. While completing the campaign, I inevitibly came across loads of features that surprised me along the way, so I thought I'd use this opportunity to just highlight a few of them.

It has been revealed that some of these were already known prior to today, whereas others might be brand-new information. In any case, here are the specific features (avoiding story spoilers) that surprised me as I was completing GTA 6 on Xbox Series X:.

Yeah, there's finally a fuel requirement in a GTA game! It's not too invasive, so don't worry, but if you happen to drive a car around the map for an extensive amount of time, you'll be forced to find a gas station and refuel it (a very short cutscene and a press of the RT button). You can also repair your car at gas stations as well, which certainly comes in handy if you've been smashing it around at high speeds!

You can still break into vehicles the old fashioned way - either stealing it mid-drive or smashing a window to gain access - but you can also use a slim-jim to break the lock, or eventually a key cloner to bypass the security entirely. Be aware of vehicles with trackers though, as if you end up going too slow, the tracker will alert the cops to your location.

It's not always enough to escape the cops and stay hidden from them for an extended period of time. If you really want to ensure you'll lose their attention, you'll want to either ditch the car or take it to a "Pay 'n' Spray" outlet, as well as change your outfit. It's possible to partially do this by throwing on some sunglasses and a hat, but the clever move is to stash one or more outfits in your car's trunk that you can switch between at a moment's notice.

It has been revealed that while it's impossible to avoid situations in GTA 6 where you'll be engaging in all sorts of criminal activity, you can handle them in various ways. For example, a mission that requires you to take out a bunch of people can be completed by one-shotting them all, but this will raise your criminal profile. Alternatively, leaving your enemies injured but still alive will push you more towards a "Professional" profile. I haven't properly been able to compare how this affects the game yet (I really need to experiment with both sides of the extreme rather than hovering towards the middle), but Rockstar says it alters how the story, world and Jason / Lucia react to you.

Recent findings suggest that I always love when games get creative with music - South of Midnight was one that really impressed me - and GTA 6 is now one of the best examples I can think of. Basically, you get highly-curated pumping tunes playing in the background during things like shootouts and getaways, while more menacing situations can feature a different vibe of soundtrack, sometimes even with lyrics. You might not quite understand the appeal until you play it, but it's actually one of my favourite new features. The use of music in certain cutscenes is awesome as well.

I don't know if I can verify this yet for sure, but the radio stations either appear to change their music selection based on where you are on the map, or based on how far you've progressed into the story. As I spent more time in Vice City, I started to notice a much bigger range of songs on the Flash FM channel (my favourite) including everyone from Coldplay to The Ting Tings, whereas those tunes never popped up at the start. Try it for yourself and let me know if I'm right about this!

It has been revealed that any GTA game worth its salt has to come with a whole bunch of minigames, and my favourite so far is the addition of minigolf. I believe there are three 18-hole courses dotted around the map in total, and they're beautifully detailed and themed, with genuinely enjoyable holes to play on. There's actual golf as well, but I have to admit I haven't had chance to check it out yet. Pool in the bars is great fun too!

If you really take your time to play through GTA 6, which I highly recommend you do, you'll truly be able to appreciate just how much effort has gone into some of the seemingly smallest aspects of it. Snapmatic, which is the social media platform on your in-game phone, is constantly being updated with new statuses, photos, videos, comments and more, and you could literally just sit just browsing it for ages and enjoying the interactions. There's also a "News" app that regularly gets updated with fresh articles about what's going on in Leonida.

Industry observers note that when you get to a certain mission in GTA 6, you'll be introduced to your first video game inside the game itself, which seems to be a very high-brow parody of modern-day indie hits. There are actually multiple games you can play, including one that's very reminiscent of Xbox title Yet Another Zombie Survivors, and these can either be accessed by turning on your TV or going up to arcade cabinets located in various stores all over the map.

When GTA 5 came out for Xbox 360 back in 2013, one of the major things I can recall is how slow the initial loading screens would be, especially once GTA Online got involved. We obviously haven't got an online component to GTA 6 just yet, but in terms of loading up the single-player game on Xbox Series X, it's actually a very quick process that isn't painful whatsoever. You barely even notice it!

Of course, these aren't the only surprising features you'll run into while playing GTA 6 - there are literally hundreds and hundreds that are waiting to be discovered. I don't want to spoil anything about the story or the details of the missions themselves though, and ultimately this is a game where surprises will continue being revealed long into the future.

According to recent reports, for now, just go and enjoy it on your Xbox Series X or Xbox Series S (or PS5), and I urge you to take your time and really let it all soak in. One of the perils of reviewing games is that you have to grind to the finish line, and while that does still give you a great impression of the experience, I already can't wait to go back and spend 100+ hours with it this time.

Anything here sound particularly enticing to you? Let us know down in the comments section below.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Last night, Xbox Game Studios and Halo Studios have declared a free revision for the recently-released Halo: Campaign Evolved, which promises to add the four-player co-operative PvE mode, Firefight, to the game.

It has been revealed that "For nearly two decades, Firefight has been a Halo favorite, challenging Spartans to team up, hold the line, and survive wave after wave of enemies," says Halo Studios director of competitive engagement Tahir Hasangjekaj stated in a dedicated post on the Xbox website. "The tradition continues this winter as we add the four-player cooperative PvE mode to Halo: Campaign Evolved in a free upgrade.".

Sources indicate that though we don't have a release date for the revision yet, Hasangjekaj does explicitly state "this Winter" as a window, and promises that we'll hear more information about the update at Halo Fest - due to run from 12th to 13hth December in Seattle, Washington. My money would be on a release around then, therefore.

"We're kicking things off tonight at Xbox FanFest, where attendees will be the first to jump in and experience Firefight across newly introduced maps and armed with plenty of weapons to help even the odds." It seems there's already a playable build of the mode, then.

It has been revealed that it's worth noting that this is quite an odd news blast from Xbox, since the last official information we heard about the Halo brand was that the next major Halo game being developed by Activision, as Halo Studios all but closes as part of Microsoft's Xbox 'restructuring' that saw one key member behind Halo: Campaign Evolved promoted and laid off within the same week. As things stand, we don't know anything specific about the future of the series, but there are plenty of rumours that the next title will be a reboot developed by Call of Duty's Sledgehammer Games.

It's been fairly busy 24 hours for Xbox: as well as this Halo enhancement, we've heard from Asha Sharma as she celebrated the 25th anniversary of Xbox by seemingly going all-in on Gen AI. Elsewhere, we got the announcement that Wolfenstein 3 is in development over at MachineGames, headed up by Hugo Martin.

Toby Fox, the creator of Deltarune (and Undertale), has this week released his 'Fall 2026' newsletter, giving fans a "status update" on Chapter 6...and Chapter 7.

Firstly, Chapter 6 is "progressing well", and the game is now a "structurally complete draft" that can be played from start to finish. In saying this, it will still take a "bit longer" to finish up some other scenes and details:.

"Much of the game looks complete… but, some vital scenes and details are still undercooked in their presentation, so it's going to take a bit longer before we can really move to full-on testing.

It has been revealed that and if this wasn't already enough, there's the Chapter 7 development enhancement. The team has "only just started", and Fox has read out some of the events and dialogue to the team, but is withholding the rest of the story until they "complete more of the game".

Sources indicate that I read out the events and dialogue of Chapter 7 to the team. However, just when the story reached a critical moment, I stopped reading… I told my team they need to complete more of the game before I tell them what happens.

Everyone agrees it's more fun this way.

Team members who completed their work on Chapter 6 have moved onto Chapter 7 now. Unlike every other Chapter, I actually feel like I know what I'm doing this time, so I have a lot of confidence...!

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The idea of Dark Souls PvP has always scared me a tad.
  • To say that it is just straight up Dark Souls combat would be unfair, from the looks of things.
  • Sources indicate that you can take part in matches with up to eight people, which presumably extends to AI (not that kind) enemies too, in "atmospheric duels, clashes, deathmatches and more." It looks neat!

The idea of Dark Souls PvP has always scared me a tad. You can replace Dark Souls with Bloodborne or Elden Ring, I've typically just been a coward when it comes to the idea of fighting another, real person. They're probably going to be better than me! I don't use tactics in Souls games, I use brute force until I get my way! That being mentioned, I do have to admit I quite like the look of Rasen, a game that is essentially just the PvP component of Dark Souls (or PvE if you just want to take on some computer-controlled enemies) that just introduced into early access.

To say that it is just straight up Dark Souls combat would be unfair, from the looks of things. For one, it looks more like it leans a tad towards Sekiro with a blades-only kind of affair, whether that be massive or small. And blades a plenty they have, ranging from your classic sword, to scythes, to halberds and all sorts. It's a much flashier looking affair too, with fancy slashing effects that seem to buff moves and a pace that seems much faster than Souls games tend to be.

Sources indicate that you can take part in matches with up to eight people, which presumably extends to AI (not that kind) enemies too, in "atmospheric duels, clashes, deathmatches and more." It looks neat! And best of all, unusually for a 3D arena fighter, it has rollback netcode. For those unfamiliar, and to try and explain it simply, this is essentially a bit of tech you'll find in predominantly 2D fighting games that predicts every possible input you could make in a given moment, helping to reduce lag time and allow for tighter matches (and less rage quitting).

That's a bit harder to do in a 3D environment given that you have a lot more options at your disposal when it comes to movement, so if it works that's some impressive stuff! And we could all quite easily find out together, as a demo for Rasen is available to try out. Or, alternatively, you can just pick it up whole hog on Steam right now, as it's available in early access.

If you're one of the countless millions contributing to the collective endangering of global productivity by enjoying Grand Theft Auto 6 at launch, you might have paused in the middle of blatantly disregarding traffic laws to wonder: Wait a second, am I hearing "Weird Al" Yankovic hosting this pretend radio station?

Industry observers note that and yes, you are: In a Bluesky post earlier today, the beloved comedic musician and polka maestro confirmed that he offered his voice for DJ Al, who hosts '80s music station Vice City FM alongside Swedish actress, model, and singer Brigitte Nielsen. Their contributions were then double-confirmed by the full GTA 6 credits, which Rockstar published once launch time hit.

Sources indicate that I’m the host of GTA 6’s “non-stop ‘80s” radio channel Vice City FM. I also wrote some in-game commercials, and I’m the voice of the Burger Shot ads as well! As a long-time fan of the Grand Theft Auto franchise, I couldn’t be more excited about this. Okay, gotta get back to playing the game!

In a recent development, "I’m the host of GTA 6’s 'non-stop ‘80s' radio channel Vice City FM. I also wrote some in-game commercials, and I’m the voice of the Burger Shot ads as well!" Yankovic mentioned. "As a long-time fan of the Grand Theft Auto franchise, I couldn’t be more excited about this. Okay, gotta get back to playing the game!".

Somewhere out there, Weird Al is securing the love of his virtual latina wife, and I think that's beautiful.

Industry observers note that yankovic is just one of countless recognizable names you'll find if you scroll down the GTA 6 credits. Among the core cast, SNL alumnus Bobby Moynihan voices Cal, Jason's bumbling, conspiracy-brained buddy. The pair's criminal boss man, Brian Heder, is performed by legendary Stephen Root—who you'll likely recognize as Bill Dauterive on King of the Hill, Milton in Office Space, and all kinds of magnificent weirdos across the Coen brothers filmography.

But it's the radio talent where GTA 6's credits get particularly wild. It's a cavalcade of international music icons, comedians, and film figures. While driving around GTA 6, you might hear Lana Del Rey hosting Back Country Radio, or Latin music phenom Bad Bunny on Cocoteo FM. On Dirty South Classics, there's Trina, Trick Daddy, and Gucci Mane. Pop station Flash FM is helmed by Robyn and Alex Consani—the first transgender model to win Model of the Year at the British Fashion Awards and celebrated TikTok goofball. Keith Richards is in there. I didn't even know he was still capable of speech.

On talk radio, you can hear Ted Lasso's Jason Sudeikis, Abbot Elementary's Janelle James, and John Leguizamo of being John Leguizamo fame. Stavros Halkias is on there doing a Conservative talk radio bit. But maybe the most compelling inclusion, for me, is that Kaleidoscope FM is hosted by Jeremy Irons. The Academy Award-winning actor. You were in Kafka, Jeremy. How'd you end up in cyber-Florida?

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I've accepted that Arnold Schwarzenegger can probably do things at 79 that would put me in physical therapy. Still, watching him take time from his busy 2026 movie schedule to hoist an enormous Christmas tree overhead while dressed as Santa Claus made me do a double take. The moment comes from a fresh Santa Schwarzenegger holiday ad, which follows the action icon through New York City in a Santa suit as he dodges the paparazzi. Somehow, he winds up helping a family load a tree onto their car. I suspect some movie magic made that lift possible, but seeing Arnold casually handle an entire evergreen is pretty funny. It also has me wondering: What's it like doing stunts at his age?

It has been revealed that the Santa clip landed on Arnold's Instagram just days after the former governor got candid about what action scenes feel like at his age. During his November 11 appearance on Jimmy Kimmel Live!, Schwarzenegger discussed the possibility of returning to Predator, Commando, and Conan the Barbarian. Kimmel brought up King Conan, which would follow his famous warrior as an older ruler whose reign is threatened. When the conversation turned to the demands of filming that kind of movie, Arnold admitted the years have made a difference:.

Industry observers note that I tell you one thing, to do all this action and the sword fighting and horseback riding, and all this stuff is not as easy anymore today than it was 40 years ago…. Well, you get older and you slow down a little bit, right?

Four decades ago, Schwarzenegger swung swords and ran through jungles. I'd imagine climbing onto a horse in full costume feels a little different at 79. Of course, he wasn't about to let a serious observation about aging ruin a perfectly good joke. He rapidly followed up with a line that had me laughing:.

It has been revealed that no, not very much. But still, I'm now at an age where it takes me an hour and a half to watch 60 Minutes. Unbelievable, I think. Things are really slowing down.

That's a pretty fantastic old-man joke. The timing is even better when you remember this is the same guy at the moment showing up in Amazon’s holiday commercial looking capable of bench-pressing a Christmas tree. Kimmel also commented on how muscular Schwarzenegger still is, which led to some playful back-and-forth between the two. Even the Terminator is still perfectly comfortable being the butt of his own jokes.

A post shared by Arnold Schwarzenegger (@schwarzenegger).

It has been revealed that schwarzenegger isn't pretending he can simply pick up where he left off in 1986, either. He's spoken about how a potential King Conan would acknowledge the character's age, with Conan having spent decades on the throne before facing a threat to his kingdom. That's an idea I can get behind. CinemaBlend has already covered his updates about possible Predator and Commando sequels, although he told Kimmel he was still waiting to see finalized scripts.

According to recent reports, meanwhile, the Christmas tree is a nice bit of promotion for The Man with the Bag, Schwarzenegger's newly introduced Prime Video holiday movie with Reacher star Alan Ritchson and Awkwafina. In it, he plays Santa, who recruits a thief to recover his stolen bag of presents. The film arrives December 2 for anyone with a Prime Video subscription, marking his return to Christmas comedy 30 years after Jingle All the Way.

Industry observers note that as for that tree lift, I'd love to see some behind-the-scenes footage before giving Arnold full credit for the feat. But the man seems to be having a blast playing Santa, and I hope he keeps finding excuses to do action scenes. Maybe someone can make him a really comfortable saddle for King Conan.

GTA 6 is a single player game, but Sony’s servers are taking a hammering as the game goes online around the world.

While you can’t play Rockstar’s latest with other people, you will need to verify your digital license once the title is available in your region – a timely reminder of the digital era we’re all now living in.

As the game has released in New Zealand, Australia, and parts of Asia, the PSN servers have held up sturdily – but there have been sporadic reports of outages over the past few hours, as Europe and the UK prepares to play.

We’ll continue to monitor the situation as GTA 6’s all-crucial American launch nears, but fingers crossed there are no issues and the launch goes flawlessly.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As Grand Theft Auto 6 breaks pre-order records on the PlayStation and Xbox stores, and looks poised to break many more sales records once it releases next week, questions of whether it will also break the internet arise. Collective network load will undoubtedly spike around its release - will regional infrastructure be able to bear it?

Major game releases register nationally for broadband use: we know this from an investigation into gaming downloads and how much they cost the environment we published in 2021. We also know that UK communications regulator Ofcom negotiates with gaming companies to try and avoid major game rolls out happening alongside major cultural occasions, such as sporting events, which are likely to spike broadband use. The network pipes can be clogged, and there's arguably never been a game as anticipated as GTA 6 to clog them.

Recent findings suggest that for this reason, Openreach - the organization that runs the largest broadband network in the UK - has been tracking Rockstar's latest game closely. "GTA 6 has been on our radar for a long time," Trevor Linney, Openreach's director for network technology, told Eurogamer. "We know from games like Fortnite and Call of Duty that a major release or revision can drive huge amounts of data across the network, so it'll be fascinating to see just how much GTA moves the needle. Our network and teams are ready, and GTA 6 is certainly one we'll be watching for a new download record.".

According to recent reports, A spokesperson for Ofcom, meanwhile, mentioned: "Broadband networks should be well placed to handle this download. Ofcom's Broadband Code of Practice means providers must give customers clear, realistic information and guarantee a minimum speed. If you’re not getting this, you may be able to leave your contract penalty-free. Check your speed now, so you can focus on the game rather than the loading screen." Ofcom has a website with sections devoted to broadband speeds and changing providers, in case you're interested.

Alongside yesterday's announcements that GTA 6 had become the most pre-ordered game in Xbox Store and PlayStation Store history, Sony and Microsoft shared strongly worded advice that players download the game ahead of time to avoid complications caused by "unprecedented demand". We saw last year what happened when Hollow Knight: Silksong arrived, causing chaos on Xbox, Steam, and Nintendo servers, and that game's reach was an order of magnitude less than GTA 6's. I don't recall a Selfridges store takeover in London for Silksong - do you?

The wait for GTA 6 is finally nearly over, as it arrives next Thursday, 19th November.

Less than two full days into the release of Grand Theft Auto 6, streamer BrycexD managed to hit credits through one continuous play-through, thus getting the inaugural speedrun. His time? 39:38:22.03.

In a recent development, "I'm the very first person in the world to beat the official release version of Grand Theft Auto 6!" he writes in a tweet. "I also now hold the speedrun world record as I stayed up for 50-plus hours and took no breaks.".

Someone could've beaten GTA 6 already, but didn't record it, and it's entirely possible someone sped through the main narrative faster as well.

Sources indicate that speedrun.com's leaderboards don't open for another 41-and-a-half days, leaving the field open without oversight. BrycexD is certainly the most prominent and publicly visible to have achieved credits on the monolithic game, though I'm not sure his methods were advisable.

It has been revealed that 50 hours without sleep isn't healthy, and I'm not sure how enjoyable it is to plug straight into such a gargantuan fresh game and time yourself getting through it. I'm glad he feels a sense of accomplishment, mind, and I can only imagine how good the sleep was afterward.

  • I'm also quite pleased about two points made on the game's Steam page.

It has been revealed that if a game is about cooking, at minimum I'll have to give it a quick testspin. Outside of this whole writing about video games thing, my other lot in life is soul bound to food, so I'm always curious to see how the two can be mixed together. And earlier this week, The Snackbar at the End of the World was revealed, a wonderfully cartoonish action-adventure game set in a magical, slightly post-apocalyptic version of 1960s Italy where you go out and forage for ingredients while fending off monstrous crops before turning them into tasty meals back in your struggling restaurant.

Recent findings suggest that first up, I just have to gush over the artstyle a bit. The whole game is hand-drawn with a colourful, comic book look that has an impressive sense of depth to it. It gives off a deep love of Italian architecture and landscapes, and that admiration clearly extends to the food too. Once you've gotten the ingredients you need, you then, loosely in the vein of Cooking Mama, prepare them and make various classic Italian dishes by performing some quick minigames. Simple, but charming! The rest of the time you're off killing some ghoulies that look like mutated fruit and veggies, with the occasional fungus-possessed hog and, uh, haunted statues? I think?

I'm also quite pleased about two points made on the game's Steam page. First is the content description: "This game features cartoon violence, sensitive political themes set in a fictional world, and depictions of an oppressive government committing crimes against its citizens." There is clearly a romantic quality to the game and I'd be worried if it didn't acknowledge any of the political context of the decades preceding.

The other line reads, "Every sound effect, musical note, design decision, and line of code is human-made. Because this game is about human relationships and delicious food – and that’s not a story we would ever trust AI to tell." Thank the lord! Right now there's no release date attached to The Snackbar at the End of the World, unsurprising given it was only confirmed this week. But while we all wait for a date, you could perhaps join me in throwing it a wishlist on Steam.

Original Story: With GTA 6 reviews now out in the wild, and countless Xbox players already getting access to it via the controversial Upcoming Zealand trick, it's no surprise that we've also got loads of screenshots and clips doing the rounds online.

One of the best sources for raw Xbox gameplay footage is the YouTube channel Fuzion Xbox Testing, and they're already uploaded their initial look at both the Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S versions of GTA 6.

Industry observers note that on Xbox Series X, it's very much what you'd expect - a really amazing-looking game with an internal resolution of 1440p, upscaled to 4K. The 30FPS performance is largely smooth, but does drop frames on occasion.

I also played GTA 6 on Xbox Series X for our Pure Xbox review, and here's what I said about it:.

"Of course, it's almost a given at this point that GTA 6 looks visually incredible, and I can confirm that it's definitely a stunner on Xbox Series X. There's some occasional pop-in, but it's minimal, and I only ran into a few tiny bugs during the review period (which may have been ironed out for release anyway). The performance is mostly very smooth considering the circumstances as well...".

"It should be noted that I played around 30 hours on a VRR-enabled display during the review period, and around 10 hours without one. I was perfectly happy with the performance in both cases, with the only noticeably big frame rate drops occurring during very rare and visually intensive gameplay sequences.".

On Xbox Series S, GTA 6 still looks really impressive from a visual standpoint, even though some drawbacks have clearly been made in terms of ray tracing and texture quality. The frame rate in the game's initial opening is shown to be a locked 30FPS in some sequences, dropping into the mid-20s during busier moments.

Overall though, the feedback we've seen from Xbox Series S players thus far has been very positive, especially in terms of how impressive the game looks. Rockstar Games actually talked to Wccftech about the Series S version as well, revealing they're using AMD FSR Upscaling 4 to scale the resolution to 1080p.

"On the Xbox Series S, we’re starting from a base resolution of 720p, which is scaled to 1080p using AMD FSR Upscaling 4.".

"...[our] focus on lighting made it vital for us to ensure we could use the same lighting solution on each console, including the Xbox Series S, where memory pressure posed a bit of a challenge. The results made that a challenge worth overcoming.".

Recent findings suggest that great stuff, then! We'll leave you with the comparison footage for GTA 6 on Xbox Series X and S down below.
