It has been revealed that xbox boss Asha Sharma has confirmed Wolfenstein 3 is in development at MachineGames, the Swedish studio behind the acclaimed Wolfenstein: The New Order, Wolfenstein 2: The New Colossal, and 2024's celebrated Indiana Jones and the Great Circle. Additionally, she revealed Doom developer idSoftware - one of the Microsoft-owned studios heavily impacted by sweeping Xbox job cuts earlier this year - is now working on a new game.

According to recent reports, sharma has, of course, been on a bit of a PR offensive of late, positioning herself alongside snippets of positive news at a time Xbox is embroiled in a massive business "reset" effort that has resulted in proposed studio closures and mass layoffs that will ultimately see 3,200 Xbox employees lose their jobs. This week's Wolfenstein 3 reveal similarly arrived in the form of a tweet posted directly from her social media account.

In a recent development, "Wolfenstein 3 is officially in production at MachineGames," Sharma wrote on X. "One of gaming's most notable franchises, and a team that has done remarkable work bringing it forward. Looking forward to sharing more." As for idSoftware's new project, confirmation of that - again attributed directly to Sharma - appeared in a post on Bethesda's website. "Slaughter Mode comes to Doom: The Dark Ages - Revelations on Monday," she wrote, "and the team is already working on its next game.".

In July, sweeping job cuts at Xbox resulted in 96 of idSoftware's 136 employees being laid off in a move one former team member described as a "bloodbath". Since then, idSoftware co-studio director Marty Stratton has attempted to downplay the cuts, recently insisting the studio was "doing great". He added id was "working more closely than ever" with MachineGames - a studio which appears to have escaped Sharma's restructuring efforts so far.

This week's Wolfenstein and idSoftware news follows similar efforts by Xbox to reassure fans their favourite franchises are unaffected by the recent layoffs. Shortly after substantial job cuts at Bethesda were confirmed, the company moved to insist The Elder Scrolls 6 was still "on the way" and that its intends were "unaffected" (the company has since released a trailer announcing its subtitle). It also confirmed a new Fallout game was in development.

According to recent reports, xbox's year of bad news - which includes ongoing boycott efforts relating to Microsoft's controversial involvement with the Israeli military - comes as the division celebrates its 25th anniversary. Earlier this week, Sharma shared a memo to staff marking the occasion, albeit one in which she seemingly championed a gen-AI future for games development, enthusing that, "A small team will be able to build worlds that today demand hundreds of developers".

Sorry to everyone named Luke in Nashville, because Kimmel had all the jokes about some of last night’s major winners, including a sly reference to Luke Combs being in a long list of male country singers named Luke, also including The Voice's own Luke Bryan. (That whole convo gets weird too because while not named Luke, Zach Bryan is also a famous country singer. None of these people are related.).

The CMAs are the single biggest night of the year for guys named Luke. Number 1! Luke Combs scored three nominations, three more than his brother Sean Diddy, they had a tribute to Dolly Parton, of course. Brooks and Dunn got the Lifetime Achievement Award. It’s the highest honor in country music, named after the highest singer.

That last bit is a Willie Nelson joke, which is quite funny, but only if you already know the Lifetime Achievement Award is named for him. I did not see it coming though when Kimmel brought up bobsledding in regards to “Choosin' Texas.”.

The major story this year is Ella Langley. She made history, her song “Choosin' Texas” spent 28 weeks at Number 1 on the Billboard charts, more than any song ever, and it’s still going. It’s still the No. 1 song. It’s been No. 1 since the Winter Olympics, which was mid February. This song has been No. 1 since the last time we thought about bobsledding!

It has been revealed that yeah, that’s a joke, but it’s also just the kind of absurd fact that’s worth remarking on. Ella Langley's crushing it, and this milestone is cool, but now I'll never think of it without also thinking of Olympics bobsledding. Sure, these are some fairly light jokes compared to his Trump stuff, but please don't say Mr. Kimmel never did anything for pop culture.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

#63357. Latest Update: Even our bunch of diehard PC gamers aren't that bothered by 30 fps in GTA 6

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 9m • 📚 Deep Dive (1897 w)

Latest Update: Even our bunch of diehard PC gamers aren't that bothered by 30 fps in GTA 6

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1897 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Pcgamer

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • For a bunch of performance snobs, we are a surprisingly forgiving bunch at PC Gamer.
  • It turns out, while we're happy to part with our money to buy expensive components to hit higher frame rates (and earn the right to brag about it), we're also just as happy to settle for less when a game does a lot of other things exceptionally well.
  • In a recent development, GTA 6 certainly does that.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For a bunch of performance snobs, we are a surprisingly forgiving bunch at PC Gamer. Yes, if you try to insult XCOM, you're going to get a slap, but we've only just started playing GTA 6 (well, some of us) and we're mostly over the whole 'only runs at 30 fps' thing already.

It turns out, while we're happy to part with our money to buy expensive components to hit higher frame rates (and earn the right to brag about it), we're also just as happy to settle for less when a game does a lot of other things exceptionally well.

In a recent development, GTA 6 certainly does that. That's the impression I get from most members of the team that have played it so far. Though if Rockstar is listening, when you do get around to our precious PC version, we'd love nothing more than 4K60—maybe more.

Recent findings suggest that I will no doubt appreciate frames above 100 fps when GTA 6 comes to PC. Heck, I'd even just appreciate going up to 60 fps. But in my handful of hours with the game thus far, I just have simply not been that bothered by it. Be it smart ways of masking low frames, or even just the slower, methodical control approach of the game, I'm less frustrated with my PS5 running the game at around 30 fps than I was recently playing Phantom Blade Zero at well above 40 fps on a handheld PC.

Maybe that's down to the world having a little bit of magic to it, maybe it's the engrossing tone and atmosphere, maybe it's just because it looks so darn pretty. Maybe it's because I haven't got to the game's most hectic moments yet and haven't really needed to hit a headshot with my console unable to keep up with me. I'll tell you how I'm getting on in another fifty hours. Cool, see you in three days, then?

I was dreading playing GTA 6 on my OG PS5—a dusty ornament that's been chilling out in my living room this last year doing absolutely nothing. I've got a nice gaming PC in my office (RTX 4090, Intel i9 13900K, 32 GB RAM), so it's been a long time since I've had to deal with games dipping below 80 fps. I have been spoiled.

In a recent development, the second I got to control Lucia, my fears seemed justified. Everything just felt sluggish. But that feeling didn't last. I played GTA 6 for around 5 hours last night (I am very tired) and I haven't thought about the frame rate once since that initial section. Whether I'm getting into shootouts with coke smugglers, speeding through the Keys at night, or bouncing around at sea, GTA 6 looks great and feels great.

I can still tell this isn't 60 fps, but it is smooth.

I can still tell this isn't 60 fps, but it is smooth. I'm sure I've encountered drops, but crucially I haven't noticed them. Sure, it's inevitably going to look better and run better on PC, but the lower performance on my PS5 promptly ceased to be an glitch, and I'm not regretting playing it on console.

In a recent development, GTA 6 is the kind of game where an uncapped framerate would be nice, but it doesn't feel essential. Like Red Dead Redemption 2 before it—a game I also played at 30 fps before it rolled out on PC—its pacing is measured. It feels designed around the limitations of the consoles it's launching on, prioritising detail and depth over twitch-based combat and precise interaction. It's exactly what I'd expect from a modern Rockstar game. Also like Red Dead Redemption 2 before it, I still feel the sense of longing for what this game will look like on PC. Make no mistake: the version currently available is a preview for what GTA 6 will be at its best. It's great, but those who can wait will be treated to a superior experience.

According to recent reports, it's also possible that the 30 fps cap will feel more restrictive once the online mode arrives—whenever that will be, and in whatever form it takes. It's one thing to handle a lower framerate within Rockstar's meticulously created campaign. It's quite another in a lobby of other players. If GTA 6's multiplayer is even half as chaotic as the current GTA Online, every frame is going to count.

As I was booting up GTA 6, I was expecting to be annoyed by the game's paltry frame rate. And I was—at first. Much like Fraser, during the opening scene with Lucia, I saw my fears come to life on the big screen in front of me. Objects juddering and blurring as I swung my camera around in the cramped cell. Did I just waste £80 on GTA 6 on PS5 when I should've held my nerve for the PC version?

It has been revealed that truth is, the frame rate has had nowhere near as much of a negative impact on my experience while I've been traversing the Floridian wilds as Jason. In part, I think that's because there's a lot more going on, as cars, shops, people, and poultry fly past me as I break most state, federal and ethical laws. That reduces the chance of my eyes fixating on any one object and noticing the adverse effects of the game's lower fps, or the ways Rockstar has gone about covering for it.

Low fps is one thing, but motion blur is the devil.

Low fps is one thing, but motion blur is the devil. That's not just my opinion, that's been scientifically verified (sorta) to be the opinion of PC Gamer readers. Admittedly, some motion blur may be required when the frame rate is this low, so I have played around with a few settings in GTA 6 to find the perfect balance. I'd heard through the grapevine that higher-than-default motion blur (default is 3, goes up to 10) may be preferential to reduce the more obvious juddering that is present at low fps, but whoever claims that is no friend of mine. I've landed on setting motion blur to 1 on the standard PS5, as it feels the cleanest overall. I wouldn't blame anyone for turning it off entirely, especially on a more powerful console where the frame rate may not dip as much.

It has been revealed that of course, I do agree with the rest of this lot: in an ideal world, playing the PC version, I'd be pushing a much higher frame rate with motion blur banished to the abyss where it belongs, and a full selection of graphics settings to tinker with to my liking. Yet, to my surprise, I'm not as much of a console version curmudgeon as I thought I'd be.

Recent findings suggest that is the low frame rate noticeable? Yep. Would it be better at a higher frame rate? Also yep. Is the low frame rate a detriment to my overall enjoyment of GTA 6? Only a smidge.

According to recent reports, I don't consider myself much of a framerate snob, but I'll admit I was side-eyeing GTA 6's 30fps just a little bit. Well, that was before the game came out. Now that I have my hands on it, with roughly six hours spent lollygagging around Leonida? I'm hardly noticing it, though I'll most definitely be appreciating a smoother experience once the PC version rolls around.

Like Jacob noted, motion blur definitely seems to be masking it somewhat—and I am traditionally a motion blur hater, so it's taken a little getting used to—but I'm genuinely pleasantly surprised at the balance Rockstar has managed to strike between a smooth performance and a dense, rich world.

GTA 6 taught me that I don't much care about frame rates as much as I expected. I got to start playing it a few weeks ago and didn't have anyone to compare notes with, and my first thought was: Huh, they got it to run at 60 fps after all! It all felt very smooth, even when I realized it was 30 fps after all. It was only a bit later I started noticing very occasional drops, like while driving during a gradual lighting chance from day to night.

I think it being consistent is key.

Industry observers note that but that's really infrequent. I think it being consistent is key. I'm on a PS5 Slim, by the way, not a Pro. That's not to say I still can't wait to see it at higher frame rates when it finally gets to PC. But 30 fps feels mostly fine for the time being.

It was actually spending a lot of time playing with handheld gaming PCs and laptops with integrated graphics that reminded me I shouldn't give as much of a shit about frame rate as I do. Largely that obsession is born of having high-end hardware sat in my desktop PC, but when crashing around with a range of handhelds I'm reminded of the old days when 30 fps was a target for PC games, too.

In a recent development, it's also reminded me that it really depends on the game engine, as well. Not every 30 fps game looks the same as other 30 fps games. And Rockstar has obviously worked incredibly hard to make sure that 30 fps looks as good as it possible can. Otherwise why would that be a solid target for all four of the console platforms it's released on?

For the most part Rockstar has done a great job of keeping things smooth.

I've been playing GTA 6 on the Xbox Series X, which does suffer from the odd dip in frame rate, too—though oddly I've only really noticed it during canned animations the characters do starting certain actions, such as opening the trunk of a car or pulling something out of it. But for the most part Rockstar has done a great job of keeping things smooth. And not just by using motion blur. For the record, I'm running that at 0 and have not looked back.

I'm less happy about the vignetting that I'm getting around the darkened edges of the screen, but I'm playing it blown up on a 4K projector so I've got plenty of screen real estate to enjoy. And I have been, thoroughly enjoying it, I mean. The frame rate, for me, hasn't got in the way once.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • While following a peculiar trail of silver and saffron leaves around the largest roots of the Treehouse, you come across a hexagonal wooden door lying half-hidden among ivy and moss.
  • You have been lured into the eternal prison of Sunday Afternoon.
  • As you step forward, your toe nudges an ornamental scroll.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

While following a peculiar trail of silver and saffron leaves around the largest roots of the Treehouse, you come across a hexagonal wooden door lying half-hidden among ivy and moss. Scraping away the dirt, you discover a faint, absurd engraving of a newspaper. What mystery is here? You turn the brass knob – strange, it is warm! – and the engraving of the newspaper flutters. The pages turn faster and faster, emitting a howling gale that bowls you head over foot. When you pick yourself up, you are inside a vast attic full of books and bricabrac, lit from one side by windows that offer no view of the outside world – just light and mist.

Tarnation! You have been lured into the eternal prison of Sunday Afternoon. Fortunately, there are several ways to escape. Each of the arcane objects before you is secretly a portal, transporting you to another site of arcane activity, in a bizarre web of diversions that cannot possibly reflect the hand of a human curator. Which will you choose?

As you step forward, your toe nudges an ornamental scroll. It growls and wriggles like a panicking caterpillar, scooting away under a table. Before you lose sight of it, you discern the title and subject of the text – it's an essay by Kyle Tam about the yokai of Promise Mascot Agency.

Deep in a drawer, you discover a sour-smelling binder full of extracts from an ancient and all but indecipherable dispute over the discovery of "generative AI" in something called "Significant Walk". The stakes are long-buried, but many of the individual pieces of writing are lively. Here is Bruno Dias noting in passing that "one of the harms of the 'AI' political project is the propaganda machine dedicated to making you feel stupid and helpless." Here is a professorial interjection from Brendan Keogh calling on the warring parties to recognise when "critiques of generative AI are actually just deflected critiques of the capitalist relations of technology and labour". Here is Mike Cook arguing that "what's happening is not unusual, it's not extreme, it's not unfair and it's not a 'public flogging'." Here is a ticker tape message from Hannah Nicklin observing that "if your radical position doesn’t have room for transformation it will not be safe until it contains just you".

A footnote in the same dusty sheaf of papers points you towards another work from Mike Cook in a different drawer. This one consists of neon slides, slotted into an antique View-Master, and explores a comparison between procedural generation and street photography.

Peering at the weirdly white and opaque windowpanes, you realise there are intricate equations traced in the condensation. It appears to be a post-mortem for a "post-cosy" game called Danchi Days, in which developer Melos Han-Tani discusses wishlist conversion rates and the problem of not fitting neatly into any recognisable genre.

It has been revealed that A snowglobe stands on a mantelpiece, the flakes still orbiting a miniature washtub as though the object had been recently shaken, even though the chamber has clearly been abandoned for decades. You put it to your ear, anticipating the faint jingle of Xmas bells. Instead, you are almost deafened by a screeching guitar chord. Here is Erin Keane to explain.

Next to the snowglobe on the mantelpiece, there's a souvenir shop conch shell, polished to a high sheen. You put that to your ear, hoping to catch the soothing shuffle of surf on shingle, and a disembodied voice tells you to piss off. Tim Sniffen has some thoughts about gentrification, and why only he should be allowed to do it.

Again, one of these mystic artefacts hides the key to your release from the suffocating stillness of Sunday Afternoon. Which will you choose? Or have you, perhaps, brought a sorcerous teleportation device of your own? Please share. Here is Joanna Newsom's Cosmia to help you think.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • When Slay the Spire 2 arrived back in March, it was to much enthusiastic acclaim.
  • In a recent development, so far major updates have brought the likes of buffs, balance adjustments, art updates, UI improvements, bug fixes, and more - and MegaCrit has also made other substantial adjustments including the jettisoning of third act boss Doormaker, after it decided the encounter was overly complex.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Slay the Spire 2, which released into early access earlier this year, is expanding once more with a major latest beta enhancement. This introduces the deckbuilder's first new character since launch - a whimsical musician armed with a bow - alongside two new modes, and more.

When Slay the Spire 2 arrived back in March, it was to much enthusiastic acclaim. Eurogamer's Bertie Purchie is a big fan, and has trumpeted its successes on multiple occasions, calling the sequel's co-op mode "transformative". And it was a commercial hit too, managing to shift over 5m copies in just a month of release. All of which means there are plenty of eyes on Slay the Spire 2, eager to see what developer MegaCrit does next.

In a recent development, so far major updates have brought the likes of buffs, balance adjustments, art updates, UI improvements, bug fixes, and more - and MegaCrit has also made other substantial adjustments including the jettisoning of third act boss Doormaker, after it decided the encounter was overly complex. And now, as 2026 nears its conclusion, the studio has released its "biggest (beta) patch yet", including a sweep of major additions.

As per MegaCrit's v0.113.0 patch notes, the headliner is The Fool; Slay the Spire 2's first fresh character, who's described as a "silly musician who wields a bow". Unsurprisingly, The Fool doesn't arrive in their final form, and the studio says it expects to make a "great number of content and balance changes" before the character is ready for the main branch.

Accompanying The Fool are two newly introduced game modes: Blitz and Dread. Blitz is described as a "condensed and chaotic" mode focused on deckbuilding. Unlocked after completing an Ascension run of any difficulty, it comes with five levels of Ascension shared across all characters. "The Merchant's wares feel a bit off," MegaCrit teases, "the map is gone, and Gold no longer matters??".

According to recent reports, if you're looking for a more gruelling challenge, though, there's the "brutally difficult" new Dread mode, designed for players who've reached Ascension 10 on all characters, including The Fool. All ascension modifiers are enabled, according to MegaCrit, while bosses are stronger and buff all enemies found across their Act. And if that's still not enough to get your heart racing, MegaCrit notes curses will also pile up as you climb the Spire.

Beyond the headline stuff, v0.113.0 tweaks rest sites so they appear one floor earlier every act, and that's alongside the usual list of UI changes, art additions, nerfs, balance adjustments, and more. Full patch notes can be found on Steam.

Recent findings suggest that those players eager to put Slay the Spire 2's latest additions through their paces will need to enable the beta branch by right-clicking on Slay the Spire 2 in their Steam library and navigating to Properties > Game Versions & Betas and selecting 'public-beta' from the dropdown menu. MegaCrit notes the game's main branch has also been updated with all content and changes from the previous beta.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, with less than a week to go before GTA 6's hugely anticipated release, the game's final map - or at least a stylised poster version of it, depicting the state of Leonida's key landmarks - has surfaced online. It was reportedly snapped during Selfridge's sizable GTA 6's takeover, and is seemingly the physical map included in Rockstar's £350 collector's edition.

Recent findings suggest that fans have been pondering GTA 6's map for some time now, cross-referencing previous map leaks with official trailer footage in an attempt to gain some insight into the major landmarks and regions Rockstar has in store. And while the newly leaked map is far from granular, it does at least appear to confirm Leonida's rough layout and the key locations players can visit this time.

Assuming the map's veracity, it's all rendered in an art style somewhere between mid-century tourism poster and Adult Swim, featuring the phrase "The Goodtime State" up top - a riff on the actual Florida's nickname, The Sunshine State - while Leonida's most notable points of interest are interspersed with cartoon figures.

There's a toking turtle (or possibly a tortoise - I'm no expert), a golfer proudly wearing assless chaps, a flying saucer, and more. I'll spare you the geographic details confirmed on the map in case you want to go in unspoiled. One point of amusement though: the way the map photo is cropped means fans searching for confirmation of an in-game Key West are still none the wiser.

It's not entirely clear where the wonkily angled photo originated from, but prominent Rockstar Games community insider Videotech, who shared the image on social media, suggested it came from a "naughty Selfridges employee" during Selfridges' GTA 6 takeover. The map itself appears to be the "double-Sided souvenir poster with map of Leonida" included in Rockstar's eyewateringly expensive GTA 6 Collector's Edition. This costs £350 and doesn't come with a copy of the game. Or assless chaps, for that matter.

It has been revealed that this isn't the first time GTA 6's map - officially remarked to be twice the size of GTA 5's - has leaked online, although previous leaks have been notably more controversial. Earlier this year, a group calling itself CyberLeek shared unofficial gameplay and map details in the name of what it called "Gamers' Rights". In August, with Netflix's official GTA 6 unveiling looming, the group cashed out nearly £200,000 from its crypto scheme.

Amid all this, Rockstar has been embroiled in legal action after it was accused of union busting following the firing of over 30 employees. The case's conclusion has been delayed until next week, meaning a verdict could arrive just as GTA 6 goes on sale.

First, Slow Horses was renewed for Seasons 9 and 10, meaning we’ll be getting at least four more seasons of the hit show, available with an Apple TV subscription. Then, just hours later, Amazon MGM finally dropped the bomb we've all been waiting for and unveiled that the next actor to play James Bond would be Robert Pattinson. Many of us had been waiting for that for months. Years, even, yet it still came as a surprise, given the latest rumors. In hindsight, I probably should have been clued in that the announcement was imminent after the Slow Horses news dropped.

Over the last few weeks and months, there have been a ton of rumors regarding the next Bond ahead of the long-awaited Bond 26 finally beginning production (we’re still not sure when that will actually happen). Names like Jacob Elordi, Henry Cavill, Callum Turner, and more have been rumored. Slow Horses star Jack Lowden was also heavily rumored in recent weeks. Sources indicate that it’s certainly possible for an actor to appear in multiple projects, but given Slow Horses' aggressive filming schedule (they have already wrapped Season 7, due next year, and are filming Season 8), it might have been a tough schedule to work out for Lowden had he been named Bond. When the next two seasons were confirmed, it should have clued me in that Lowden likely wasn’t going to be James Bond going forward. It’s quite possible that Apple may have actually been waiting on the Bond decision to announce it was moving forward with more seasons of Slow Horses, too. So, when the news dropped about the show's renewal, I should have known Bond’s announcement was on deck.

Sources indicate that interestingly, despite the announcements coming almost at the same time, there are also rumors that Lowden might not be part of Seasons 9 and 10. A report in Variety calls Lowden’s return “uncertain.” I’m not sure what to make of that. The book-to-screen adaptation has been adapting one book per season, generally. Season 6 was an exception, as it combined two books, the 6th and 7th in Mick Herron’s series Slough House. That's not all, though.

Warning! There are some spoilers ahead from the books Slow Horses is adapted from!

That would presumably mean that Season 7 will be an adaptation of book #8, Bad Actors. As fans of the TV show know, Season 6 ended on a cliffhanger with River having been poisoned by the Russian assassins. Book readers know that River spends Bad Actors on the sidelines, recovering from the assassination attempt, and doesn’t appear in the novel at all. If the show has adapted Bad Actors for Season 7, might Lowden be mostly absent? Cartwright does return in the ninth book, Clown Town, which we do know is going to be Season 8 of the show.

Sources indicate that here’s where it gets interesting. As of today, Clown Town is the most recent book to be published in the Slough House series, so we don’t know what Herron or the producers intend to take the series, so all eyes are on Lowden!

#63351. This is technically the worst version of GTA 6 that we'll ever play

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1432 w)

This is technically the worst version of GTA 6 that we'll ever play

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1432 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Pcgamer

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that I've been playing GTA 6 through the morning to try to see what the fuss is about, and now I totally get it.
  • In a recent development, that sounds like an insult, but I mean the exact opposite.
  • I work for PC Gamer, so forgive my snobbery when I say the PC version should be far superior to what we're right now playing on consoles.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that I've been playing GTA 6 through the morning to try to see what the fuss is about, and now I totally get it. After mere hours in the game, I'm already coming to terms with the scale of it; not just the size of the map, but the attention to detail on every object and interaction. But I have to remind myself, this is sure to be the worst version of GTA 6 we'll ever play.

In a recent development, that sounds like an insult, but I mean the exact opposite. If this is where the game is at launch, at its most barebones, running on years-old consoles on their way out, then think of what it will be like at its peak.

I work for PC Gamer, so forgive my snobbery when I say the PC version should be far superior to what we're right now playing on consoles.

A part of that is the possible frame rate bump from running on modern PC hardware. The standard PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series S/X are powered by pretty outdated architectures by today's standards: RDNA 2 and Zen 2. You're looking at the Radeon RX 6000 series and Ryzen 3000 series for PC equivalents.

Recent findings suggest that these chips have recently received support for more modern ML-powered FSR upscaling techniques from AMD, though Rockstar has only seen fit to enable FSR 4 on the Xbox Series S to help the underpowered console along. Sony also has AMD-powered upscaling tech for the PS5 Pro, but the standard PS5 doesn't get a whiff of that.

Industry observers note that it's only really the PS5 Pro with a more modern GPU—loosely equivalent to an RX 7800 XT—that might temper expectations for how fast the game may run on a modern gaming PC. Rockstar has mentioned the PlayStation 5 Pro wouldn't be capable of a steady 60 fps even with the more powerful hardware compared to the base model; however, hints at the sluggish CPU as perhaps the weak link. The PS5 Pro runs the same old eight-core CPU as the standard PS5, and if Rockstar's engine can make use of faster, more multithreaded CPUs with lots of cache, we should see a performance bump on PC.

In a recent development, that's not to exclude older gaming PCs. The Xbox Series S can cope with GTA 6, so should many gaming PCs of all levels. Notably so if Rockstar offers a range of upscaling options.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

It's ubiquitous upscaling that should make an even bigger difference to an eventual PC release and performance on all manner of PC. We know the game supports FSR 4.1, as both Sony and Microsoft are already using this as the foundation for their upscaling technologies on console, and Red Dead Redemption 2 offers both FSR and DLSS on PC. Since that game's release, we've seen the advent of frame generation technologies from both AMD and Nvidia, which could further increase how smooth GTA 6 feels on PC.

As a serial settings tweaker, I've been sorely disappointed by the sliders, or lack thereof, available to me in GTA 6 on the base PS5. I want levels to this stuff; an advanced menu for advanced men like me. I want to manage the foliage detail, draw distance, and ray-traced effects. Speaking of which, I'm sure we'll have the option to enable ray-traced shadows, right now exclusive to the PS5 Pro, and crank up the quality of most effects in the game on PC.

According to recent reports, the non-RT shadows are one of the few noticeable drawbacks about the standard PS5 version of GTA 6 I'm right now playing. They can pop in and out from reflections, and there is a jagginess to them in places.

Is any game going to be modded more than GTA 6? Our Joshua has been busy modding GTA 5 to try to turn it alchemy-like into GTA 6 for months now, and he never ran out of mods to install. While he may have strayed from his original mission almost immediately, the message is clear: GTA 6 is going to have a seriously busy mod scene.

The game will be all the better for it, too. Not every mod is going to enable a roving band of militant furries (Joshua's words, and no need to mod those into GTA 6) or trap the player in a tiny car; I'm sure GTA 6 will actually be a better game for the efforts of modders. It just takes a PC version and some intrepid people to make it happen.

In a recent development, this one is easy; one of the reasons for GTA 5's long-lasting legacy is the combination of GTA Online and custom jobs via the creator. Neither of which are actually here for GTA 6 yet. So on a very basic level, and you don't have to be a PC gamer to agree on this point, GTA 6 is going to get a lot better for the eventual online mode. And there will be an online mode, right? Even if Rockstar hasn't technically announced one is on the way yet.

On the flipside, if you're constantly getting griefed by a guy that only plays GTA 6 all day and won't let you leave your house in GTA Online, perhaps you could argue the game was better when it was single-player only.

In a recent development, it pains me to admit it, but GTA 6 is not only going to eventually run better on PC. It might be the definitive version in my eyes, but console gamers do have a high-fidelity future ahead of them, too. Both Sony and Microsoft are planning upcoming consoles that seem pretty likely to come out in roughly a year's time—providing the memory crisis doesn't ruin everything—and AMD is set to be providing more powerful silicon for these systems.

In a recent development, we're expecting to see the RDNA 5 architecture make its way into the next-gen consoles, paired with Zen 6 CPU cores of some size and description (these may be heterogeneous). That would put the consoles on a level playing field with PC components likely to launch around the same time (Zen 6 should be available on desktop by then, while perhaps a more limited launch for RDNA 5 by early 2028).

So that whole spiel about how current-gen consoles are years behind our fancy PCs won't get me so far once these fresh systems come out. I'll have to find a new stick to bash consoles with… er, not enough RGB LEDs? Anyways, the definitive GTA 6 experience on console is still yet to come—that'll be the version that's ready to make the most of these more capable units sometime next year or in 2028.

It has been revealed that there are going to be a helluva lot of patches, upgrades, and DLCs to come for GTA 6. Remember, GTA V got a new first-person mode with the then-next-gen PS4 and Xbox One, so there's plenty of opportunity for genuine upgrades down the line.

It has been revealed that though, saying that, by recent PC standards (poor ports, game-breaking bugs, and more), this GTA 6 launch has been relatively glitch-free. I mean, I've seen a couple of visual glitches and my colleagues have had some strange men falling out of the sky, but besides those open-world oddities you may expect of a game of this size and stature, it's been pretty smooth sailing so far.

I just hope the PC version can claim a similarly clean sweep for its eventual launch. So far, no word on when that might be.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • As shown off in the video above, CyberMP's not about being able to play through the base game's missions with friends, but rather cruise around Night City as a gang getting into races and PvP shootouts.
  • Sources indicate that "After almost six years of development, countless reworks, and code rewrites, we're finally launching the public beta," the modders wrote on Discord.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After a couple of years of regular testing behind closed doors, Cyberpunk 2077 multiplayer mod CyberMP is now out in open beta, giving anyone who fancies a bit of multi-merc action a chance to give it a go. Though, if you do, be prepared for bugs and crashes, as work on the mod is far from over with the release of this "true beta".

As shown off in the video above, CyberMP's not about being able to play through the base game's missions with friends, but rather cruise around Night City as a gang getting into races and PvP shootouts. In that regard, it seems more akin to GTA 4's online mode than GTA 5's, with classic improvised hijinks the main draw over being able to pull off gigs with a crew. Though, there do also look to be roleplaying servers which could scratch the itch of those more interested in pretending to be a merc than blowing up other people's rides.

Sources indicate that "After almost six years of development, countless reworks, and code rewrites, we're finally launching the public beta," the modders wrote on Discord. "Anyone can jump in and play now — no invites or applications needed. Fair warning: this is a true beta. Crashes, desyncs, and server drops under heavy load are completely normal for now. That's exactly why we need testers. We welcome everyone: regular players, future server admins, and those who just love breaking game mechanics.".

"Right now, our absolute priority is stability and fixing crashes," they continued later in the post. "New features are planned, but we need to polish the foundation first. A huge thank you to everyone who has been with us since the early versions, helped with closed testing, and patiently waited. We've finally reached this milestone. Let's see how the project handles real player traffic!".

It has been revealed that according to the modders, CyberMP's "client doesn't have a digital signature yet", which could cause antivirus software not to be a fan of it. They're also anticipating "problems with the anti‑cheat system", so it may be worth holding off on giving the mod a go if you're not keen on being trolled by someone with the sort of destructive power usually reserved for megacorps and AIs from beyond the blackwall in the Cyberpunkverse.

According to recent reports, for info on how to get CyberMP up and running, as well as create a custom server dedicated to the likes of roleplay or races, head over to its website. As you might expect, the mod requires a legit copy of Cyberpunk bought on either Steam, GOG, or the Epic store.

Tech Report: A new report reckons 40% of developers in the video games industry are using generative AI - but even more think it's harmful

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Despite all the outrage and criticism around game developers and publishers using generative AI in gaming, a new report from the Game Developers Conference (GDC) calculates that as many as 40 percent of developers active in the industry use the controversial tools in their work.
  • That's according to the latest State of the Game Industry report from GDC, which gathers data from more than 2,300 respondents including, but not limited to, game industry professionals, made up of developers, producers, marketers, executives, and investors.
  • Industry observers note that the report notes that 57 percent of developers who say they do use it, use gen-AI for "text generation, research, early prototyping, coding, and presentations".
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Despite all the outrage and criticism around game developers and publishers using generative AI in gaming, a new report from the Game Developers Conference (GDC) calculates that as many as 40 percent of developers active in the industry use the controversial tools in their work. This is up four percent compared to the same report last year.

That's according to the latest State of the Game Industry report from GDC, which gathers data from more than 2,300 respondents including, but not limited to, game industry professionals, made up of developers, producers, marketers, executives, and investors.

Industry observers note that the report notes that 57 percent of developers who say they do use it, use gen-AI for "text generation, research, early prototyping, coding, and presentations". There appears to be a big split between triple-A studios that use gen-AI (with 27 percent of triple-A developers noting that they "feel encouraged or pressured" to use it) and indie devs, of which only nine percent say the same. Perhaps unsurprisingly - given how vocally against gen-AI a lot of 'frontline developers' have been - the tools are mostly used by "business operations and services, mobile-only studios, and free-to-play developers".

Industry observers note that there seems to be a gap in the ages of those willing to use AI tools as well; per the report, over half (54 percent) of people 45 years or older reported using the tools - an eight-point increase from last year's survey. There is also more usage among men (45 percent) than women (33 percent).

According to recent reports, what is perhaps more striking is that more people responded to the survey saying that they think AI is having a negative impact on games (55 percent) than responded saying they use the tech, suggesting a trend of caution rather than widespread adoption. Notably, respondents saying they are wary of the technology increased one percent since last year, so more people think AI is having a negative effect on the industry now than at the same time in 2025. Perhaps that's because of the sweeping layoffs we've seen across the games industry, often mentioned in the same breath as AI. Or the 'AI slop' that's been flooding Steam and pushing more traditional developers out. Orr some of the abysmal projects we've seen launch that have clearly used gen-AI assets.

"I did not get into a creative industry to hand over the creativity to an algorithm," remarked one respondent from the UK when explaining why they don't use gen-AI tools. "I got into this industry to collaborate with creative people, not to have an advanced chatbot riff on the ideas of someone who was laid off," said another from California. "I believe that no one should have to read what no human has written and shouldn't have to see what no human has created," said yet another from Minnesota.

The use of generative AI remains controversial in the games industry, though with substantial companies like Epic and Microsoft doubling down on the tech, it seems this split between developers that want to embrace it and those that don't is only growing larger.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that knowing how to workout in GTA 6 will help you to increase your Strength and Cardio, which in turn will improve your health and increase your stamina. Working out will also manage your weight and build up muscle, affecting your appearance in GTA 6. While fancy gym memberships all over Leonida will become available in time, Jason has everything needed to get a sweat on right outside his house from the beginning of the story.

Realism is key here, so you can't just spend all day crunching weights as you'll soon hit a wall where no further gains can be made until you rest and recover – though consuming some protein after will halve the time you need to wait before you can go again. On screen prompts will inform you when you reach that point, and you can check the Fitness app on your phone to see what your current status and stats are. If you want to get fit fast, here's how to workout in GTA 6.

Recent findings suggest that the lower deck area behind Jason's house is full of Strength workout equipment, so this is a great place to start building muscle. If you're still in the process of repairing the property, then this is also where to fix the railing in GTA 6. To start exercising with any of the equipment, walk up to it and follow the prompt.

Industry observers note that most of the Strength workouts in GTA 6 follow the same basic method – hold both triggers to lift the weight (or yourself), then gradually release the triggers to lower back down in a controlled way, before fully pushing in both trigger to repeat the process. You shouldn't rush this, but keep an eye on your stamina gauge in the top-left corner as if that fully depletes then your workout will end. You may also need to quickly press X/A to push out the last few difficult reps, so watch out for that prompt too.

Industry observers note that kettlebell swings in GTA 6 are not like the other Strength workouts, as instead of carefully lowering the weight you need to let it drop freely then start your next swing at just the right time to maintain the momentum into the following rep. Look for the point where the kettlebell is between your legs and almost as far back as it will go, then squeeze both triggers to swing it back up to the top again before letting go.

While most of the early GTA 6 workouts you can do at Jason's house are Strength-based, there is a way to build your Cardio here too. Head to the back of the workshop underneath the house and you'll see a HANG BAG prompt appear, so hold that button to set up your punching bag outside.

Industry observers note that unlike the Strength exercises that you have to interact with to begin, you can simply walk up to the punching bag and start pressing the Melee button to rain down hits on it. No progress bar or rep counter will appear, though you'll get a notification when your Cardio gains have been maxed out for the time being.

Sources indicate that while this isn't a specific workout activity in GTA 6, you can also increase your Cardio by running or swimming for a period of time. A notification will appear to confirm this, but remember to check the Fitness app as if you've already maxed out your current Cardio gains then running all over the place won't give you further improvement.

As well as looking after your physical health, make sure you work on your GTA 6 relationship status to keep things sweet between Lucia and Jason.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The good folks over at Digital Foundry have been sharing their deep dive analysis on the Xbox Series X|S versions of GTA 6 today, presented in the form of a 23-minute video on YouTube, and a separate article over on their website.
  • Looking at both of these, there's a ton of interesting information that's shared about the two Xbox versions of the game, so we thought we'd provide a quick summary of what they think about GTA 6 on Xbox Series X and S.
  • This is just a summary though, and there's way more context and detail in the video at the bottom of this article.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The good folks over at Digital Foundry have been sharing their deep dive analysis on the Xbox Series X|S versions of GTA 6 today, presented in the form of a 23-minute video on YouTube, and a separate article over on their website.

Looking at both of these, there's a ton of interesting information that's shared about the two Xbox versions of the game, so we thought we'd provide a quick summary of what they think about GTA 6 on Xbox Series X and S.

This is just a summary though, and there's way more context and detail in the video at the bottom of this article.

According to recent reports, digital Foundry reckons that the Xbox Series X version of GTA 6 is a great-looking game for the most part, highlighting things like lighting, reflections and even the incredible hair system, while also pointing out minor downsides such as missing shadows and occasionally blurry appearances. They also reckon that the frame rate generally maintains its 30FPS target, but will slip in busy situations like chases and explosions.

In a recent development, "Generally speaking, the game acquits itself quite well on Microsoft's senior current-gen console. Visual settings seem pretty solid across the board.".

Recent findings suggest that the Xbox Series S version is also noted to be pretty good in the graphical department, retaining the core features that make GTA 6 such a great game visually. It's the frame rate that bothers DF the most, as it's much more variable and prone to falling below its 30FPS target. That said, it appears to hover around 25-30FPS for the most part.

In a recent development, "Series S offers the loosest 30fps lock, with large portions of the game playing out at frame-rates from the mid to high 20s. Again, it's possible to depress the frame-rate to around 20fps with vehicular destruction. The other consoles do a credible job of hitting 30fps, but Series S often lies in a 25-30fps no-man's-land.".

According to recent reports, if you're wondering which console is the absolute best to play GTA 6 on, it's unsurprisingly the PS5 Pro. Nevertheless, Digital Foundry claims that both the Xbox Series X and the PS5 versions "look and play well" despite their softer image (and the Series X is actually "slightly smoother" when setting the Xbox to 120Hz with a VRR display), while the Xbox Series S version is the "hardest to recommend" despite its surprisingly impressive visuals.

"In terms of visual features and performance, the PS5 Pro version is the best option available, with solid frame-rates, 4K-like image quality and a noticeable visual upgrade thanks to ray-traced shadows. However, the game looks and plays well on base PS5 and Xbox Series X as well, despite occasional minor frame-rate drops during regular play and a softer 1440p image. The Series S version of the game is the hardest to recommend, with consistent frame-rate drops to the mid-20s, a 1080p output resolution and a long list of visual cutbacks, though the overall character of the game's visuals still shines through.".

Both the video and the website article are totally different from each other, so it's worth watching / reading the pair of them and getting a better idea of how GTA 6 fares across both Xbox consoles (and PS5 for that matter).

In my experience, I've found GTA 6 to be fantastic on Xbox Series X across the board for the most part, and while the Series S version is clearly a little more unstable, I'd wager that most players will still be perfectly happy with it.

What are your thoughts on this? Let us know down in the comments section below.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

"Nobody was hurt" in a shooting last week near the California office of Clockwork Revolution developers InXile, both the studio and local police have confirmed. The incident, which took place on November 11th, is currently being investigated and police have reportedly taken a suspect into custody.

"Officers got there [on November 11th]," Tustin police sergeant Christopher Peterson said in statement to Aftermath. "They responded to a report of a drive-by shooting there. Located multiple shell casings. Nobody was hurt. Processed the crime scene, and then sometime [Friday] morning, a little before 11 [AM], they took a suspect into custody. And the investigation is still kind of ongoing as to where and why.".

"We’re relieved that no one was hurt at our inXile office," a spokesperson for InXile mentioned in a separate statement. "Our focus is on supporting our team, and we are working closely with law enforcement as they investigate.".

InXile are set to release steampunk RPG Clockwork Revolution next year. The studio, developers of the likes of Wasteland 3 and The Bard's Tale IV, are one of the few Xbox-owned studios not to have been affected - at least as of writing - by Microsoft's ongoing mass layoffs this year.

According to recent reports, since being announced in 2023, Clockwork Revolution's dripped with Bioshock-ish vibes and popped up semi-regularly at Xbox showcases. "Wield the power of an incredible device to travel back in time, changing the past and rewriting the future of the city you call home: the vibrant steampunk metropolis of Avalon," reads its Steam synopsis. "In this immersive RPG, you'll step into the shoes of Morgan Vanette, a fully customizable player-character and member of the Rotten Row Hooligans. Travel between past and present as you battle the ruthless Lady Ironwood, who has been manipulating time to keep the working class struggling while amassing immense wealth and power.".

Best wishes to the staff at InXile, here's hoping that going forwards they're able to get with making what's looking to be an intriguingly funky game without enduring any more concerning incidents like this one.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

All GTA 6 pre-orders come with a free month of GTA+, which nets you some in-game bonuses like a free vehicle, garage, and higher selling prices.

But before you excitedly claim your freebie, it’s essential you understand auto-renew will be enabled.

This means unless you disable it, you’ll be charged the monthly price of $7.99/£6.99/€7.99 as soon as your free month is over.

Once you’ve claimed your free trial, from the PS5’s home screen scroll left to the PS Store and select ‘...’ > Subscriptions:.

You’ll see all of your active subscriptions listed.

Select ‘GTA+’ and press ‘Cancel Subscription’:.

Don’t worry, you’ll still get to enjoy the entirety of your free month, this will just prevent you from being charged.

If you want to keep GTA+, then of course you don’t need to do this. Just be aware you will get charged every month. You can also re-activate your subscription if you choose to do so by repeating the steps above:.

Hopefully this heads-up helps anyway.

To be fair, the PS5 does tell you about this when activating your free month, but it’s GTA 6 release day and I suspect some of you will be giddy and not necessarily in the mood for the fine print.

Ubisoft has laid off 166 people from its offices in Montreal and Quebec City, saying in a statement provided to PC Gamer that its "production needs are changing, requiring us to adjust the size of some teams to ensure our resources are aligned with current production priorities and business needs.".

In a recent development, founded in 1997, Ubisoft Montreal is one of the biggest game studios in the world, with roughly 4,000 employees as of 2022. Ubisoft Quebec, launched in 2005, is somewhat smaller but still substantial: Its website says the studio has "a team of over 600 creative, passionate, and innovative talents." The cuts reportedly impact employees who could not be assigned elsewhere after their existing projects were cancelled or rescoped.

Whatever the reason, it's bleak: This is the latest round in a series of layoffs that have battered the tech giant since it unveiled a major restructuring in January, which followed years of struggles including workplace misconduct scandals, persistent difficulties getting games launched, and underperformance among major releases. Ubisoft noted in today's half-year financial report report that it's reduced its headcount by roughly 1,100 people over the past six months.

According to recent reports, ubisoft did have a significant hit earlier this year with Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced, but that wasn't enough to prevent post-launch layoffs at developer Ubisoft Singapore. Ubisoft CEO Yves Guillemot said today that "Q2 exceeded our expectations, driven by the continued success of Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced and solid contributions from our broader portfolio.".

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Crimson Desert and DokeV developer Pearl Abyss is planning to further integrate generative AI into its workflow.
  • The South Korean studio said as much in its latest quarterly Earnings Letter, explaining that it had previously "validated game systems only after implementing them manually." Now, Pearl Abyss is using AI "to rapidly validate diverse design concepts prior to actual implementation," and argues the move "enables a more efficient allocation of development resources and enhances overall production speed.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Crimson Desert and DokeV developer Pearl Abyss is planning to further integrate generative AI into its workflow.

The South Korean studio said as much in its latest quarterly Earnings Letter, explaining that it had previously "validated game systems only after implementing them manually." Now, Pearl Abyss is using AI "to rapidly validate diverse design concepts prior to actual implementation," and argues the move "enables a more efficient allocation of development resources and enhances overall production speed.".

"However, AI serves strictly as a tool to support concept validation and pipeline productivity, while the core gameplay experience and actual content creation remain fully driven by our development team," the developer noted.

When Crimson Desert first launched, players spotted a crop of suspicious in-game images that looked like they were prompted into existence. Pearl Abyss soon explained that some "2D visual props" were generated with AI tools, but were always intended to be replaced with human-made art, before swiftly patching them out of the hit open-world game.

It seems Pearl Abyss is now even more keen on the controversial tech, however: "We are integrating AI technologies to enhance development productivity and overall quality. AI is being utilized across various stages of development - including the automation of repetitive tasks, content creation support, and test optimization - and we are expanding its implementation throughout our entire development pipeline. We view AI not as a substitute for human developers, but as a tool to elevate development efficiency and quality. We will continue to expand our application of AI to deliver higher-fidelity games to the market more expeditiously.".

It has been revealed that elsewhere in the letter, the studio said its previously unveiled creature-collector DokeV is "targeting a launch in the second half of 2028" and we should hear more about it within the year. DokeV was initially targeting a 2023 launch a few years ago. Meanwhile, Crimson Desert is being prepped for a Nintendo Switch 2 launch "in the first half of next year.".

Recent findings suggest that the use of generative AI in game development has been a hot topic for years, though it's only become more prevalent in recent months as 'AI slop' floods Steam and big companies like Epic Games proudly adopt the tech. A recent report even estimated that around 40 percent of active developers use AI tools in their work.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Legend of Zelda was in "dire straits" before Breath of the Wild gave the beloved series a massive second wind, according to two former Nintendo marketing leads.
  • Industry observers note that the Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time's most recent remake has been a mega success, becoming the fastest-selling Switch 2 game so far, but the shiny new adventure has also prompted some online debate over where the series should go next.
  • Nintendo of America's ex-director of social media marketing Kit Ellis and former public relations manager Krysta Yang chimed in on the discourse in their latest podcast (below), and explained that Zelda wasn't doing too hot before the Switch era.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Legend of Zelda was in "dire straits" before Breath of the Wild gave the beloved series a massive second wind, according to two former Nintendo marketing leads.

Industry observers note that the Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time's most recent remake has been a mega success, becoming the fastest-selling Switch 2 game so far, but the shiny new adventure has also prompted some online debate over where the series should go next. Should Zelda lean into its carefully directed history - like the one brilliantly remade in Ocarina of Time - or keep the ball rolling with Breath of the Wild's wide open, spontaneous sandbox?

Nintendo of America's ex-director of social media marketing Kit Ellis and former public relations manager Krysta Yang chimed in on the discourse in their latest podcast (below), and explained that Zelda wasn't doing too hot before the Switch era.

"There has been some revisionist history out there lately," Ellis remarked in response to fans who reckon "the Zelda team ripped away" series staples, like classic dungeons and linear worlds, at the height of their popularity.

"I remember, I was going to the focus groups where it was a really dark moment," Ellis continued. "The feedback was like, 'The fan base is dwindling. This is not bringing in fresh players.'".

The Legend of Zelda was supposedly "shrinking," while "interest in the audience was getting smaller and smaller" with each new entry. "They had to do something dramatic," Ellis stated.

"This series was in dire straits. They were selling, like, nothing," Yang added.

The Zelda series was certainly never irrelevant, but there's a pretty major gap between the roughly 8m copies Twilight Princess sold at the beginning of the Wii generation, the roughly 3m copies Skyward Sword sold at the end of the console's life, and the 34m copies that Breath of the Wild sold just one console generation later.

Recent findings suggest that it was a success so massive it spawned a wildly ambitious sequel, Tears of the Kingdom, and even influenced the latest 2D Zelda, Echoes of Wisdom. Now that classic Zelda's back in the spotlight, though, I do hope Nintendo's able to slot the series' curated dungeons into whatever the next mainline game becomes.

Sources indicate that I'm modding GTA 5 every day in a quest to either transform it into a PC version of GTA 6 or break it entirely. Come back tomorrow to find out what new horrible thing I've done to Rockstar's baby, or check out what I got up to earlier.

It has been revealed that it is time to say goodbye to Grand Theft Auto 5. Did we not say goodbye literally yesterday, when I installed a mod named Farewell Los Santos, and there was even a video and everything, and we put Komm Susser Tod over it?

No. 53 mods ago, I told you, the reader, that my mission here was to either mod GTA 5 into a version of Grand Theft Auto 6 on PC, or break the game trying. Admittedly, my mission was successful: GTA 5 is actually better than GTA 6 now. But that means only one thing: as a final send-off, I can think of nothing better to do than finally fulfil the other potential outcome of our initial gambit. It is time to break GTA 5 entirely.

I have installed Fences Network, Simple Weapons Saving, Dragon Trainer V – How to Train Your Dragon Mega Pack, Empire: Singleplayer Overhaul, In The Hood (Gang), BodyGuard Menu, Addon Car Spawner Plus, Rideable Sandworm, Buckme Money App, Realistic Tactical Loadout - GTA VI Inspired Visible Weapon Carry, Pickup, & HUD System [Legacy & Enhanced], Gang Mod Respect System, Los Santos Collapse [Legacy & Enhanced] Zombie mod, The Last Heist - An ending for GTA V [Story Mod | 10 Missions], Real Life Mod [Legacy], Raul's Revenge DLC, Warzone Infil, RageHandlingEditor (RHE) [Legacy & Enhanced], On foot radio (with animations and headphones customization), Keep Right, and Ending C with M83 Midnight City.

In other words, everything that was on the front page of GTA 5 Mods dot com's scripts section when I loaded it up this morning. This took some doing, involving quite a lot of faffing around with OpenIV and myriad .rpf packages to get everything installed.

Recent findings suggest that would you be surprised to hear (you will not be surprised to hear) the game does not start anymore? GTA 5 has gone to that great sleep that awaits us all. Oh, don't get me wrong: it will boot to the main menu, but try to resume a game or start a new one and GTA 5 will, valiantly, spend about a minute and a half with its cogs audibly grinding against another before simply dumping you back at your desktop—no fanfare, no error message, just swift death. After enduring 53 other mods without completely breaking, it rests now in the great beyond.

I can't wait to do this to GTA 6.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Bigfoot in GTA 6, also known as Skunk Ape or Mr Mangrove, isn't just an Easter egg, but a full blown chain of side quests tied to a character called Kirk, who's obsessively hunting the cryptid through the Floridian swamp.
  • To start with you'll have to ensure your random encounter with the Skunk Ape, but afterwards you can pursue the quest line pretty straightforwardly.
  • For a friendlier form of wildlife, check out how to pet animals in GTA 6.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bigfoot in GTA 6, also known as Skunk Ape or Mr Mangrove, isn't just an Easter egg, but a full blown chain of side quests tied to a character called Kirk, who's obsessively hunting the cryptid through the Floridian swamp. After your character stumbles across Bigfoot's location, you can contact Kirk and help him hunt down the Skunk Ape for good across several missions, in which you find the strange effigies that this creature is leaving behind. All this wraps up with a fairly significant choice, one that harkens back somewhat to the famous bigfoot encounter in Red Dead Redemption.

To start with you'll have to ensure your random encounter with the Skunk Ape, but afterwards you can pursue the quest line pretty straightforwardly. Pick the right choices, and you can get a real cash reward.

For a friendlier form of wildlife, check out how to pet animals in GTA 6.

The Skunk Ape questline in which you help Kirk hunt down a monster he calls "Mister Mangrove" is broken up into several smaller quests and objectives.

This is a questline you can start very early on in GTA 6, all the way in chapter 1 1, and see through to the end in the same chapter. The rewards are pretty significant, assuming you make a certain choice.

It has been revealed that to find Bigfoot initially in GTA 6 before starting the Skunk Ape quest, you need to go to the location on the GTA 6 map marked above. Once there, you'll see Bigfoot moving fleeing into the marshland after eating a deer.

It's not mandatory that you follow (or even that you have this encounter for the larger quest), but if you do, you'll be led to an effigy tied to a tree. Examining it for too long causes you to inhale spores from it and pass out.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more.

To start Kirk's quest "Skunk Apeology 101", go to the Rusty Anchor bar in North Key Lento. On entering through the main doors, look immediately to the right and examine the notice board. There'll be a poster left by Kirk, with a number to call if you've seen the Skunk Ape.

In a recent development, with the number added to your contacts, call Kirk. He'll give you a meeting place and time to start the quest, marked on your map with KK.

Industry observers note that meeting with Kirk and getting some explanatory dialogue, he'll have you hit a stick against a truck to trigger the distant howls of Mr. Mangrove. You'll follow him into the woods (I recommend you equip your flashlight in the equipment tab in the bottom left radial menu).

To find Mr. Mangrove after splitting up, use your Focus Mode when you hear the Skunk Ape howling, and there'll be a ripple effect. Follow those ripples until a chase is triggered, leading to another effigy.

At this point, after studying it, you'll be chased by a strange boar. Don't worry too much about escape – whether it catches you or not, you'll end up back at the car, either because you flee successfully or because you're knocked out and Kirk drags you there. He'll tell you he'll contact you again with the next steps, which will take about half a day in-game.

Kirk tells you that he needs you to find three tree Effigies left behind by Mr. Mangrove. There are actually nine of them in total, but you only need to find three of them. We've marked all their locations on the map above – when you're close, use Focus Mode again to see them through the trees, then use L2/LT to study them.

After completing this, you'll be given another message to wait, as now Kirk has the data needed to track the Skunk Ape down for good.

Recent findings suggest that on meeting back up with Kirk at night, you'll be given a customised tranquilizer rifle and taken up in a helicopter. After flushing out the Skunk Ape, you need to fire several rounds into it. Despite the long range, there's no drop-off or delay on the rifle, so just aim at Mr. Mangrove's centre mass and you should be fine.

Eventually he'll end up in a small encampment. Follow him into the building, and you'll see him pass out. When you try to lift him however, things get weird, as you'll be exposed to the pollen spores he emanates and pass out.

In this questionably hallucinatory experience, you'll now control a frog and have to find flies to eat. There are three different spots to go to where flies congregate over corpses.

Sources indicate that be wary that there are alligators who will try to eat you. Keep your distance, and use Focus Mode to home in on the flies.

Recent findings suggest that having eaten flies, now you'll become one, obviously. Head back to the shack you found the Skunk Ape in, but now follow the other pier around back to the helicopter (its lights should mark it out). Stay close to Kirk, and you'll hear him talking about a man named Harry Sherrick who disappeared – who actually is Mr. Mangrove, with a valuable QR code tattoo that will lead to open his substantial bank account.

It has been revealed that waking up in the shack with Kirk and the unconscious Mr. Mangrove, you can choose to side with either of them, now knowing that Kirk is fully aware that the Skunk Ape is some transformed human being and is only hunting him to rob him. You can choose to shoot either of them with the dart gun, or neither. Here are the options and what they give you:.

No matter what outcome you pick, you get to keep the rifle, a legendary variant "Mister Mangrove" Laird 350 Bolt Action Rifle. That reward, at least, is consistent.

It has been revealed that of the three, the best choice if you want to make money fast in GTA 6 is to shoot Mr. Mangrove. However, if you want to be an ethical criminal, I would shoot neither and let the Skunk Ape have his revenge.

According to recent reports, it's heavily implied that Mr. Mangrove is a man named Harry Sherrick who was transformed by swamp spores into a Skunk Ape, similar to the mutated boar that chases you early in the quest chain.

Kirk knows this and has been relentlessly hunting and hounding Sherrick anyway – not to help him, or to reveal the truth to the world, but to simply get access to the tattoo and steal the money. Kirk's a pretty shitty person, simply put, especially as he had no intention of even cutting Jason and Lucia in on the reward.

If you lose track of your newly introduced rifle, make sure you know how to store and recover your weapons in GTA 6.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A hacker has pleaded guilty to a number of online crimes, including the 2022 breach of Rockstar Games which resulted in a bunch of mid-development clips of GTA 6 in action leaking onto the net.

It has been revealed that the BBC report that, on November 16th, Arion Kurtaj pleaded guilty at Woolwich Crown Court to the Rockstar Games hack and a number of others he carried out with the hacking gang Lapsus$ while aged 16 and 17. Kurtaj, now aged 21, was previously sentenced to stay in a secure hospital indefinitely due to the severity of his autism, but was subsequently deemed fit to stand trial. He'll be sentenced at a later date.

Kurtaj carried out the 2022 Rockstar hack while on bail for other hacking offences and being housed at a Travelodge hotel under police protection, the latter on account of rival hackers threatening to attack him over stolen Bitcoin stashes. The Rockstar hack was reportedly done using an Amazon Fire Stick plugged into the hotel room's TV, plus a Bluetooth keyboard and mouse.

According to recent reports, 90 clips of unfinished GTA 6 were flung online by that hack, with Rockstar having refused to cooperate with Kurtaj's demand via an internal Slack channel that the company contact him on massaging app Telegram within 24 hours. Rockstar claimed the breach cost them $5m million to recover from, in addition to staff having to waste thousands of hours.

Earlier this year, GTA 6 suffered yet another leak, with a hacker or hackers going by "Cyberleek" posting various videos of the game in action. Rockstar and parent organization Take-Two quickly sprung into action, taking down videos, filing subpoenas, and issuing a statement that called the leak "heartbreaking".

It has been revealed that hopefully with the game's console release later this week, those will be the only two GTA 6 leaks which have to be added to the annals of gaming history. As much as marketing can leave a bad taste in the mouth, especially when it barely shows anything of the actual product being advertised, neither of the GTA 6 leaks served much of a purpose beyond forcing people to waste some time and energy talking about the perpetrators.

Instead of a full season, it’s only getting ten episodes and will be replaced by NCIS: Sydney in January, which is also getting just ten episodes. Now, with the Season 3 finale fast approaching, Kyle Schmid is very passionate about getting a Season 4 renewal, but his words don’t exactly reassure me.

The NCIS prequel is only three seasons in, but it’s definitely become a favorite among fans. And with Mark Harmon back as Leroy Jethro Gibbs for all of Season 3, these upcoming episodes are better than ever. And the hope for a fourth season is getting stronger. Unfortunately, there’s no telling when CBS could be making a decision, so Schmid is jumping on the campaign train. The Mike Franks actor told TV Insider just how much the show, crew, and cast deserve another season, and I desperately need it:.

Recent findings suggest that the show is exceptional this year. I’m so proud of the writing team, our cast, our crew, everybody that I had the pleasure of working with for the past four or five months. I think we found our thing this year. I think the show’s found its shape. I think the characters have found their meaning.

In a recent development, as a day one Origins fan, I would love nothing more than to never see this show end, especially because it’s gotten better the longer it’s been on. Plus, while Schmid couldn’t go into detail about what’s to come, his comments make it clear that Origins cannot end any time soon:.

And let me tell you, when I say I don’t want the show to end like this, the show can’t end like this, and I mean that with all my fucking heart. So when you get to the finale of the show, you will know damn well what I mean when I say it cannot go out like this, so there better be a Season fucking 4.

Recent findings suggest that this has me very concerned, because Schmid is implying that we're going to be dying to see what happens after Season 3 ends. And let me tell you, I absolutely hate cliffhangers, and I hold grudges against them when reveals are canceled right after one, because I know we'll never get a resolution. So, if Origins ends in a way that leaves me ravenous for more, it better not get axed.

Season 1’s finale saw Lala getting into a car crash, while Season 2 ended with Randy getting abducted. If Season 3 follows the pattern and ends on a cliffhanger, which it sounds like it will, a cancellation would be heartbreaking.

I am also passionate about the show getting another season, and if the finale is as significant as it sounds, I will be hopping on the campaign train with the actor.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Industry observers note that new Game Plus, as mentioned below, raises the level cap to 100, and scales enemies and regions in the game around you.
  • Recent findings suggest that there'll be latest versions of equipment with new stats to find, and they'll be labelled with "NG+" so you know when you've picked one up.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

ENHANCEMENT 17TH NOVEMBER: The Blood of Dawnwalker update 1.2 - the update that brings a New Game Plus mode, predominantly - is now available on PC, PS5, and Xbox Series S/X.

Industry observers note that new Game Plus, as mentioned below, raises the level cap to 100, and scales enemies and regions in the game around you. Previously, the game was zone-scaled, so some zones were tougher than others. In New Game Plus, this will no longer be the case, so you can go and explore Xanthe's region at the back of Vale Sangora straight away, if you want to.

Recent findings suggest that there'll be latest versions of equipment with new stats to find, and they'll be labelled with "NG+" so you know when you've picked one up. You can unlock New Game Plus from the main menu after choosing your base save and difficulty option. All of your accrued skill perks and abilities will be available to you at the start of the Withering Away quest in the game's prologue.

The full patch notes for Dawnwalker upgrade 1.2 are:.

ORIGINAL STORY 13TH NOVEMBER: A New Game Plus mode is coming to vampiric RPG The Blood of Dawnwalker next week.

Developer Rebel Wolves has now detailed everything coming with The Blood of Dawnwalker's Update 1.2, at the moment planned to go live sometime next week, and top of the list of changes is a New Game Plus for players who have already rolled credits on the game.

It has been revealed that "If you completed the Epilogue, you can dive right back into Vale Sangora with New Game+," the developer revealed earlier today. "Your level, skills, and inventory will carry over." Rebel Wolves is upping the level cap to 100 for New Game Plus, which will also have items with updated stats and enemies "balanced and scaled uniformly across all regions.".

Elsewhere in Revision 1.2, the studio is making tweaks to "enemy health pools and how often they use their abilities during combat," and improving terrain geometry to allow for "smoother movement during combat and exploration." We'll need to wait for more comprehensive patch notes before finding out which enemies are getting spongier or flimsier, however.

While the incoming patch doesn't seem to be as beefy as the last - the one that added animal petting and an easier Story mode - it'll be a good way to sink your teeth deeper into a game that's already begging to be replayed, thanks to a time management mechanic that can drastically change any given run.

The new game from some former The Witcher 3 veterans came out in September and seems to have been a hit. Eurogamer's The Blood of Dawnwalker review called the game a "familiar dark fantasy adventure, but one with bold and provocative ideas of its own, that's mostly, enormously successful.".
