💡 Key Takeaways
  • GTA games are big, beautiful sandboxes of destruction, and sometimes I want to forget about story missions and just magically fill my pockets with cash, spawn a tank or a jet, and go on a rampage with infinite incendiary ammo.
  • Naturally, you can do that with GTA 6 cheats.
  • Maybe that's fair—Rockstar devs don't want you busting out cheats and skipping through the game they spent 10 years crafting.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Using cheats in GTA 6 is a given. GTA games are big, beautiful sandboxes of destruction, and sometimes I want to forget about story missions and just magically fill my pockets with cash, spawn a tank or a jet, and go on a rampage with infinite incendiary ammo.

Naturally, you can do that with GTA 6 cheats. But only eventually. If you were hoping to try out some cheats the moment you step into the game, I've got some bad news for you—and then some worse news. Here are the problems:.

Maybe that's fair—Rockstar devs don't want you busting out cheats and skipping through the game they spent 10 years crafting. But then again, if you shell out potentially $100 for a game, shouldn't you be able to play it however the heck you want? I think so.

Industry observers note that GTA 6 is a big, long game, with a five chapter main story that contains 91 missions. It took me about 90 hours to finish, at which point I could finally access the cheats menu.

That's where I found the next bit of bad news...

Congrats on playing those 90 hours: are you ready for 90 more? Most cheats on the menu are locked because there are requirements you need to meet to use them. Want a cheat that removes fall damage? First you'll need to survive 20 falls of over more than 40 feet. Want to spawn a parachute? First complete 50 skydives and basejumps.

Using an infinite ammo cheat means first winning 25 medals on shooting ranges. To fast-forward time you'll need to find 10 collectible watches—and in 90 hours I found exactly one of them. Spawning a jet means first completing every single challenge in the game, which is gonna take, ooh, let me check… forever.

Keep up to date with the most vital stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

I don't love this cheat unlock system at all, but there's even more bad news:.

Sources indicate that want to use a cheat to give yourself an extra $250,000 so you can go on a car buying spree? Cool, go ahead. But you won't be able to save your progress once you enable a cheat.

Sources indicate that whatever fun you have cheating is purely of the sandbox variety. You can buy cars and clothes and guns with cheated money, but you'll lose it all when you stop playing because you're not allowed to save your game once you use a single cheat. Booo.

And there's one final bummer for ya:.

I tried it. I opened an older save where I hadn't yet completed the main story, and tried to input the cheats I'd learned from my complete game save. No dice! The cheats don't work unless you're using a save file that's story complete. So, starting over at the beginning and using cheats? Not gonna happen.

I'm really not a fan of this. With so many restrictions in place, Rockstar has really taken the fun out of being a huge GTA cheater! When GTA 6 finally comes to PC, I hope modders make cheats their top priority.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Tech giant Intel are being taken to court for allegedly "misleading" their investors about the sheer scale of the impact of generative AI-fuelled component price hikes on PC sales.
  • All this follows Intel's last round of quarterly results, in which they revealed a significant revenue fall; this triggered an Intel stock price drop from $92.07 per share on October 29th to $65.76 per share the next day, which this week's lawsuit characterises as "the largest single-day price decline for Intel common stock in over 50 years".
  • The lawyers in question are from Robbins LLP, who specialise in "shareholder, whistleblower, antitrust, & consumer litigation".
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tech giant Intel are being taken to court for allegedly "misleading" their investors about the sheer scale of the impact of generative AI-fuelled component price hikes on PC sales. The class action lawsuit in question claims that Intel's distribution and manufacturing partners have had to deal with "a massive glut of unwanted PC inventory", and that the gains from Intel's investments in AI datacenters aren't enough to make up for slowing sales of PCs to regular Josephines who just want fancy boxes they can play Deadlock on.

All this follows Intel's last round of quarterly results, in which they revealed a significant revenue fall; this triggered an Intel stock price drop from $92.07 per share on October 29th to $65.76 per share the next day, which this week's lawsuit characterises as "the largest single-day price decline for Intel common stock in over 50 years".

The lawyers in question are from Robbins LLP, who specialise in "shareholder, whistleblower, antitrust, & consumer litigation". In a press release, they say they've filed suit on behalf of anybody who bought Intel stock from July 23rd to October 29th this year.

The suit claims that Intel neglected to tell investors that falling PC and component sales were having a "materially greater negative impact" on their third financial quarter 2026 Client Computing and Physical AI Groupresults than Intel had previously stated – to the tune of "hundreds of millions of dollars" in revenue shrinkage, compared to the previous quarter, with the situation still expected to "worsen".

They also accuse the company of keeping schtum about the aforesaid "massive glut of unwanted PC inventory", together with the fact that "any positive impacts to Intel’s business and financial results resulting from data center construction and other aspects of the AI boom were more than offset by the negative effects on the Company’s business and financial results resulting from the PC market slowdown and the excess inventory buildup described above.".

Finally, they say Intel bosses have failed to disclose that they're struggling to procure an adequate supply of substrates – that is, materials used to create the base layer of chips, circuit boards and similar components. As such, the lawyers claim, Intel couldn't "ramp up production to meet data center CPU demand even if the Company chose to divert production resources because of a slowdown in PC-related sales.".

It has been revealed that once the Godzilla of personal computing, Intel haven't been having a brilliant few years. Back in 2024, they recorded a multi-billion dollar quarterly loss, pushing then-CEO Pat Gelsinger to resign. As regards sales of gaming PCs, they've fallen behind AMD, though they've reportedly taken some ground back recently as regards desktop CPUs. As regards graphics cards, they have long been dwarfed by Nvidia.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Netflix's long-gestating Magic: The Gathering animated series is called Planeswalker, and it's coming in 2027.

It has been revealed that the title was revealed at MagicCon Atlanta, and Netflix shared a first look at the show on Twitter/X on 13th November. "Every great story begins with a spark. Here's your first look at Planeswalker, a newly introduced animated series based on Magic: The Gathering. Coming to Netflix in 2027", the firm wrote, and shared a teaser, which you can see below:.

According to a synopsis shared with IGN, the series follows Chandra Nalaar, "a volatile pyromancer hunted for her gifts, and haunted by her past". It continues: "Confronted by an insidious force, Chandra and some of the most legendary Planeswalkers must harness their extraordinary abilities, navigate treacherous alliances, and battle their own inner demons to prevent a cataclysmic war that threatens to consume their very existence".

Netflix first announced a Magic: The Gathering series in June 2019, with Avengers: Endgame directors Joe and Anthony Russo attached, and it was originally due in late 2022. Two years in, the original showrunners departed over creative differences, and in September 2024, Netflix confirmed it had started again from scratch with Star Trek: Picard and 12 Monkeys showrunner Terry Matalas in charge.

IGN reports that Matalas, who most recently ran Marvel's VisionQuest, is running the show alongside Cindy Appel. Budapest-based studio DIGIC Pictures is handling the animation.

At the end of last month, we learned PUBG is also being turned into a live-action series for Netflix, with Donald Glover set to direct, write, executive produce, and star.

Glover is a two-time Emmy and Golden Globe winner, best known for Atlanta and Community. Krafton calls PUBG "one of the world’s most enduring gaming franchises", and says the game, which is credited with popularising the battle royale genre, holds seven Guinness World Records.

According to recent reports, just like with the EU sale, we have assembled the following list of every game in the Adventure Awaits offer that we awarded a 9/10 or higher. We've also added a personal pick from the 8/10s at the end, because we couldn't see it go unmentioned.

As ever, if you're looking to grab some eShop credit before diving in, we've got you covered with the following links from our store.

Please note that some external links on this page are affiliate links, which means if you click them and make a purchase we may receive a small percentage of the sale. Please read our FTC Disclosure for more information.

13 Sentinels: Aegis Rim is a wonderful achievement for dynamic storytelling, as it puts forth a compelling and multifaceted narrative that’ll keep you guessing right up until the very end.

This excellent story, combined with enjoyable combat portions, a striking art style, and some top-notch voice acting make for an experience that you shouldn't miss. It’s the kind of game that’ll have you wishing that you could play it again for the first time, just so all its best elements could be fresh again.

Aegis Defenders is a fantastic game, brilliantly blending the tower defence and platforming genres in a unique way to produce a memorable and enjoyable experience.

Lovable characters, interesting lore, plenty of secrets, engaging gameplay, and gorgeous presentation combine to make this a must-have for your Switch, a real gem on the eShop.

Recent findings suggest that AI: The Somnium Files – nirvanA Initiative is one of the most interesting visual novels we’ve played through in a while. The murder mystery at its heart is brought to life by some great writing and quirky characters alongside the satisfyingly integrated, beautifully balanced Psync puzzle elements.

It has been revealed that even with some minor control complications, there is a lot to love in this game, even if you never picked up the original. Highly recommended if you're even a little bit curious.

Sources indicate that the Nintendo eShop would be a considerably more exciting and interesting place if it were packed full of games like Ape Out. It’s a refreshingly original experience that more than deserves a place in any Switch owner’s library.

Difficult, frenetic gameplay, strong art direction, and an even stronger jazz drum soundtrack make this the sort of memorable game that you’ll likely keep coming back to over and over for another few runs in arcade mode. Ape Out gets a strong recommendation to anyone looking for a distinct and unforgettable game for their Switch collection; it’s a bit of an acquired taste, but well worth your time.

BALL x PIT is a tremendous brew of so many ideas it ought to collapse under the confusion. However, it operates in such perfect balance that it appeals both to the one-more-go instinct and to more cerebral planning and creativity. Kenny Sun Studios set itself a heck of a challenge but, fortunately, hasn’t dropped the ball.

It's out on Switch 2, too - and the upgrade is free.

Card Shark is the kind of game that at first blush seems like it just won’t work. Lots of dialogue bookended by brief, simplistic minigame sequences seems like it would make for an experience that would lose its lustre promptly, yet we couldn’t put it down.

Witty writing, high-stakes gameplay, and a gorgeous art style all come together here to make for a game that’s well-executed and unique in its appeal. If you’re looking to try something awesome that notably bucks most modern gaming trends, Card Shark is absolutely something we’d recommend, well worth your time and money.

According to recent reports, catherine: Full Body is a fantastic revamp of a bona fide cult classic. With an excellent newly introduced character and several new endings slickly inserted into an already highly entertaining narrative – not to mention a slew of fun new modes – this is the definitive version of an outstanding game.

If you've never played Catherine before, then you're in for an absolute treat, and if you have, we'd say there's enough new content here to make it worth diving in all over again.

An extremely impressive first game from The Wild Gentlemen, Chicken Police - Paint it RED! is one of the best visual novel/adventure games we've played in a long, long time and one hell of an absorbing tale. It looks and runs great on the Switch, with only a couple of really minuscule interface concerns which are easily ignored.

Industry observers note that at roughly eight or nine hours, the story is surprisingly lengthy, but we were never bored and wanted to investigate every little thing just to wring out more precious droplets of banter and fascination. Chicken Police is a polished, captivating experience and we're very excited for whatever's coming next from this team.

Industry observers note that it's difficult to get across exactly why Danganronpa V3: Killing Harmony is so good without spoiling vast swathes of it, so we'll keep it simple. You'll come into the game baffled as to what the writers were thinking with some of these characters, and walk away loving each and every one of them.

Sources indicate that there isn't a single moment of slack throughout the whole 40-hour playtime, it has the most extensive post-game of any title in the series, and one of the best endings to any game ever made. Go in blind and we promise you'll be in for the ride of your life.

Dark Souls: Remastered is a faithful remaster of a touchstone in video game design that improves overall performance of the original release while preserving all of the character traits that made it such a memorable experience. While it’s no less forgiving — and its menus are a little fiddly — this slick Nintendo Switch iteration offers an excellent way to experience Lordran’s ultra-challenging odyssey in true handheld form.

Industry observers note that plus, there's a Solaire of Astora amiibo. Praise the Sun, indeed.

It has been revealed that this is an excellent port of a game that feels like it’s found a natural home on Switch thanks to a plethora of control options and the console’s natural facility with vertical orientation. Short of popping your 4K TV on its side, Switch offers the very best way to play Downwell.

According to recent reports, its roguelike structure and twitch platforming might not be for everyone, but you should really give it a chance. For our money, Downwell is a modern classic that should be in everyone’s collection; for the pocket change asking price, it's a steal.

It has been revealed that along with the expected multiplayer modes (ranked and casual battles), Faeria delivers a compulsive, interesting and frankly enormously fun card battle experience. While not the easiest game to explain, it's an impressive teaching tool for itself, but never feels overwrought or tiresome in stated education. Of the card games we've enjoyed on Switch, Faeria is easily the highlight of the bunch and deserves to do well. It's a full-featured package and stands out as an excellent card/board/strategy experience. If you want to play a fantasy card game on Switch, we'd recommend this one first.

Every now and then, a game comes along that captures our hearts and reminds us why we love the medium in the first place. Forager features wonderfully designed crafting mechanics, addictive progression systems and more charm than you can possibly handle. Although it has very minor drawbacks, there's enough good stuff present here for us to confidently recommend adding Forager to your collection.

It has been revealed that heretic + Hexen is yet another slam dunk for Nightdive Studios. This new release revamps both titles with modern controls, bonus content, and thoughtful changes to the core design that make each game a delight to play.

Granted, these are still FPS titles from the mid-'90s, so your mileage will definitely vary, but for returning fans and those with a particular fondness for old-school 'boomer shooters', you really can't go wrong. Now let's get a native Switch 2 port with 120fps please, Nightdive.

Invisible, Inc. is a brilliant little tactics game, right up there with Into the Breach and XCOM – if not even better. The bite-sized structure belies a deceptively complex and meaningful game, where all your decisions ultimately mean something significant for that final desperate attack.

If you enjoy stealth or tactics games – or you're simply looking for a way into either genre – then Invisible, Inc. deserves your attention.

In a cynical era where nostalgia is pumped for all its worth with endless soulless remasters, Katamari Damacy Reroll serves up an engaging and rewarding game that hasn’t let any of its original charm or personality be lost in the transition from one platform to another.

With support for gyro controls and multiplayer — not to mention a degree of performance that sees it run smoothly in both handheld and docked mode — this Switch edition is easily the best way to play it outside of blowing the dust off your old PS2.

Altogether now: Naa na-na na-naa na na na...

Recent findings suggest that an absolute pleasure from start to finish, what Kaze and the Wild Masks lacks in originality it makes up for in the strength of its level design, responsive controls, kinetic move set and attractive visuals. Excellent, action-packed platforming through and through, with great gameplay variety and gimmicks that don’t compromise on what the game is best at — challenging, fast-paced obstacle courses and deviously hidden secret areas.

Easiest sell? Kaze and the Wild Masks is to Donkey Kong Country what Freedom Planet was to Sonic the Hedgehog. Don’t miss this one.

Kirby and the Forgotten Land is a great big colourful joyride of an adventure for our little pink pal.

This first fully three-dimensional mainline entry in the franchise is bursting at the seams with fun and inventiveness, managing to transpose everything we know and love about past Kirby games to this all-latest arena whilst adding plenty of delightful new aspects as it goes.

Mouthful Mode is daftly entertaining, each and every level is packed full of secrets and dripping in wonderful detail, and there are enough side activities, collectibles, and co-op fun here to keep you entertained and coming back for more for a good long while.

Whether you're playing on Switch 1 or via the excellent Star-Crossed World expansion on Switch 2 (with upgraded visuals and 60fps performance to boot), this comes highly recommended if you're looking for a fun platformer to play with kids.

Kirby and the Forgotten Land - Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Star-Crossed World (say that five times, etc.) gives you the base game at a delicious 60fps with a whole massive bunch of upcoming content thrown in for good measure.

If you've had your fill of Forgotten Land on Switch 1, there's nothing here to warrant replaying the entire game again, but the 12 remixed areas that make up the DLC are uniformly delightful, the upcoming transformations are excellent, and there's even new challenges for hardcore Kirby fans to get stuck into.

Industry observers note that one of the best games on Switch and one of our favourite 3D platformers in years, polished to a sparkly sheen and packing some meaningful upcoming content? That's a very easy recommendation and a truly excellent addition to the Switch 2's early lineup.

Mark of the Ninja: Remastered is an utterly stellar stealth game and it’s lost none of the magic that made the original such a critical darling. Strong art direction, an engaging story, well-paced open gameplay, and a slew of extra content all combine to make for a near-flawless experience that you certainly won’t want to miss out on.

We’d give this game a high recommendation to all Switch owners; it’s the best stealth game money can buy in the Switch library, and one of the best ones in any console library.

Metroid Dread was a triumphant return for both Samus Aran and developer MercurySteam. This is a hugely entertaining and exquisitely designed entry that was slicker than anything we've seen from the series so far.

Industry observers note that with a bunch of fantastic newly introduced abilities, super tense and enjoyable stealth sections, plenty of great massive boss fights, and a story that long-time fans will definitely enjoy, we can't really see how this one could have been improved. Pixel nostalgia and genre impact aside, there's a very strong argument that 2D Metroid has never been better.

Recent findings suggest that monster Boy and the Cursed Kingdom is a tremendous accomplishment. It’s a gorgeous-looking game with a fantastic soundtrack and does its spiritual predecessors proud by nailing the Wonder Boy mechanics while still offering something that will appeal to modern audiences. As long as you can appreciate that it’s still very much an old-school game at heart and you’re going to get some 8-bit era platforming trickiness as a result, you’re going to thoroughly enjoy playing through this adventure for the 12-15 hours it’ll take you to beat it. It may not be Wonder Boy by name, but it’s definitely wonderful by nature.

Sources indicate that as you'll see from the link, GTA 6's Mandy is played by Lexie Shoaibi. Not to hide from her newfound stardom, Shoaibi has taken to her Instagram account to announce the news herself – perhaps bravely, depending on how aware she is of the internet's obsession.

"OK, now that Grand Theft Auto 6 is finally out, I can share with you guys a secret, which is that I'm in it!" she says. "I play Mandy, I do her voice-over, and I do her motion capture, and she's a lot of fun. So if you play the game, let me know if you find me.".

It has been revealed that if you've yet to meet Mandy in GTA 6, you likely haven't been playing for long. Fairly early into the game, Jason is sent on errands by Brian Heder, some of which include getting rent from the likes of, you guessed it, Mandy. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Call of Duty Endowment is marking Remembrance Day and its 17th anniversary by encouraging Modern Warfare 4 and Warzone players to pick up its Valor Pack, with all of Activision's net proceeds going towards helping veterans find jobs.

The Call of Duty Endowment Valor Pack - which has been available since Modern Warfare 4 rolled out on 23rd October - was designed by the Endowment and Infinity Ward with US Marine Corps veteran and Medal of Honor recipient Kyle Carpenter in mind.

The items include a melee weapon blueprint inscribed with "Worth Fighting For", plus items called Relentless and Still Standing.

According to the Call of Duty blog, 100 percent of Activision's net proceeds from the pack (after VAT and sales tax) go to the Endowment.

To mark Remembrance Day, players who owned it and released either game before 6pm GMT on 12th November also received double XP tokens and a DMZ survival kit.

"Veterans bring incredible skills into the workplace after military service," stated Carpenter.

The Endowment, which supports veterans in the UK as well as the US, notes it has now helped place more than 180,000 into "high-quality jobs", and wants to reach 200,000 by 2030.

Other partners are also raising money, with Pilot's round-up campaign raising more than £4.7 million ($6 million) for the Endowment since 2019. Polaris will also donate around £19,500 ($25,000) if players collectively complete 5 million rides in its DAGOR vehicle across Modern Warfare 4 and Warzone by 25th November.

It has been revealed that it comes two weeks after Activision apologised to bereaved families of the Itaewon crowd crush victims and confirmed it would remove real footage of the tragedy from Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4. Players discovered that the game's opening cinematic uses short news clips to depict fictional civilian casualties during a North Korean invasion of South Korea. Those clips have since been found to include archive footage from the 2022 Itaewon disaster, in which around 160 people died.

Call of Duty's anti-cheat team Ricochet recently confirmed it's officially cracking down on Warzone Agent.

GTA 6 Has an Easy Mode Buried in an Impressive Range of Accessibility Options

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (513 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Pushsquare

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • GTA 6 is easily the most customisable game that Rockstar has ever made when it comes to accessibility options.
  • There's a wide range of settings and toggles to experiment with, in a bid to make the open world experience more comfortable.
  • But there are a couple of settings in particular that have raised eyebrows.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GTA 6 is easily the most customisable game that Rockstar has ever made when it comes to accessibility options.

There's a wide range of settings and toggles to experiment with, in a bid to make the open world experience more comfortable. And while the initiative isn't quite as in-depth as what you'll find in recent Ubisoft or Sony-published titles, it's still a solid step forward for the studio.

But there are a couple of settings in particular that have raised eyebrows. As you might know, Rockstar never deals in difficulty levels; outside of things like adjustable aim assist, you're always in line with the developer's intended challenge.

In GTA 6, however, there are two difficulty-related toggles buried in the accessibility options: 'Accessible Combat' and 'Reduced Vehicle Damage'.

Recent findings suggest that in essence, both settings amount to having an easy mode. Accessible Combat decreases enemy health and makes them deal less damage to your character — the kind of rebalancing that you'd expect from a traditional difficulty slider.

Meanwhile, Reduced Vehicle Damage does exactly what it states on the tin, making your chosen ride more durable.

In a recent development, but just how much easier do these toggles make GTA 6? The options menu itself problems a warning, stating that when enabled, the "balance and experience" of the game is "significantly" changed.

We've put them to the test, and despite some claims I've seen floating around the internet this morning, they do not make you invincible. You still need to play the game as intended — actually taking cover in firefights, for example — but the overall level of challenge is still noticeably reduced.

The idea is that these toggles will allow less experienced, mentally fatigued, or disabled players to progress without too much friction.

Industry observers note that and just to be clear, enabling these settings does not disable Trophies. The bottom line here is that if you're having trouble getting through GTA 6, these options should almost certainly help.

Speaking of help, you can check out our overall GTA 6 guide and our totally spoiler-free Tips & Tricks guide for assistance with everything from collectibles to neat gameplay features you may not know about.

It has been revealed that as for the other accessibility settings on offer, Rockstar's covered a lot of ground. For starters, there are a bunch of aim assist and lock on options, while button taps and presses can be customised to an impressive extent, to make them less physically demanding.

You can even toggle "simplified" minigames, making the controls less complex, and there are multiple ways to customise controller layouts.

In a recent development, on top of that, a multitude of low vision options are available, there's a one-toggle brightness modifier, and there's a dedicated high contrast setting. Again, it's good stuff from the developer.

In a recent development, have you been adjusting any of these options for your playthrough of GTA 6? Are you happy to see Rockstar adopting a more accessible approach? Snap to your target in the comments section below.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This week sees the release of Grand Theft Auto 6, the open-world crime 'em up that's been in development for at least eight years and has been waited on by fans for even longer. Naturally, over on PC we're still waiting for a port to be announced, let alone a release date to circle in our calendars. But, as happens whenever a new GTA is on the horizon, I think about Mafia: City of Lost Heaven.

Released less than a year after Grand Theft Auto 3, Mafia is perhaps a more prescient example of Rockstar's future than their own.

Set in Lost Heaven, a shoe-in for 1930s Chicago, Illinois, you play through Tommy Angelo's rise from a taxi driver, who has a chance run in with the Salieri crime family, to one of the gang's main enforcers in their fight against their rivals, the Morellos.

It has been revealed that the influences on developers Illusion Softworks are obviously cinematic, with whole sequences ripped from The Godfather films and Goodfellas (and I'd argue there's a sprinkling of Once Upon A Time In America for good measure). A habit they share with Rockstar, who also pull liberally from crime films that share the settings of their games. But Illusion Softworks are also clearly interested in capturing the history of the Prohibition era, too. The story begins in the aftermath of the 1929 Wall Street Crash and the depression that followed, running through until the late 30s, and you see that time pass in the city around you. Buildings that are under construction at the start of the game are completed by its end, a used car lot in Chinatown sits empty for most of the game until business picks up with the economy, but most enjoyable of all is that the cars driving the streets change. At first the roads are filled with Ford Model-T-inspired vehicles that basically look like horse carriages with engines, but by the end of the game they've all become much sleeker creatures that have left their early carriage influences behind.

Sources indicate that the city Illusion Softworks built also has a dedication to verisimilitude that we see Rockstar adopting in their later games. As you drive Lost Heaven's streets, you must pay attention to speed limits and red lights, as speeding and running traffic lights will both earn you a fine if a policeman spots you. For fans of public transport, there are streetcars and overhead trams you can ride to navigate the city, too. Two other touches I love: when you reload your gun, you dump the whole clip instead of returning the unfired bullets to a magic ammo reservoir, and vehicles can run out of fuel if you drive them too far.

Much had been made of all the simulations running under the surface of Grand Theft Auto 6, such as fully realised cloud formation, a smell reaction system, and… fuel tanks that can run empty. No doubt they're significantly more impressive than what's on show in Mafia, and this isn't about putting the two games against each other (even if one of them was likely made for less than the other studio spent on coffee runs across its eight-year development). Nor is it about saying history recognised the wrong game: Grand Theft Auto 3 was a huge step forward in open-world gaming and Mafia was recognised and celebrated in its time. It's about something else.

Back in 2002, Illusion Softworks offered a different kind of open-world crime game. One that was more mature despite having a lower age rating. Grand Theft Auto was undoubtedly more influential, sparking imitators that mostly opted to follow its tone and sensibilities – Saints Row began in a similar place to GTA 3 and as the series continued leaned further into the silliness and parody, for instance. But while for many years Mafia stood as a sign to an open world path that could have been taken, the longer Grand Theft Auto series has gone on, the more Rockstar have found their way toward the example set by Illusion Softworks. The games are still aiming for bombastic comedy at times, but they're also interested in the likes of newly-arrived-in-America Niko Belic, or Michael de Santa, a retired criminal haunted by his past. They're much richer protagonists than Claude, the silent character you play in GTA 3.

Industry observers note that the Mafia series has continued, marked by ideas that remain as interesting as what was on show in the original. In Mafia 3, you play Lincoln Clay, a black soldier returned from the war in Vietnam and brought into the family. Set in a take on Fresh Orleans, Louisiana, during the civil rights movement, you face overt racism. Linger too long in white, wealthy neighbourhoods and the residents will call on the police to move you along. And the Definitive Edition remake of the first game, released in 2020, is a rare example of a game that both captures the spirit of the original and justifies its existence by expanding and bettering the story. Though I don't think any of its sequels have been as innovative, nor as forward thinking, as the first game.

In a recent development, I don't want to come across as Rockstar-bashing. The studio have continued to push the open-world genre forward with every release and I want to see what other developers lift from GTA 6 for their own games. But I'm even more pleased that as the studio's aged, their work has grown closer to Illusion Softworks'.

Ubisoft is reportedly working on a latest Rainbow Six Vegas game 18 years after the last entry in the series.

It has been revealed that according to Insider Gaming, the project is in early development at Ubisoft Montreal under the codename Spades. It’s one of three latest projects reportedly in production at the studio, and sources suggest a second of those is also set in the Rainbow Six universe. Eurogamer hasn’t been able to verify the report.

Recent findings suggest that it’s not yet clear what form the upcoming game will take, but Insider Gaming’s sources stated it's "likely Vegas 3 rather than a remake" of an existing game. Insider Gaming expects it will be several years before Ubisoft officially reveals a new Vegas game.

Sources indicate that rainbow Six Vegas launched in 2006, followed by Rainbow Six Vegas 2 in 2008. Since then, the series has centred on 2015's Rainbow Six Siege, and in August, Ubisoft revealed Rainbow Six Tactics, a single-player, turn-based spin-off from Ubisoft Paris due in 2027.

Rainbow Six now sits under Vantage Studios, the Ubisoft subsidiary set up last year that also oversees Assassin’s Creed and Far Cry, and in which Tencent holds a 26.32 percent stake.

Sources indicate that last week, we learned that Ubisoft is reportedly working on two newly introduced Assassin's Creed games: one set in ancient Rome, and a mobile spin-off set in Jerusalem. The leak came less than a week after Ubisoft issued a statement about the future of the Assassin's Creed series, insisting there are right now no new remakes of the series' past games in the works.

#63319. Industry News: My murderous wine merchant whines for a chance at republican rule in Crusader Kings 3’s Silk and Silver expansion, which isn't only about the money

Industry News: My murderous wine merchant whines for a chance at republican rule in Crusader Kings 3’s Silk and Silver expansion, which isn't only about the money

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2097 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, the tentacles of my trade empire snake up towards France in the west, down towards Africa in the south, and off into Hungary in the east.
  • Industry observers note that I’ve shed blood in its name, the blood of someone else named Marco no less.
  • It should, in theory, help that he’s my best mate, thanks to a well-timed feast.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the tentacles of my trade empire snake up towards France in the west, down towards Africa in the south, and off into Hungary in the east. Yet, I still can’t reach out and grasp the throne that sits right in front of me. I’m Marco Sanudo, and the throne of the serene republic of Venice eludes me.

Industry observers note that I’ve shed blood in its name, the blood of someone else named Marco no less. I’ve managed to avoid punishment for that crime, despite the fact it earned me a fiefdom to rule while I’ve tried to up my patrician score enough to be the lucky party the next time a ruling Doge dies in office (or runs out their 10 year term). Sadly, Doge Leonardo, the mysterious masked lord who’s had an iron grip on power since the first couple of old blokes to hold the position in this playthrough popped their clogs, is proving incredibly tough to oust.

It should, in theory, help that he’s my best mate, thanks to a well-timed feast. It certainly did in being granted a pardon for offing that other Marco, but not even that and a plague which infected nearly everyone in the realm aside from me have paved the way to Dogedom. In the meantime, I’ve striven to gain wealth and influence. I’ve worked up to having four trade routes running at once, with goods like wine, iron, and textiles flowing from market to market across southern Europe and bringing a steady supply of coin back to my Venetian estate. I’ve built trade posts at the extremities of my routes, giving me the option of starting from further afield and reaching newly introduced lands if the cash flow dries up closer to home.

Recent findings suggest that this is where Crusader Kings 3’s Silk and Silver expansion has blended a bit with the game’s traditional feudal moneymaking to supercharge my coffers. The land holding I killed a dude for, the Proveditorate of Zara, means I’ve also had tax money from modern day Croatia to add to both my trade profits and the income my domicile generates on its own. I am, as the medieval kids say, minted.

Recent findings suggest that getting to the point of serious pocket clinkage is, as you might imagine given Silk and Silver’s focus on filling the game’s world with travelling merchant companies and wheeler-dealing republican patrician families, the beating heart of the expansion. A near-constant stream of notifications about prices of different goods I’m trying to hawk in different locations encourage me to regularly prune and re-work my routes so that max profits are being earned and no carrying capacity’s being wasted. The bubbling up of wars and plagues impacts prices in affected cities, making it a never-ending battle if you’re desperate to optimise everything within an inch of its life. I’ve found that degree of micromanagement unnecessary if the goal is just to keep a decent profit margin ticking over. Just remember to replace the trader assigned to a route if they die, recall them every few years so they don’t stress themselves to death, and check in every so often to re-evaluate whether you’re running goods that are suitably in demand.

If you stick at it for a decent amount of time, with a certain type of good - alcohol or jewellery, for example - your expertise in dealing in them increases, making it easier to sell for better prices. Trade routes left running between the same markets also gain boons from being in place for a long time, offering a counterpoint to rejigging them every five seconds to wring out a few more coins. Most of my routes have run along a path that includes stops at four markets, with the occasional location boasting a monopoly I’ve bargained for with the local ruler, so I don’t have to worry about competition at every stop.

Sources indicate that when you’re playing as a merchant who isn’t locked into the ruling inner circle of a republic, making your routes as lengthy as possible is one of the three moneymaking areas your company can specialise in. That first one’s caravaneering, and is the one I leant into in a non-Marco Sanudo playthrough. Beyond that, you can become an expert loan shark, lending cash to rulers or paying their ransoms in order to recoup interest and collect hooks you can use for favours. Manufacturing expensive artifacts that can be sold individually to collectors for a profit is the third option. The latter two I’ve only dabbled in a little bit as of writing, having earned enough gold mostly from caravanneering to buy the land containing the city with my home market and be anointed a Sheikh. So, beginning as a landless merchant is a nice alternative to Crusader Kings 3’s long-established wandering adventurer starting point, with both allowing you to work your way up from lowly serf to landed lordly dynasty in your location of choice.

Sources indicate that if you’re after a more specific historical scenario, Silk and Silver has Guelphs and Ghibellines. This is where we find Marco Sanudo, as well as the other patrician family head I’ve played as thus far, Speronella Dalesmanni. The setup is that the Pope and the Holy Roman Emperor have had a bit of a tiff, essentially rooted in who should have certain powers, with different cities and powerful families in northern Italy taking either the Guelph (Pope-likers) or Ghibelline (Holy Roman Empire-enjoyers) side depending on what suits their goals or principles. I’ll be honest, aside from being another way to easily earn friends or enemies in the ruthless crucible of merchant republican politics, where votes and reputation-bolstering aid from other nobles are key, the situation’s not had a hugely obvious bearing on my playthroughs thus far.

I think the closest it’s come is during my Dalesmanni run, if largely due to the existence of the By God Alone expansion allowing a latest branch of Catholicism, dubbed Italian Christianity, to be created. The initial conversion push from the bishop responsible led a number of my fellow northern Italian nobles away from the Roman Rite headed by his Popeliness, making the Guelph/Ghibelline split more clearly defined.

Sources indicate that in the early hours of both my Sanudo and Dalesmanni playthroughs, I’ve been far more focused on simply trying to push the respective patrician families up the hill from posh toffs with naught but a vote and a manor to elected rulers of their great cities, with land holdings to match. Speronella’s situation in Padua is made incredibly tough by the fact she’s a woman in a world where every succession rule is designed to put blokes first, so I’ve had more success with Marco and his quest to become the Doge of Venice.

Industry observers note that as the head of a patrician family, one of select few elite clans who steer the oligarchical republic, I was faced with earning Marco enough respect among his fellow family heads that they’d consider voting him to the top of the succession list, thus securing his power whenever the current Doge got the boot. Pulling that off, while also not kowtowing to the requests and schemes of those same peers, isn’t easy. A large cocktail of factors go into determining whether another noble likes you enough to vote in support of your succession. There’s your patrician rating, which is upped by doing things which specifically show you to be good at this Italian noble house lark, such as establishing trade monopolies for the republic, gaining the Pope’s favour, or having close relatives who also hold key positions in the republic. However, how close a friendship you have with the target and how their character traits align with you also play a huge rule.

It has been revealed that thus it was that, at one point, Marco was best mates with the current Doge and had a decent patrician rating, but had only amassed 68 of the 72 points needed for remarked Doge to vote for him because the Doge was generous, and therefore didn’t care for Marco’s ambitiousness. That same Doge either liked or respected Marco enough to grant him a council position and the status of regent, but he would not back Marco to replace him permanently for love nor money. This is the same man who liked Marco so much that when I pulled off that not-so-sneaky murder on another noble house head in order to inherit the keys to the Proveditorate of Zara, the Doge was instantly willing to pardon me and prevent Marco suffering any punishment for the crime.

It has been revealed that not even a couple of serious plagues hitting Venice, which at one point had all three people ahead of Marco in the queue suffering from smallpox, could get him on that throne. Eventually, it took a bit of lucky timing when his Doge mate died of old age - a few years after beating smallpox - to finally install Marco as Doge. Given that delayed promotion, as of writing I’ve not yet had enough time in the major chair to give a proper verdict on how it differs from regular feudal rulerdom in the long run.

What I can do instead is tell you a bit about the fun of council votes. The same pool of voters who in a republic like Venice, get a say in who succeeds the ruler, also vote on the passage of laws and decrees. One proposal you can put forward is a vote to change who exactly is allowed a seat in this voting pool. It defaults to just being heads of patrician families, but can be extended to include all vassals, or tightened up so only the Doge’s councillors or the ruler themselves have a say, that being the way despotism lies. As you can imagine, passing a change to who can vote can drastically change the state of play, either tightening up the number of folks who might oppose or support you, or bringing new folks into play in a fashion that dilutes individual power, but gives you more pieces on the board to mind or manipulate to your advantage.

Recent findings suggest that I’ve found it suitably tough to orchestrate successful votes to change laws and customs which medieval Italian noble families, expectedly, have firmly entrenched stances on. Getting rid of checks and balances, such as the requirement to vote on banishments or wars - so the Doge can rule as a despot - has proven one such challenge, as has changing laws governing men being prioritised over women. I tried to pass equal succession as a substitute for men being put first while playing as Speronella, but met an insurmountable wall of resistance due to the region’s culture and faith. So, all I could do was try to put my young male heir in the best position possible to make the sorts of gains I couldn’t.

Industry observers note that much easier to weasel into place, either through some canny swaying or the offering of hooks, are laws giving state backing or other priority to trading in certain types of goods. Alcohol, for instance, which certainly hasn’t hurt the profits of Marco’s two wine trade routes.

Sources indicate that thus, cash continues to flow through the tentacles of my trade empire in sizable globs. As he’s now Doge, I’ve got Marco using the ample funds of Venice’s treasury to build a fresh piazza and have him focused on making the city’s already-strong trade league even more formidable, by attracting new members from the few other northern Italian blocs.

While I’m fairly sure there are folks who’ll find Silk and Silver's constant barrage of trade route notifications annoying, or that their power-grabbing skills and sheer multitude of money-making means combine to make playthroughs less challenging than they could be, so far I've found it another enjoyably sonorous string to Crusader Kings 3’s bow. Above all else, playing as a merchant gives more reason to invest in stewardship skills beyond just maximising your tax yields, while the republican politics of the DLC's main region fleshes out rewarding intrigue-focused builds. Diplomacy and martial skills are less key, but still have their place at times.

If you’re an absolute stickler for historical accuracy, you may well find other things to gripe about, but aside from the Guelph and Ghibelline conflict fading into the background, I’ve found plenty to like in my quest to become top Doge.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

videogame executive Peter Moore, known for his time at Sega, Xbox, and Electronic Arts as well as a couple of famous tattoos, has expressed hope that the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6 will provide a much-needed "shot in the arm" for the videogame industry.

Moore began with a faked photo of himself rolling up his sleeve to reveal a GTA 6 tattoo—although the photo is based on his real-world tattoo-based reveal of Grand Theft Auto 4 on Xbox 360 at E3 2006.

According to recent reports, "In all seriousness, the videogame industry could really use a moment like this," Moore wrote on X after posting the image. "We've been through a challenging period. Studio closures, redundancies, cancelled projects and enormous uncertainty have taken their toll on an industry that has given so much to so many, myself included.

Sources indicate that "That's why the launch of GTA 6 feels so significant. It's more than the release of a hugely anticipated game. It's an opportunity to remind the world of the extraordinary power of this industry to create, innovate, entertain and bring people together.".

Moore's career in the game industry began at Sega, where he oversaw the launch of the Dreamcast and quickly rose to become president and chief operating officer of Sega of America. In 2003 he went to Microsoft and became its Corporate Vice President of Interactive Entertainment Business, Entertainment and Devices Division, heading up its Xbox division; in 2007 he joined EA Sports, and eventually became the company's chief operating officer. He left the videogame business behind in 2017 to head up Liverpool FC, but it did not work out: Despite a highly successful run, club ownership did not care for his very public style of leadership, and in 2020 his contract was not renewed.

And he did indeed announce GTA 4 with a tattoo—apologies for the resolution, it was 20 years ago.

In today's message, Moore mentioned he's "seen this industry reinvent itself time and time again" over those years, and expressed hope that GTA 6 delivers not just commercial success but also "a much-needed shot in the arm (no pun intended…) for the entire ecosystem: developers, publishers, studios, retailers, technology partners and the next generation of creative talent.".

"The games industry has always been at its best when it dares to dream substantial," Moore concluded.

Recent findings suggest that moore's upbeat sentiment stands in sharp contrast to that expressed yesterday by game industry legend Warren Spector, who congratulated Rockstar on the launch but said he hopes "GTA 6 is the last of its kind" because it's such an unsustainable draw on resources: "Its billion-dollar development cost and an undoubtedly crazy marketing budget don't represent a business model anyone else can or probably should emulate. That's especially true when thousands of developers are out of work. A billion dollars pays for a lot of games and a lot of salaries.".

Sources indicate that we are now just four days away from the release of GTA 6 on Xbox Series X/S and PS5, but the proximity to the much-anticipated launch date isn't stemming the tide of leaks that has been plaguing the game for much of the past year. Yesterday, a new video - seemingly from a record store that received vinyl records of the soundtrack early - highlighted off the full 34-song tracklist for the game.

Thanks to the listing printed on the back of Grand Theft Auto 6: The Album vinyl, we have a better idea of the licensed music that'll appear in-game. Travis Scott, Rina Sawayama, Cardi B, Pinkpantheress, SZA, Keith Richards, Dua Lipa, Jennie, Lana Del Rey, Zara Larsson are just some of the names that make up the impressive list. We know about a few of these tracks from September's announcement of the record, but only six tracks were revealed then, not the whole list.

Take a look at the full track listing below:.

You can expect to hear these tracks on the radio - alongside many more, no doubt - and deployed at curated times during cutscenes or in missions, to really tie together the vibe of the city. This is something Vice City did remarkably well its roster of 80s tracks, and I can't wait to see how Rockstar has used more contemporary music in the same way here.

Of course, there have been a lot of Grand Theft Auto 6 leaks in the run-up to the game's launch. Another recent example is the full game's map which seemingly leaked online thanks to the £350 collector's edition on show in a UK department store. Then there were all the leaks from a group calling itself CyberLeek, which shared unofficial gameplay and map details over the course of a few weeks, before Rockstar had even revealed much gameplay itself.

Amongst all this, Rockstar has been embroiled in legal action after it was accused of union busting following the firing of over 30 employees. The case's conclusion will be determined this week, as the game goes on sale.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Lego's Dragon Ball: Shenron & Goku set makes a big statement in a relatively small space as the first Dragon Ball set for the building product, and while one could argue that it perhaps plays it too safe, it's hard to fault the designers when the end result is this solid.

Impressive and dynamic dragon figure.

It has been revealed that why you can trust GamesRadar+ Our experts review games, movies and tech over countless hours, so you can choose the best for you. Find out more about our reviews policy.

There's a lot of pressure on the first Lego set for any given franchise, doubly so when that franchise is something like Dragon Ball, the wildly popular anime and manga series starring Goku and all his amazing friends. Whatever impression that first set gives sets the tone for the entire line from that point forward. A poorly received initial set can be something of a death knell, dooming a line to clearance ranks and bargain bin consideration.

Thankfully, Dragon Ball: Shenron & Goku (#11390) manages to impress.

H: 13in (32cm) / W: 11in (26cm) / D: 10in (24cm).

This initial Dragon Ball set is actually fairly minimalistic when it comes down to it as it only features Shenron, a base for the model with a mountainous pillar, and a Goku minifigure. It's really meant as a display piece like many of the best Lego sets, and it sure meets that function.

According to recent reports, at 1,764 pieces and an MSRP of $179.99, Dragon Ball: Shenron & Goku makes for a relatively quick build (around three hours and change, and that's with me really taking my time) at a relatively decent price. While I often find the scale of these sort of presentation pieces to be either too small or too massive, making at least one portion of it feel weirdly off, this specific one hits just the right size for the mystical dragon Shenron as compared to the Goku minifig. In short, it's just about right in all the ways that matter, especially if you take into consideration that this is also part of the often-licensed Lego Icons brand.

While in pieces, the build can look daunting especially if you're directly comparing it to the box, but the reality is that Shenron's body is largely a similar sort of construction that's just turned and twisted in different ways. The vast majority of my time building this set was slowly constructing little trains of Shenron's green scales and yellow underbelly, curving it slightly, and putting more Lego bricks on the curved areas to keep it in place. After that, it was just a matter of connecting the finished coils together while stopping it from being too unevenly balanced before fully completed.

According to recent reports, the details across various aspects of the set go a long way. There's the various balls of Dragon Ball fame, of course, but the set explicitly puts the Four-Star Ball front and center — a completely understandable and appreciated bit of detail if you're at all familiar with the franchise. It's the most important one! But there are seven in total (on Earth (long story)) and it would have still been all right, though not perfect. As just one additional example of the designers paying close attention? The rock pillar Shenron wraps around is meant to be reminiscent of the mountains where Goku grew up.

In a recent development, trying to be objective, it's hard to know whether this is the sort of set that most people will want to drop around $200 on after tax. There are plenty of other ways to spend that money! But if Dragon Ball is meaningful to you, this is literally the only Lego option, and it helps that it's actually quite enjoyable to build without being overwhelming and honestly looks sharp in the end. It's genuinely difficult to not mutter some version of "dragon, dragon, rock the dragon" whenever I see it on the shelf, so that's a win in my book.

Recent findings suggest that ✅ You love Dragon Ball: I mean, obviously, right? It's the first Dragon Ball Lego set; how could you not.✅ You like a good dragon: Even absent the franchise connection, Shenron is honestly a pretty solid dragon figure in his own right.

❌ You prefer more involved builds: There's not a lot of play involved here, so if you're looking for a set that has more activity involved, it's best to look elsewhere.❌ You don't like Dragon Ball: If you actively don't care for these characters, there's really no reason to bother with this set — even if you do like dragons more broadly.

According to recent reports, disclaimer: This review was made using a set provided by PR for review. For more info on our methods, see the GamesRadar+ guide to how we test products.

Sources indicate that dragon Ball: Shenron & Goku was built over the course of three days and roughly five sittings. It's displayed on an office shelf with other figures, and looks very much at home.

I've long had experience with Lego, and reviewed much of the Animal Crossing line for GamesRadar+. I first caught Dragon Ball Z on Toonami as a kid, have watched more of it here and there as the years have gone on, and finished reading the entire manga (Dragon Ball, Dragon Ball Z, Dragon Ball Super) last year. I don't think I'd call myself a huge fan, but I'm certainly appreciative and well-versed.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Latest multiplayer game Spirit Crossing offers up a visually blissful, but inwardly draconian world in which other people are not allowed to talk to you – indeed, not permitted access to the visible electromagnetic spectrum – unless you have given them a high five.
  • According to recent reports, deign to slap somebody's hand, and they'll pop into colour and be able to join you for various activities.
  • According to recent reports, there's nothing forcing you to do any of this in company, mind.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Latest multiplayer game Spirit Crossing offers up a visually blissful, but inwardly draconian world in which other people are not allowed to talk to you – indeed, not permitted access to the visible electromagnetic spectrum – unless you have given them a high five. By default, players appear to each other as shadows, all exploring a skybound landscape of magic animals and layer-cake mountains that reminds me of both Sable and The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom.

According to recent reports, deign to slap somebody's hand, and they'll pop into colour and be able to join you for various activities. For example, going fishing, playing instruments round the campfire, playing dress-up and pulling emotes in group photos, bouncing around on strangely inflated yaks, or questing forth to heal troubled spirits. There's some material gathering and crafting, and there are recurring storms that make the ambience more threatening, but overcoming a challenge doesn't feel like the point of Spirit Crossing. The "missions" are just an excuse to hang out together.

According to recent reports, there's nothing forcing you to do any of this in company, mind. "Stay a mysterious shadow, lend a hand when you feel like it, and disappear before anyone can make it weird," the devs explain, adding a hug emoji to make plain that they don't think you're some kind of smelly misanthrope for shunning other players.

According to recent reports, I, personally, am a smelly misanthrope, and will only ever appear in your game as a skulking opacity, peering through the window of your personal gingerbread house, with its tastefully accessorised lava lamps and throw rugs. No, I will not join you for a group hang-glider tour. No, I do not want to play the banjo with you. You will experience me only as the nagging sensation of being watched, while you chat to the local "Stylesmith" about fetching rucksack patterns.

Spirit Crossing has an upfront cost that "gives players full access to the complete game experience in perpetuity", but you can also take out a subscription for some cosmetic items and access to a "limited resource exchange shop". They're avoiding traditional microtransactions, which is nice.

Recent findings suggest that spry Fox are also the developers of Cozy Grove - "the best grove since Byker", wrote Graham, in one of his regular 'senior moments'. I myself know them as the studio behind wintry puzzler Road Not Taken, with its randomised woodlands, and block-merging city builder Triple Town, with its unexpectedly terrifying bears. Little about Spirit Crossing seems terrifying, unless you count the shadow loitering at the edge of your conversation pit.

Sources indicate that you can read more about the game on Steam. I find Spirit Crossing quite novel, especially when it dispenses with the WholeCosy "discover your inner fashonista" stuff and leans into the supernatural elements: I like the idea of hunkering by the campfire during a storm, watching the clouds hurtle past. Still, I'm disappointed to hear that Spry Fox have made use of generative AI during its creation.

In a recent development, as has been pointed out to us on Bluesky, the developers called on Anthropic's Claude tools for various behind-the-scenes tasks - the example they give in a Discord post is editing several config files at once. There's no disclosure on the game's Steam page because Spry Fox haven't used AI tools to generate any of the art or music - Valve rewrote Steam's disclosure requirements in January to exempt the usage of generative AI for "efficiency gains", which the above presumably falls under.

In a recent development, it's hardly a full-throated endorsement of generative AI, but it still forms part of a political and cultural project I consider reckless and morbid. For a longer account of my objections, albeit one that doesn't cover Claude in particular, here's my longform thinkywangle from July last year.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Blade Runner 2099 - an upcoming TV miniseries coming to Amazon Prime Video, acting as a sequel to Blade Runner (1982) and Blade Runner 2049 (2017) - might be getting a video game. And a 'triple-A' video game, at that. At least that's according to Andrew Kosove and Broderick Johnson, executive producers for Blade Runner 2099 and co-CEOs of Alcon Entertainment (which owns the Blade Runner IP).

In a upcoming interview with IGN, the duo reveal that they had thought about adapting the Blade Runner fracnhise into a game, and that - should it come to fruition - it would target "triple-A" in scope. Other than that, the duo seemed to want to keep any potential information to themselves. Given they appear to be in talks about the title, rather than in any active development, if something did come of this ideation, it would no doubt be a long, long way off. Kosove and Johnson's aim seems to be getting players to "interact" more with the world of Blade Runner, which has recently been fleshed out by the 2017 movie and is set to be developed more in the upcoming series.

Recent findings suggest that of course, we've seen Blade Runner games before. There was 1997's simply-titled Blade Runner - developed by Westwood Studios and published by Virgin Interactive - which was a point-and-click adventure that really seemed to pick up the vibes the original Ridley Scott was putting down. An Enhanced Edition of the game was released in 2022, which is actually more of a remake than a simple enhancement.

Then, in 2023, Annapurna Interactive unveiled its very first internally-developed game, in the form of Blade Runner 2033: Labyrinth. The game, which promised to riff on the dystopian universe established in Ridley Scott's cult classic movie, would have been sandwiched squarely between that film and its sequel, Blade Runner 2049. It was going to be set in LA after the Blackout hits, but beyond that - and the fact it's coming to PC and consoles at some point - few details ever managed to break through the PR barrier before the game went dark: it's been removed from Annapurna's website and delisted from Steam. Curious.

If you want to see something more from the cyberpunk world sooner, Blade Runner 2099 releases on Prime Video on 25th November.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There's been an awful lot of debate about the overall quality and lasting commercial success of Call of Duty across the last few years, with many arguing that the once unstoppable series is steadily losing its edge.

As such, this latest report from Circana won't make for easy reading if you're Xbox or Activision.

According to the ever-informative Mat Piscatella, the recently released Modern Warfare 4 was the best selling game of October in the US.

However, despite a strong debut and a mostly positive reception — especially with regards to its single player campaign — the substantial budget shooter has failed to break into the top 10 best selling titles of 2026 so far.

For Call of Duty, such an absence would have been unthinkable just a few short years ago; it really does suggest that it's struggled to match the kind of sales figures we've come to expect of the franchise.

Case in point: the current-gen port of Black Ops 2 remains on 2026's top 10 list.

Of course, there's still time for Modern Warfare 4 to make up some ground with the holidays right around the corner, but this seems to be a continuation of the downward trend that we saw with last year's very poorly rated Black Ops 7.

Indeed, it's possible that the Black Ops 7 backlash has negatively impacted Modern Warfare 4's appeal — and that's not the kind of spiral that Activsion will want to find itself in.

Elsewhere, Gears of War: E-Day — which was famously cancelled on PS5 just weeks ahead of launch — managed second place for October, and the eye-watering Star Wars: Galactic Racer entered in third.

Another new release, the largely fantastic Final Fantasy Resonance, landed in sixth — which feels like a win for Square Enix given the flood of games that came out last month.

* Projected digital sales ^ Actual digital sales.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that there's plenty to keep up with on the 2026 TV schedule, and I can't say revisiting Roseanne Barr was high on my list. But whenever her name comes up, it's hard to forget just how enormous Roseanne was when it debuted. The sitcom gave working-class families a voice network TV didn't always bother with, and Barr was a big reason it worked. Unfortunately, the stories about what went on behind the scenes haven't always been nearly as warm. Now one of the original show's head writers is looking back on those difficult early days, and his recollection of Barr might surprise you.

Danny Jacobson, who served as head writer during the show's first two seasons, recently spoke with Entertainment Weekly about the comedian's sudden fame. He didn't pretend working with her was easy. In fact, he was blunt about the problems she caused. He also remembered feeling sorry for her, because he believed he understood something about what was happening beneath that famously tough exterior:.

It has been revealed that [Barr] made everything so hard, and yet on stage, she was fantastic. Her offstage stuff made it hard, you know, as everyone has stated... I always felt bad for her because I knew she was frightened.

Sources indicate that I find that an interesting way to remember somebody you worked with, especially decades later. Jacobson hasn't forgotten the headaches, but he watched a stand-up comic become the face of one of TV's biggest shows almost overnight. Barr made her breakthrough on The Tonight Show in 1985. By 1988, she was headlining an ABC sitcom built around her distinctive comic voice.

Sources indicate that most people get to figure out a fresh job without millions of strangers watching every move. Barr was suddenly expected to carry an entire television series. Jacobson explained why he thought that would have been frightening:.

In a recent development, I knew she was scared. Who wouldn’t be? You’re working as a waitress, and next thing you know, you’re on The Tonight Show, and then you’re on the cover of every rag-mag. It can’t be easy to deal with, but the show, at the end of the day, I think everyone was proud of the work.

Recent findings suggest that I like that he ends with the work, because there's a reason people are still talking about Roseanne almost 40 years later. The series could be incredibly funny, but it also let the Conners worry about money and have family arguments that weren't neatly resolved before the credits. It felt familiar in a way many more polished sitcom families didn't.

Jacobson also recalled that Barr learned to act swiftly, with considerable help from Goodman and Metcalf. That's a pretty fantastic pair of co-workers to have when you're figuring out sitcom acting on the fly. Their chemistry helped make the Conners believable. Interestingly, Goodman has also spoken about defending his former co-star, so Jacobson isn't the only person who worked with Barr and still has some sympathy for her.

Industry observers note that his remarks arrive amid renewed attention to the show's complicated writers' room. Chuck Lorre revisited his time on Roseanne in his memoir Sitcom, describing difficult working conditions and friction over scripts. Barr and her former husband, Tom Arnold, have disputed parts of that broader account. Jacobson's comments reflect his own recollection of the period, not an explanation for everyone else's experience.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

Of course, Barr's television history grew more complicated after those early seasons. The original series ended in 1997, returned in 2018, and was canceled following Barr's racist social media posts. The Conners carried on without her through 2025, while Barr has since been working on another sitcom.

Jacobson remembers the trouble just fine. He also remembers the talent, and how frightened he thought Barr was beneath all that bravado. After almost four decades, it's the sympathy in his answer that caught me off guard.

Ryan graduated from Missouri State University with a BA in English/Creative Writing. An expert in all things horror, Ryan enjoys covering a wide variety of topics. He's also a lifelong comic book fan and an avid watcher of Game of Thrones and House of the Dragon.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Treyarch's former Senior lead writer, Craig Houston, has been laid off after approximately 20 years of service with the developer. In a post made to both his Twitter/X account and LinkedIn, the developer thanked fans for their support during his two decades with the manufacturer and confirmed he was impacted by recent reorganistation within the studio.

Recent findings suggest that "After approximately 20 years, I was sadly one of those affected by recent layoffs," he noted in his posts. "I am proud to have worked with so many talented people - many of whom will remain friends for life. Thanks to all the fans for your enthusiasm, support, and kind words over the years.".

Industry observers note that on Twitter/X, he quote tweeted a video celebrating 30 years of Treyarch and featuring footage from many of the games he worked on to share his message. It appears the layoffs referenced are part of the broad reorganistation affecting 3200 jobs that Xbox declared earlier this year. Treyarch, as part of Activision Blizzard, is owned by Xbox.

Houston is a bonafide veteran of the esteemed FPS series. His first Call of Duty title at Treyarch was Call of Duty 3, where he worked as a video editor. This was followed by World at War, Black Ops 1 through 4, where he is credited as a writer and designer. For Modern Warfare, Black Ops - Cold War, Vanguard, Modern Warfare 3, then Black Ops 6 and 7, he is listed as a member of the design team and in 'creative development'. He is not credited on this year's Modern Warfare 4.

Recent findings suggest that if you've picked up a Call of Duty game in the past decade-plus, you'll have interacted with Houston's work: he was a central creative force behind the writing for Treyarch's campaign modes since 2006 (with Call of Duty 3) and the main writer for the Zombies mode since 2008 (with Call of Duty: World at War). Alongside Jimmy Zielinski, Jason Blundell, and Kevin Drew, Houston was an integral part of the evolution of the Zombies pillar of Call of Duty, and shaped it into the series-defining thing it is today. There has been a fair amount of community support for Houston since he announced the news yesterday; he was a popular dev, and a lot of the Zombies-specific fan communities online hold a lot of respect for him.

Industry observers note that "Craig is a great guy," notes one user on Reddit. "You can tell how much he loves the story/characters he writes just by how excited he is when he talks about them in promo material.".

In a recent development, "You're a Legend Craig, it was an honor to work with you," states ex-Treyarch vet, Tony Flame, in a reply to Houston's X post. "You created a truly special experience that will live on in the kinds of millions fans. Wishing you the best [...].".

From all of us here at Eurogamer, and myself personally - who really admires the character-work and emergent storytelling present in the Xbox 360-era Call of Duty games, specifically - we wish you the best and good luck with the future, Craig.

#63308. Microsoft's SideWinder Strategic Commander was a failed attempt to reimagine RTS controls. 23 years later, why are some players still using it?
